lawyer:
Manzil Murshed with Zamirul Akhtar, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner. 
JK Paul, Advocate ----- For Respondents.
parties:
Golam Sarwar & others ----- Petitioner 
Vs.
Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Mamtaz Uddin Ahmed J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why impugned letter contained in Memo No. মুঃ বিঃ মঃ/প্রঃ-১/বিবিধ-৩৪/২০০২/৩৭১ dated 28-10-2003 by the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs in respect of payment of honorarium with other benefits for the 5% disabled freedom fighters including the petitioners at Taka 600 should not be declared to be illegal and without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seen fit and proper.

2. The facts stated in this writ petition are that the petitioners have challenged the legality and propriety of the letter No. lees fro Its/Os-V Rkt-o8Aoo/oc0 dated 28-10-2003 by which the decision has been communicated to pay State Honorarium benefits to the petitioners at the rate of Taka 600 instead of Taka 2004 and other facilities (State Honorarium benefit) for the wounded freedom fighters and also sought direction to give state Honorarium to the petitioners as like others who are getting since 1987, the same being discriminatory and violative of the fundamental right to equal protection of law and right to be treated in accordance with law as guaranteed under Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

3. The petitioners further stated that they are valiant freedom fighters who were wounded seriously in the war of liberation in 1971. The petitioners actively took part in number of successful operations launched against the Pakistani invading army and were seriously injured in combat.

4. The Bangladesh Muktijoddha Kallayan Trust (herein after referred to as Trust) erstwhile Bangladesh (Freedom Fighters ) Foundation was established by the President Order No. 94 of 1972 dated 7th August 1972 (PO No. 94 of 1972) for the welfare of the freedom fighters disabled (incapable of pursuing any normal vocation because of injuries suffered during the war of liberation) freedom fighters and dependents of shaheeds (martyr) of war of liberation, and to provide assistance for their relief and rehabilitation and in exercise of power conferred under section 17 (1) of PO 94 of 1972 the Board of Trusties, entrusted with the management of the Trust, promulgated Bangladesh Muktijoddha Kallayan Trust Regulation 1984 in order to regulate the affairs of the Trust concerning the rehabilitation of disabled/wounded freedom fighters, through proper listing and ensuring payment of benefits (allowance/ honorarium etc) to them.

5. The petitioners being war wounded freedom fighters having come to know about the welfare Scheme by the Trust for the fully/ partially disabled freedom fighters due to the injury/wound sustained during the war, applied between 1987-2000 for enlistment with the Trust to receive Rastrio Sammani Bhata (State Honorarium Benefit) from 1987.

6. It is stated further that while the applications amongst other of the petitioners for Rastrio Sammani Bhata (State Honorarium Benefit) were pending for consideration, the Trust in its both 60th (sixty) meeting held on 26th November 1998 and chaired by its chairman, the then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, and decided that new applicants would be given Rastrio Sammani Bhata, if found proper, on investigation by the Deputy commissioner or Superintendent of police of the respective District and that following the meeting dated 26th November 1998 the petitioners obtained prescribed forms from the concerned authority and filled up the same with their particulars in detail and submitted to the Trust. The Trust considered some cases but did not consider the petitioners' cases for which the petitioners deprived of Rastrio Sammani Bhata from 1987. Subsequently, the Health consultant (medical practitioner) of the Trust requested by letter dated 14-1-2003 (Annexure F series) each of the petitioner to be present before the Medical Board for medical examination on specific dates with relevant medical documents with the indications of their disability. And in compliance with the said direction the petitioners attended the Medical Board and after thorough and proper medical checkup the said Medical Board confirmed their disability and selected the petitioners in "F" Category with 5% disability and on the basis of interview of the witnesses who identified the petitioners as genuine freedom fighters. Thereafter the Respondent No. 4 by letters on different dates individually, called the petitioners and confirmed the status of the petitioners as genuine disabled freedom fighters and recommended them as qualified to be listed with the Trust for receiving State Honorarium benefits and the respondents started to give Rastrio Sammani Bhata Taka 600 (six hundred) per months (Annexure-"G" series) instead of Taka 2004 (two thousand four) from 2003 and also suspended other facilities which the trust had provided as per trust resolution to other General disabled freedom fighters, by Memo No. মু : বি : ম:/প্র:-১/বিবিধ -৩৪/২০০২/৩৭১ ১৩ ইং কার্তিক ১৪১০/২৮ শে অক্টোবর ২০০৩।

7. As per order of Memo No. মু : বি : ম:/প্র:-১/বিবিধ -৩৪/২০০২/৩৭১ ১৩ ইং কার্তিক ১৪১০/২৮ শে অক্টোবর ২০০৩  the petitioners are getting their Rastrio Sammani Bhata at the rate of Taka 600 instead of Taka 2004 through their pass book although other 5% disabled freedom fighters are receiving State Honorarium at the rate of Taka 2004 per month from the respondents and that the Ministry of Defense Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh by its Memo No. Budget-1/94/D-8 dated 10th January, 1999 sanctioned an amount of Taka 1316 (one thousand three hundred Sixteen) per month for each general disabled freedom fighters.

8. As like as the petitioners of same category, 73 disabled freedom fighters filed Writ Petition No. 6235 of 2008 and 213 disabled wounded freedom fighters of "E" category Standard (1.19)% fixed by the Government filed Writ Petition Nos. 2182 of 2004, 3186 of 2004, 3262 of 2004, 4339 of 2004, 955 of 2005 and 7342 of 2007 in the Hon'ble High Court Division. In all writ petitions he Hon'ble High Court Division made the Rule absolute and directed the respondents to provide all the facilities due for disabled freedom fighters since 1999 and also to pay state Honorarium as per earlier rate of Taka 2004. Against the above judgment and order passed in the writ petition, the respondents filed Civil petition for leave to Appeal No. 1157-61 of 2007 before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court and Hon'ble Appellate Division also upheld the judgment and order of the High Court Division on 23-3-2008.

9. The petitioners urged the respondents by sending legal notice through their lawyer for providing such benefit as is being given to the same category as per regulation of Muktijudda Kallayan Trust and as per order of Hon'ble High Court Division of the Bangladesh as stated above and in compliance with order of the Apex Court, the Government issued memo No. Budget-1/94/0-8 dated 10-1-1999. But the respondents have not respondent to the legal notice of the petitioners under the above facts and circumstance, the petitioners have acquired a vested right to get the same remuneration from the year 1987 on being same footing and as such the petitioners are entitled to equal protection of law but the discrimination to have been made fixing the rate Taka 600 as allowance per month is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

10. The petitioners having been aggrieved by the decision of the respondents have filed this writ petition.

11. Mr JK Paul, the learned Advocate on behalf of the respondent No. 3 entered appearance and filed affidavit in opposition denying the material allegations and assertion of the petitioner. The learned Advocate stated in the affidavit-in-opposition inter alia that the selection of the petitioners as disabled freedom fighters are totally false and are hereby denied, only petitioner No. 15 Abdur Rab, son of Late Abdul Aziz of village Ambornagar, Police Station Begumganj, District-Noakhali was enlisted as disabled freedom fighter earlier and used to get state honorarium at the rate of Taka 2004 (two thousand and four taka) per month but this time his disability is found to be 5% and other petitioners for the 1st time are getting Taka 1,350 (one thousand three hundred and fifty taka) per month as their disability are found to be 5%.

12. It has been stated further that the petitioners did not challenged the Regulation of 2002 by virtue of which their medical examination was held Joddhahatta Mukti-joddha Kallayan Trust and the Government after thorough medical examination and on the basis of the medical report, the petitioners were found to be 5% disabled freedom fighters and they are given the "F" category facilities.

13. The respondent No. 3 further stated that the petitioners by submitting Annexure-"B" admitted that PO 94 of 1972 is the controlling law for the welfare of disabled (in capable persons who fails to perform any normal vocation, because of injuries suffered during the war of (Liberation) which is annexed as Annexure-B. In addition of power conferred in PO 94 of 1972, the Government promulgated Regulation in the year 1984 to regulate the affairs of rehabilitation of disabled freedom fighters through proper listing and payment of benefit which is annexed as Annexure-C. It is admitted that the petitioners' cases were not considered in the year 1999. Thereafter, in the year 2002 another Regulation is promulgated for ascertainment of disability of the new applicants prayed for honorarium and also to ascertain the degree of disability freedom fighters who have been receiving state honorarium and for the said reason the petitioners were issued notices Annexure-F on the basis of Regulation dated 31-3-2002 and they all appeared before the Medical Board for ascertainment of disability and it is found that their disability is 5%. According to the provisions laid down in the Regulation 1984, they were not entitled to get facilities of the disabled freedom fighters but received the allowance having disability within 20%-100%. It is further stated that the freedom fighters whose disability is found is less that 20% or who are on service or those are doing business with the help of Trust fund will be treated as rehabilitated disabled freedom fighters. According to provisions of Rule 3(Ga) of 1984 Regulation and under the said Regulation were enlisted for giving allowance which has been defined in definition Ka, Kha and Ga of Rule 3 of Regulation 1984. So, in the instant case all the petitioners are found to be 5% disabled after medical test and for the said reason, they are grouped in "F" category for granting minimum quantum of allowance. The grounds taken in the writ petitioner are not tenable in law.

14. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has taken us through the judgment and order 6-7-2007 passed in writ petition No. 7815 of 2005 and also placed the judgment passed in writ petition No. 3186 of 2004 and then taken us through the judgment of the Appellate Division and relying upon those judgments and orders submits that in the earlier cases, the respondents had reduced the allowance from Taka 2,004 to Taka 600 and while the General Freedom Fighters were receiving taka 1316/ and in the present case, the respondents fixed Taka 600 instead of Taka2004 though Taka 2,004 was fixed in January, 1999 as per decision of the 60th Meeting of the Board of Trust of the same category being "F" category who had 1 % - 19 % disability and by the above judgments the High Court Division and the Appellate Division directed the respondents to pay the allowance (Annexure-'K') at the rate fixed in January, 1999.

15. The learned Advocate further contends that it would be evident that the rate of allowance should have been as was fixed in January, 1999 in the 60th meeting of the Trust and as such, fixing the present allowance at the rate of Taka 600 have discriminated with other disabled Freedom Fighters who being the same category are receiving the allowance at the rate fixed in January, 1999 and as such, the fixation of Taka 600 per month should be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

16. The learned Advocate for the petitioners has submitted that giving benefit to some and denying the same to others on the same footing is not only illegal but also offends fundamental rights of the petitioners guaranteed under Article 28 and 29 of the Constitution. He cites the decision reported in 50 DLR 396 paragraph 8 which is reproduced below:

"8 In such circumstances we fail to understand why the petitioner refused the similar benefits to the respondent Nos. 2 to 22 when they became eligible under the agreement being promoted to the post of office assistants or equivalents and thus became entitled to get the scale. Giving benefit to some and denying the same to others under the same agreement and service condition, is not only illegal but also offends fundamental rights of the respondents guaranteed under Articles 28 and 29 of the Constitution. We, therefore, hold that in the aforesaid facts and circumstances the agreement is also applicable to the respondents."

17. Another decision reported in 55 DLR (AD) 132 paragraph 10 the latter part of which is reproduced below:

"10 (Later part) The matter of fixing the age of retirement of the Stewards and Stewardesses being gender-based the same has rightly been held by the High Court Division discriminatory and further the discrimination so made being violative of the Article 28 of the Constitution is not legal. There is another aspect as regards the matter of discrimination between the writ petitioners and the employees of the Corporation of the writ petitioners' category employed immediately before them. It is not disputed that employees of which of batch Nos. 1-27 of the writ petitioners category although were employed on contract but on satisfactory completion of initial period of employment they have been absorbed permanently in the service of the Corporation, but in the case of the writ petitioners that has not been followed, rather on completion of the initial period of employment instead of renewal of their agreement of employment they were given fresh employment. Since some employees of the Corporation inter se standing in the similar situation have not been treated in the similar or in other words have been treated differently from the others the contention of the writ petitioners that they have been discriminated against has rightly been found genuine by the High Court Division."

18. On the other hand, Rule has been opposed by the respondent No. 3 by filing affidavit in opposition. Mr JK Paul, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 3 refuting the submissions of the petitioners submits that Rastrio Sammani Bhata has been fixed after careful examination of the disability and the medical reports states that the degree of disability falls under category 'F', so, their Honorarium was fixed at Taka 600 on the basis of medical report which has been done on rational basis.

19. He further submits that there has been no breach of fundamental rights of the petitioners and also have not discriminated the petitioners with the same category of Freedom Fighters. He further submits that there has been no breach of fundamental rights of the petitioners as the basis has been determined on the basis of the Medical report of Juddahat Muktijudda Bachani Committee, it calls for no interference by the Hon'ble Court.

20. The Core question before us on the face of the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates of the parties as to whether Rastrio Sammani Bhata of the petitioners were rightly and legally fixed by the respondents.

21. In order to appreciate the contentions advanced by the learned Advocates, we have perused the writ petition, Annexure and other materials on record as well as the decisions annexed to the writ petition vide Annexure-K (judgment dated 6-7-2007 passed in writ petition No. 7815 of 2005, Writ petitioner No. 3362 of 2004 and Writ Petitioner 3186 of 2004) and the judgment of the Appellate Division decision judgment passed in Civil Petitioner for leave to appeal Nos. 1157-61 of 2007.

22. We have very carefully and meticulously gone through those decisions of both the Divisions and found that the High Court Division (where one of us namely Mr Justice ABM Khairul Haque is a signatory) in the similar matter in as much as in those cases the respondents reduced Bhata from Taka 2004 to Taka 600 but in this case the respondents fixed Taka 600 having 5% To disability of the Freedom Fighters. We have also found that their Lordships in the High Court Division had categorically taken into consideration of all pros corns along with the disability of the Freedom Fighters and examined the relevant laws and the law on natural justice and upon scrupulous scrutiny came to the conclusion, the relevant of which from the judgment passed in writ petition No. 3186 of 2004 are quoted for appreciation.

"We find the Trust was established by President's Order No. 94 of 1972 dated 7-8-1972, subsequently in 1984 Bangladeshi Muktijudda Kallayan Trust Regulation 1984 was promulgated, in order to regulate the affairs of the Trust covering the rehabilitation of disabled/wounded dependent of Shahid (martyr) Freedom Fighters, through proper listing and ensuing payment of benefit/allowance honorarium to them.

It appears that after examining all required documents of the petitioners and in compliance of the required legal formalities as enshrined in Regulation 1984, the petitioners were finally granted Rastrio Sammani Bhata under which they were allowed to receive a sum of Taka 2004 each on monthly basis. We are also find that the petitioners were listed as disabled Freedom Fighters with effect from January, 1999 as per the decision of the 60th meeting of the Board of Trustee of the Trust. Thereafter, they, as listed disabled Freedom Fighters have been receiving their respective "Rastrio Sammani Bhata" in full since January, 1999.

It is a matter of surprise, that after long lapse of 32 years, the degree of disabilities of the petitioners were again determined by the Committee and pursuant to the report dated 31-3-2003 (Annexure-X-3), the "Rastrio Sammani Bhata" of the petitioners were reduced to Taka 600 each, per month.

Admittedly, before passing the impugned orders, the petitioners were not served any notice or show cause, against the proposed action. They were not given any opportunity to be heard National Justice requires that before a person is punished an opportunity to show cause against the proposed punishment should be aforesaid to him.

The essential feature of the principle of natural justice is that no person should be deprived of his right without hearing before an independent authority. Its purpose is to prevent miscarriage of justice.

The concept of natural justice cannot be confined to any precise definition. It is not justice in the abstract or moral sense and is not even justice accordingly to natural law. The essential feature of the principle of natural justice is simply that no person shall be deprived of any vested right be any order, judicial or otherwise without a hearing before an independent authority, not interested in the proceedings or in any party to the proceedings:

In the case Saiyyid Abul A'la Maudoodi vs The Government of West Pakistan reported in 17 DLR (SC) 209=PLD 1964 (SC) 673 wherein it is held:

"Principle of audi alteram partem is applicable to administrative orders- The principle of natural justice requiring a hearing to be granted to a person before being condemned, applies not only to judicial o quasi-Judicial proceeding but also to administrative proceeding provided that the relevant statute does not exclude its application and requires the administrative authority concerned to base its decision on an objective determination of facts." This view receives support in the cases reported in 16 DLR (SC) 722, 49 DLR (AD) 177, 48 DLR (AD) 33, 31 DLR (AD) 272, 16 DLR (SC) 470, 11 DLR (SC) 113, 12 DLR (SC) 223, (1963) All ER-66.

With regard to the submissions as to no provision for show cause as advanced by the learned Counsel for the respondents. It will be pertinent to say that respective freedom fighter, against whom action is proposed to be taken, is entitled to such opportunity on principle of national justice, which are to be read in every enactment in the absence of a provision to the contrary. No present can be condemned without an opportunity to defend himself. The vested right to received "Rastrio Sammani Bhata" cannot be taken away without giving them any opportunity to be heard even there is no specific provision to show cause. Therefore, we are unable to accept his submissions. On the contrary, the submissions of the learned Counsel for the petitioners prevails and appears to have a good deal of force.

In view of the discussions made above and the preponderant judicial views emerging out of the authorities referred to above we are of the view that the impugned memos issued by the respondent No. 3 curtailing /reducing the "Rastrio Sammani Bhata" of the petitioners suffer from legal infirmities which call for interference by this Court. Thus the Rule having merit succeeds.

In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The impugned memos issued by the respondent No. 3 curtailing /reducing the "Rastrio Sammani Bhata" of the petitioners, are declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The respondents are directed to cause payment of "Rastrio Sammani Bhata" to the respective petitioners fixed at the time of award of the "Rastrio Sammani Bhata" in January, 1999.

The respondents are also directed to pay all arrear outstanding to the respective petitioner within two months from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment and order."

23. The respondent having been aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and orders preferred Civil Petitioner for leave to Appeal No. 1157- 61/2007 before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court. It appears that their Lordships have expressed the considered view on the subject of the similar matter and affirmed the findings of the High Court Division and for proper appreciation we are tempted to reproduce the relevant findings from the aforesaid judgment which are as follows:—

"We called upon the learned Counsel representing the leave petitions to address the Court as regard the finding of the High Court Division that the writ petitioners were paid Honorarium/Rastrio Sammani Bhata for 32 years in the light of the list prepared and published in the official Gazette and that before taking the impugned action i.e. cancelling curtailing, reducing or stopping payment of Honorarium/Rastrio Sammani Bhata whether the writ petitions were heard or that they were given opportunity to establish the fact that they were and are the Freedom Fighters and to establish that earlier they were listed as Freedom Fighters since they established that fact, i.e. Freedom Fighters, by reliable materials.

The learned Counsel for the petitioners could not refer to any materials or in other words from the materials as are in the paper books of the respective petitions for Leave to Appeal nor could produce any materials to establish that before taking the action in respective of the writ petitioners, who established their right to receive Honorarium /Rastrio Sammani Bhata as Freedom Fighters after being listed in the list of Freedom Fighters published in the official gazette and enjoyed the said right for the last 32 years without interruption or question from any corner. In the afore state of the matter we are of the view the High Court Division was not in error in making the Rules absolute upon arriving at the finding that the writ petitioners of the respective writ petitions were deprived of their establish right of receiving the Honorarium /Rastrio Sammani Bhata in an whimsical and capricious manner and that action impugned i.e. cancellation /curtailment/reduction/stop/non-payment of the Honorarium was a mala fide action of the Writ Respondents and same manifest from the nature and kind of the action complained of and is evident from the material on record. The materials in the paper books clearly demonstrate that the action was anything but not fair since the writ petitioners were deprived of the benefits, which they acquired upon establishment of the fact of their being freedom fighters and they were paid for the 32 years, for receiving Honorarium /Rastrio Sammani Bhata in total disregard of the university accepted principle of natural justice or in other words without hearing or affording opportunity to place their case and the action impugned was taken to their prejudice keeping them in dark.

The learned Counsels for the writ petitioner-respondents submitted that the action complained of was a motivated one and that the action impugned in the writ petitions was parochial as well as suffered bad faith and as such the high Court Division was correct in declaring action of the Writ Respondents illegal and of no legal effect.

The submission of the learned Counsels of the writ petitioner-Respondents in the back ground of the nature and kind of the action complained of as well as the materials on record appears to be of merit and thus worth consideration.

In view of the discussion made hereinbefore we are of the opinion that the judgments of the High Court Division sought to be appealed call for no interference by this Division." Accordingly, petitions are dismissed."

<u>24. Upon overall analysis of the above mentioned materials along with the judgment of both the Divisions, our conclusive view is that the respondents in issuing Memo No. Mu:/Pro/Bivid-34/2002-371 dated 28-10-2003 have committed fundamental wrong and also discriminated with the other disabled Freedom Fighters who are receiving allowance at the rate fixed in January, 1999 by the Trust and thereby, fixing of allowance at the rate of Taka 600 per month is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.</u>

25. We are of the opinion that the petitioners are entitled to receive Rastrio Sammani Rhata at the rate which was fixed in January, 1999.

26. The respondents are also directed to pay all outstanding allowance/allowances with effect from July 2003 to the respective petitioner within three-months from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment and order.

27. In the result, the Rule is disposed of with the observation made above and direction without any order as to cost.

Communicate the order at once to the respondents.

End.

lawyer:
Khandker Mahbub Uddin Ahmed with Shah Khashruzzaman and Toufique Newaz—For the Petitioner.
Garib Newaz with Maksuda Akhter—For Opposite Party No.1.
parties:
Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakha ------ Defendant-Appellant-Petitioner.
vs
Abdul Zakir & another ------ Plaintiff-Respondent Opposite Party.
full_judgment:
Granting of relief to plaintiff-opposite-party by Trial Judge in a suit declaring his Title in suit property and directing defendant-petitioner to release suit property in his favour and sustained by Appellate Judge in appeal prompted the latter to invoke this Court's Revisional Jurisdiction envisaged under section 115 of The Code of Civil Procedure (for short the Code) on laying this Revision Petition as petitioner.

2. Concurrent decisions have been recorded in a suit being Title Suit No. 160 of 1997 laid by plaintiff-opposite-party before Senior Assistant Judge, Sixth Court, Dhaka seeking:

(a) Decree declaring plaintiff's title on property described in schedule to the plaint which will be described as suit property

and

(b) Directory Decree directing Defend-ants to release suit property. In the suit, Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakhya and The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by Additional Deputy Commissioner (Land Acquisition), Dhaka are First and Second Defend-ants respectively. In Revision Petition they will be described as defendant-petitioner and defendant-opposite party.

3. Case of plaintiff-opposite-party as projected in plaint was that Yasin Bepari had been owner and possessor of suit property. Afsaruddin inherited suit property as grandson of Yasin Bepari and he remained in possession thereon. Suit property was wrongly recorded in the name of one Ayatunnessa and Afsaruddin instituted suit being Title Suit No. 55 of 1973 in Fifth Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. Suit was decreed. Decree was maintained upto High Court Division in appeal being First Appeal No. 60 of 1975 and title of Afsaruddin was established. Record of Right stood corrected in the name of Afsaruddin. On the death of Afsaruddin, his son Mobarak Miah got the entire suit property and being owner and possessor transferred suit property in favour of plaintiff-opposite party by deed of conveyance dated 22-9-1994. Plaintiff-opposite party got his name mutated in connected Record of Right on 15-11-1994 in Mutation Miscellaneous Case No. 11779/95 and has been exercising acts of possession on suit property on payment of rent to Government. The plaintiff-opposite party approached defendant-petitioner for approval of map for purpose of establishment of industry on suit property and then became aware that suit property was allegedly acquired by former DIT now Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha in Land Acquisition Case No. 2 of 1966-67. Defendant-petitioner did never take over possession of suit property and owners did not receive any compensation money and suit property was not required by Requiring Body and owner of suit property although possessed the same, the Requiring Body nor Acquiring Body and nor anybody else did exercise acts of possession on suit property for the last 30 years after alleged acquisition and did not undertake any development work. The owner being in exclusive possession of the suit property transferred the same in favour of plaintiff-opposite party. Plaintiff-opposite party on 5-6-1997 submitted a petition praying for release of suit property in his favour and defendant-petitioner refused to release suit property. Plaintiff-opposite party, thus, have been constrained to lay suit before Court seeking reliefs stated above.

4. Defendant-petitioner only contested the suit on presentation of written statement raising contentions that suit property along with other properties with houses standing thereon had been acquired by Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka in Land Acquisition Case No. 2 of 1966-67 and compensation money had been paid to owners of acquired property. Possession had been handed over to defend-ant-petitioner on 20-8-1985 and acquisition matter had been finalised through Gazettee Notification published on 24-12-1987. Plaintiff-opposite-party got no title and possession on suit property. Suit property vested with defendant-petitioner from the date of publication of Gazette Notification. Defendant-petitioner made improvements on suit property and in accordance with layout map, suit property had been allotted as industrial plots and there remained no scope for release of suit property.

5. Over the above pleadings learned Trial Judge framed four (4) issues which are hereunder:

i. Is the suit maintainable in its present form?

ii. Is the suit barred by limitation?

iii. Has the plaintiff title and possession on the suit property and is the suit releasable

and

iv. Is the plaintiff entitled to get reliefs as prayed for?

6. Evidences, both oral and documentary, had been led in support of contentions of respective parties. Two witnesses, plaintiff as PW 1 and vendor Mobarak as PW 2 stood on witness box in support of plaintiff's case. One witness, Kanungo of defendant-petitioner stood on witness box in support of defendant's case. Documents produced from plaintiff side had been exhibited as Exhibits 1 to 12. Documents of defendants had been exhibited as Exhibit Ka to Ga.

7. Learned Trial Judge took up Issue No. II firstly and he decided the issue in favour of plaintiff and found that the suit is not barred by limitation.

8. Learned Trial Judge then took up Issue No, III which is the fundamental issue in the suit. Learned Trial Judge decided issue No. III in favour of plaintiff. In deciding the said Issue learned Judge found:

(a) There is no denial from defendant side that vendor of plaintiff was the actual owner of suit property prior to alleged acquisition of suit property.

(b) Defendant could not submit any document in respect of claim as to payment of award money documents Exhibit Ka to Ga did not prove claim of defendant. From Exhibit 12 it appears that no payment of award money was made for acquisition of suit property in favour of plaintiff's vendor.

(c) Plaintiff had submitted deed dated 22-9-1994 Exhibit 5. Plaintiff had submitted documents in support of payment of rents, Exhibit 6 to 7 series. Documents Exhibit Ka to Ga PW 2 Mobarak (Vendor) supported the claim of plaintiff and documents, Exhibits 1 to 12 proved title and possession of plaintiff over suit property and suit property is releasable.

9. In view of decisions recorded in Issue Nos. 2 and 3. Issue Nos. 1 and 4 were, also, decided in favour of plaintiff.

10. Learned Trial Judge, thus awarded decree in favour of plaintiff granting relief sought by him. Trial Judge declared plaintiff's title on suit property and directed defendant Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha and The Government of The People's Republic of Bangladesh to release the suit property in favour of plaintiff within forty-five (45) days from date, on failure plaintiff is entitled to get the suit property released as per law. Judgment and decree is dated 30-11-1997.

11. Defendant having felt dissatisfied with the above adjudication as appellant sought setting aside through a medium of appeal being Title Appeal No. 48 of 1998 before learned District Judge, Dhaka. Learned Subordinate Judge and Second Commercial Court, Dhaka by Judgment and decree dated 29-7-1998 dismissed appeal and maintained Judgment and Decree passed by Trial Judge.

12. Learned Appellate Judge as last and final Judge of fact discussed and considered pleadings of the parties, evidence both oral and documentary and held:

(a)	Defendant's witness DW 1 in his testimony testified that the name of vendor of plaintiff and plaintiff had not been noted in the list of persons who were awarded compensation and it is evident that vendor of plaintiff did not receive any compensation in respect of acquired property. Exhibit 12 is, also an evidence that plaintiff's Vendor PW 2 did not receive any compensation money in respect of suit property.

(b)	From testimonies of witnesses it reveals that no work of earth cutting occurred on suit property land. Exhibit Ga, also, demonstrated that the character, nature and class plot of Nos. 615 and 616 (suit plots) were nal and ditch and suit property was unfit for setting up of industry.

(c) Suit property was not allotted to any person for establishment of Industry in spite of acquisition of the same in Land Acquisition Case No. 2 of 1966-67.

(d) Suit property remained unutilised since the year 1967.

(e) Suit property appeared to be in exclusive possession of plaintiff Vendor PW 2 and plaintiff got suit property by way of a sale deed from Vendor PW 2.

(f) Government did not take over actual possession of suit property for a period of more than 30 years. In recording those decisions learned Appellate Judge came in full agreement with the decisions rendered by learned Trial Judge.

13. Decisions that owners of suit property did not receive any compensation money in respect of acquired suit property and defendant-petitioner did not take over possession over suit property on the strength of acquisition in Land Acquisition Case No. 2 of 1966-67 and the vendor of plaintiff and, thereafter, plaintiff remained in possession for more than 30 years have been concluded by concurrent finding of fact.

14. Defendant still feeling dissatisfied approached this Court in this Civil Revision Petition as petitioner.

15. Mr Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, with Mr Shah Khashruzzaman and Mr Toufique Newaz, learned Counsel, appeared for defendant-petitioner. Plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 is represented by Mr Garib Newaz with Ms Maksuda Akhter, learned Counsels.

16. Basic ground and contention pressed into service from the side of defendant-petitioner is that suit property stood acquired under The Town Improvement Act of 1953 (hereinafter referred as The Act of 1953) in Land Acquisition Case No. 2 of 1966-67 and possession was handed over to petitioner and acquisition of suit property stood concluded on publication of Gazette Notification on 12-12-1987 and suit property vested with Government by operation of law and non-payment of compensation did not confer any title upon plaintiff who purchased suit property after acquisition and plaintiffs suit was misconceived and not tenable in law. Section 93A(4)-(h) of The Act of 1953 and The College of Music vs Government of Bangladesh 27 DLR 487, Abul Basher vs Bangladesh 50 DLR (AD) 11 and Jamir Ali vs Ministry of Land 52 DLR (AD) 176 have been referred to in support of contention raised.

17. Repelling the said contentions, argument had been put forward in bringing home submission from the side of plaintiff-opposite-party that no notice as mandated in law had been served upon owners of suit property and owners having not been given compensation money of the acquired suit property and defendant-petitioner having signally failed to prove the case of defendant as to payment of compensation money to plaintiff and defendant having not at all taken possession of suit property and having not exercised any acts of possession and suit property having been in possession of owners and, thereafter, of plaintiff and suit property having been unutilised plaintiff was entitled to have a declaration of title on suit property and to have the same released and Courts below properly and correctly awarded decree in favour of plaintiff and concurrent decisions reached by Courts below are not to be disturbed by this Court in the exercise of Revisional Jurisdiction under section 115 of The Code. Learned Advocate for plaintiff-opposite-party when confronted by this Court with the question put to him as to plaintiffs' entitlement to be graced with a decree declaring plaintiffs title on suit property contention has been pressed that even if plaintiff is not entitled to have a decree declaring his title on suit property but he is very much entitled to have a Directory Decree in the form of Mandatory Injunction directing defendant to release suit property from the mischief of Requisition and Acquisition proceeding. Plaintiff's entitlement to have decree declaring Title on suit property, thus, is not pressed. Support for contention has been sought to be drawn from Noushad Ahmed Chowdhury vs Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms 3 BLC 18, Government of Bangladesh vs Basaratullah, 40 DLR 554 and Dacca Improvement Trust vs Waliullah 28 DLR (AD) 150.

18. In the wake of rival contentions advanced from both sides the fundamental question which survives for determination in this Revision Petition is, whether plaintiff got entitlement to have a Directory Decree directing defendant-petitioner to release suit property from the ambit of Requisition and Acquisition proceeding and whether decree granted by Trial Judge and maintained by Appellate Judge directing defendant to release suit property warrants any interference by this Court in the exercise of its Revisional Authority under section 115 of the Code.

19. The question posed now may be approached and answered.

20. In approaching and answering to the question posed relevant provisions of law may profitably be noticed.

21. The Act of 1953 had undergone massive amendments by way of Town Improvement (Amendment) Act, 1987 (Act XXIX of 1987) which came into force on 30th April, 1987. By amendment sections 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 87, 88, 89, 90, 91, 91A, 92, 93,93A and 93B stood omitted.

22. Relevant portions of section 93A(1), 93A(2), 93A(3) and 93A(4) (h) of The Act of 1953 before amendment by Town Improvement (Amendment) Act 1987 are extracted hereunder.

23. Section 93A(1) enjoined that if in the opinion of the Provincial Government it was expedient or necessary so to do, for the construction, betterment of roads, waterways or any other communications, and the development of areas for residential, commercial, industrial purposes or for establishment of parks, playing fields and open space for the relief of congestion in any area to which this Act extends the Provincial Government might, by order in writing, requisition any property for the Board and could make such further orders as might appear to the Government necessary or expedient in connection with such requisition.

24. Section 93A(2) postulated that when any order of requisition had been made under the previous sub-section, it would be served on the owner of the property personally by delivering or tendering it to him or where the owner could not be found, it would be served by leaving an authentic copy of the order with some adult male member of the family of such owner, or if no such adult member could be found, the notice might be served by affixing a copy to some conspicuous part of the premises in which he was known to have last resided or carried on business, or personally worked for gain, and also by affixing such copy to some conspicuous part of the requisitioned property. Service of notice upon owners, thus, had been made imperative and mandatory

25. Section 93A(3) stated that when the order of the requisition had been served under sub-section (2) in respect of a property the Provincial Government might direct the District Magistrate to take and deliver possession of the property within 2 weeks to the Board, and the Board might use or deal with the property as might appear to it to be expedient.

26. Section 93A(4)(h) enshrined that the Provincial Government would publish in the Official Gazette a notice to the effect that the Provincial Government had decided to acquire requisitioned property for the Board and on and from the beginning of the day on which the notice was so published, the requisitioned property would vest absolutely in the Board free from all encumbrances and the period of such requisition of such property would end.

27. Section 79 had been inserted by The Town Improvement Amendment Act, 1987 which runs thus:

79. (1) The Kartripakha may for carrying out the purposes of this Act, acquire, by purchase, lease, exchange or otherwise, any land or interest in land and dispose of, by sale, lease exchange or otherwise, such land or any interest in such land.

(2) The acquisition of any land or interest in land for the Kartripakha under this section, or for any scheme under this Act, shall be deemed to be an acquisition for a public purpose within the meaning of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (II of 1982), and the provisions of the said Ordinance shall apply to all such proceedings.

28. The Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (hereinafter described as The Ordinance of 1982) has been made applicable to all such proceedings undertaken under The Town Improvement Act, 1953.

29. Section 93(c) has been inserted in The Town Improvement Act, 1953 by East Pakistan Ordinance No. III of 1965 which states that except as expressly provided in this Chapter, no Civil Court shall entertain any suit or application against any order passed or any action taken under this Chapter and all suits and appeals pending in any such Court against any such order passed or any action taken under this Chapter shall abate with effect from the date of coming into force of the Town Improvement (Amendment) Ordinance 1965. Under section 93(c) any order passed or any action taken thus has been made bar to jurisdiction of Civil Court and not any other matter and jurisdiction of Civil Court has been totally ousted.

30. Section 12(1) of Ordinance of 1982 states that where in any case the estimated amount of award of compensation has not been deposited by requiring person for acquisition of any property under section 5 within the period specified in section 7(4), all proceedings in respect of such acquisition shall, on the expiry of that period, stand abated and a declaration by the Deputy Commissioner to that effect shall be published in the Official Gazette.

31. Section 17(2) of The Ordinance of 1982 postulates that if any requiring person uses any acquired property in contravention of the provision of sub-section (1), or does not use it for the purpose for which it is acquired, he shall be liable to surrender the property to the Deputy Commissioner on being directed by him to do so.

32. Exhibit 3 is Judgment and Decree passed in Title Suit No. 55 of 1973 of Fifth Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka wherein plaintiff's vendor's father Afsaruddin's title has been declared against heirs of Ayetunnessa Bibi whose name stood wrongly recorded in the State Acquisition Record of Right. In that Title Suit present defendant-opposite party Government of The People's Republic of Bangladesh had been defendant No. 15. Exhibit-4 is a Judgment passed by a Division Bench of High Court Division in Appeal from Original Decree No. 60 of 1975 wherein Judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 55 of 1973 had been maintained by the High Court Division on dismissing First Appeal filed by defendants of that Title suit. Defendant-opposite party is very much bound by said Decree. Exhibit 5 is deed of conveyance executed by Mobarak Mia, PW 2 Vendor and owner of suit property in favour of plaintiff. Exhibit 6 a Duplicate Carbon Receipt in respect of mutation and sub-division of holding in the name of vendor PW 2. The order of mutation and separation of holding in the name of vendor PW 2 is dated 29-11-1992. Exhibit Kha is a Rent Receipt showing payment of rent by Vendor PW 2. Rent Receipt is dated 16-8-1992. Exhibit 7(Ka) is Duplicate Carbon Receipt showing mutation and division of holding in the name of plaintiff. Exhibit 7 is Rent Receipt manifesting payment of rent by plaintiff to Tahsil office, Tejgaon Circle, Dhaka. Exhibit 7 (kha) is Mutated Khatian in the name of plaintiff and the order of mutation and separation of holding is dated 15-12-1994. Exhibit Nos. 8 and 9 are two petitions addressed to Chairman, Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakha praying for release of suit property. Exhibit 10 is a letter contained in Memo No. Sha-8/Raj /8/94 /8 dated 10-1-96 sent by Senior Assistant Secretary of Works and Housing to the Chairman, Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakha for consideration of prayer filed by Vendor PW 2 for release of suit property. Exhibit 12 is a document showing that in the Award prepared in Land Acquisition Case No. 2 of 1966-67 the name of Vendor or the heirs of Afsaruddin did not appear as Awardee. Exhibit Ka is Gazette Notification. Exhibit Ga is defendant's document detailing the names of awardees for properties acquired in Land Acquisition Case.

33. The above Exhibits demonstrate that plaintiff-opposite party in the presence of present defendant-opposite party, The Government of The People's Republic of Bangladesh, obtained decree in Title Suit No. 55 of 1973 and that decree was maintained upto High Court Division in First Appeal. Vendor Mobarak Miah got his name mutated in connected Record of Right and got holding separated through Revenue Officer of Government. Plaintiff-opposite party on the strength of the sale deed dated 22-9-1994 got his name mutated in connected Record of Right and, also, got holding separated and paid rents to Government. Revenue authority who is an organ of the Government accepted rents from plaintiff-opposite party and rent receipts are evidences of possession of plaintiff over suit property. Vendor PW 2 filed petition for release of suit property and the said prayer had been forwarded to defendant-petitioner by Ministry of Works. Exhibit 12 is an evidence that no award was prepared in the name of vendor PW 2, the owner of suit property. DW 1 Kanungo of defendant-petitioner gave testimony that in Award List the name of vendor or the plaintiff did not appear. No evidence came forth that suit property had been allotted to some persons for the purpose of establishment of industry. No paper had been produced from side of defendant-petitioner that notices as required under law had been served upon owner i.e. vendor PW 2 or his father. Exhibit 12 and Exhibit Ga and the testimony of DW 1demonstrate that compensation money had not been even assessed not to speak of preparation of award and payment of award money to owner vendor side. True it is that Gazette Notification had been made on 12-12-1987 but in the absence of service of notices upon the owner Vendor PW 2 as mandated under section 93A of The Town Improvement Act, 1953 and, also, in absence of any evidence of taking actual possession over suit property, Gazette Notification dated 12-12-1987 has got no legal basis and validity and also binding force and the same can be characterized to be a paper published in colourful exercise of power. Gazette Notification cannot be evidence that proceeding to Requisition and then Acquisition without proof of service of notice upon owner and also of taking of possession and exercising of acts of possession over the suit property had been proved and established. The bar of section 93(c) of The Town Improvement Act is, also, not applicable to this Gazette Notification which had been published in colourful exercise of power.

34. This takes me to the authorities relied upon from the side of defendant-petitioner. Before adverting to authorities cited from both sides it is to be kept in view that decision is only an authority for what it actually decides. It cannot be quoted for a proposition that may seem to follow from it. Every Judgment must be read applicable to the particular facts proved or assumed to be proved. The generality of expression that may be found cannot be intended to be exposition of whole law but must be regarded as governed or qualified by the particular facts of the case in which such expression occurs.

35. In The College of Music vs Secretary, Revenue Department, 27 DLR 487 Government's decision to requisition or not to requisition of property is final was point for decision in that case. It was held that the Third Party got no say in such matter in respect of Government's decision to requisition or not to requisition a property and High Court Division got not power to interfere with Government's decision. The fact and circumstances of the case cited got no manner of application in the fact and circumstances of the case in hand and defendant-petitioner cannot get any benefit from this authority. In Abul Basher vs Bangladesh 50 DLR (AD) 11 original owners had already received 90% of their compensation money and only 10% remained unpaid and after getting 90% compensation money they claimed release of requisitioned property on the basis of Inter-Ministerial Communications. In said case it has been held that no legal and vested right has accrued in favour of petitioner by mere Inter-Ministerial Communications and petitioner cannot have any legal right to ask for return of land. In the case in hand, no evidence had been placed before Court manifesting that at least some compensation money had been paid. The fact and circumstances of the case are quite distinguishable in the fact and circumstances of the case in hand and got no bearing. In Jamir Ali vs Secretary, Ministry of Land 52 DLR (AD) 176 section 12 of Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance of 1982 had been considered and in that case principle laid down is that non-payment of compensation within one year from the date of decision of Government for acquisition of land as contemplated under section 12 of 1982 Ordinance did not render such land liable to be released. In the case in hand no payment of compensation had been made not to speak of whether it was within one year or more than one year. Defendant-petitioner side, also, cannot have any benefit from this authority as the said is quite distinguishable.

36. I shall now address myself to authorities relied upon from side of plaintiff-opposite party. In Dacca Improvement Trust vs Waliullah 28 DLR (AD) 150, scope and applicability of section 93(c) had been considered along with other aspects. It was held therein that in view of the nature of the case as made out in plaint it cannot be maintained that suit is barred under provision of section 93C of the Town Improvement Act and this point was considered in disposing of a petition laid under Order VII, rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejecting a plaint on the question of maintainability. The authority cited is applicable in the manner that in view of nature and fact and circumstances of case and relief sought by plaintiff-opposite party bar of section 93C of The Act cannot be made attracted in respect of plaintiff-opposite party's suit. In Government of Bangladesh vs Basaratullah, 40 DLR 554, non-service of notice upon owner before decision taken by Government to acquire requisitioned property came up for consideration before the High Court Division. It was held that notice under section 5(1a) and 5(3) is mandatory before Government can at all decide to acquire requisitioned property far less publish a notification to that effect and if no notices were received or if notices were invalid or illegal then the subsequent acquisition under section 5(7) is, also, illegal. The observation of their Lordships are couched in the following language.

"A notice under section 5(1a) and 5(3) is mandatory before the Government can at all decide to acquire any requisitioned property, far less publish a notification to that effect. If no such notices were received or if notices were invalid or illegal then the subsequent acquisition under section 5(7) is also illegal. We concur with the Courts below that the Gazette Notification dated 25-6-73 has no legal basis or validity or binding force and that it is illegal and void. The bar of section 14A is also not applicable to this Gazette Notification."

Section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 was bar to Jurisdiction of Civil Court. It has been further held that mandatory injunction given under the circumstances is the most appropriate and correct decree. The fact and circumstances of the case is applicable in the sense that no evidence came forth from side of defendant-petitioner as to service of notice upon owners of acquired property as required under section 93A(1) of The Act of 1953. In Noushad Ahmed Chowdhury vs Government of Bangladesh 3 BLC 18 section 79 of The Act of 1953, section 17 of The Ordinance of 1982 and section 93A(4)(h) of The Act of 1953 had been considered. The High Court Division taking into account fact and circumstances of the case and also, taking stock of relevant provisions of law directed the respondent i.e. Requiring body, to release the property in favour of petitioners who are the owners. The authority is wholly applicable in fact and circumstances of case in hand though that was under Writ Jurisdiction under Article 102 of The Constitution.

<u>37. It has already been posited that compensation money had not been given to the owners and in the award list the name of owners did not appear as evidenced from Exhibit 12 and Exhibit Ga and, also, from the testimony of DW 1 who is no other than Kanungo of defendant-petitioner. In the absence of evidence on the part of defendant-petitioner and defendant-opposite party in respect of payment of compensation money of acquired suit property the proceeding in respect of acquisition stood abated under section 12(1) of The Ordinance of 1982. The suit property was not utilised by requiring body and remained unused and suit property under the provision of section 17(2) of The Ordinance of 1982 is required to be released by defendant-petitioner Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakha as well as defendant-opposite party, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and hand over to plaintiff-opposite party who stepped into the shoes of owner Vendor PW 2 on strength of a deed of conveyance dated 22-9-1994. Defendant-petitioner and defendant-opposite party cannot keep suit property unused and unutilised for years and decades and cannot deny right of plaintiff-opposite party to get suit property released.</u>

<u>38. Examination of decision, reasons and conclusion reached by Trial Judge and maintained by Appellate Judge directing defendant-petitioner and defendant-opposite party to release suit property in favour of plaintiff-opposite party indicates that those rested upon proper and correct assessment of evidence and materials brought on record and fact and circumstances of case and, also, correct application and appreciation of law. The decisions of Trial Judge and Appellate Judge are concluded by concurrent decisions of fact warranting no interference by this Court in the exercise of Revisional Jurisdiction under section 115 of the Code.</u>

39. The Rule arising out of Civil Revision Petition under section 115 of the Code is devoid of any substance and the same stands discharged. Decisions recorded by Courts below are maintained.

40. Regard being had to the fact and circumstances of the case I direct the parties to bear their respective costs.

41. Lower Court Record be sent down as immediate as possible.

Copy of this Judgment be transmitted to Courts below.

End.

Md Ozair Farooq with Sk Md Morshed and Md Shakhawat Hossain, Advocates—For the Petitioner. 
Golam Rabbani, Advocate—For the Opposite Parties.
