Abdul Aziz and others ------ Petitioners 
vs
Kabir Ahmed Patwary & ors ------ Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This revisional application at the instance of the defendants under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the judgment and decree dated 14-11-2000 passed by the learned District Judge, Lakshmipur in Title Appeal No. 117 of 1996 allowing the appeal and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 31-8-1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Lakshmipur in Title Suit No. 4 of 1992 dismissing the suit.

2. The opposite parties Nos. 1 to 4 as plaintiffs instituted the suit for declaration that the order passed on 24-11-1991 by the opposite party No. 5 Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 104 of 1988 affirming the order of redemption of the suit land dated 25-9-1984 of Upazila Revenue Officer, Raipur, was illegal and without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs and in respect of the suit property measuring 1.20 acres and out of this land, 0.32 acres appertained to plot Nos. 200/2001 of khatian No. 101 and 0.88 acres appertained to plot Nos. 62/ 202/204 of khatian No. 130 of mouza Char Beconsfield, Upazila-Raipur, District-Lakshmipur.

3. The case of the plaintiffs-opposite parties, in short, is that the suit land belonged to the petitioners Abdul Aziz and Bodiuzzaman who transferred the same to Bashirullah Bepari for a consideration of Taka 1,000 by a kabala dated 22-12-1960 on condition of repayment of consideration money within 6(six) years ensured by a separate deed of agreement for re-conveyance made on the same date; that Bashirullah while possessing and enjoying that suit land transferred the same to opposite party No. 6 Ledu Miah alias Lokman Miah subject to the condition of repurchase on 6-11-1962; that the defendants petitioners did not receive the re-conveyance within time, that opposite party No. 6 Ledu Miah sold the suit land to defendant No. 3 namely, petitioner No. 2 Bodiuzzaman on 20-9-1977 who again sold the same to the opposite party No. 6 Ledu Miah alias Lokman Miah on 16-3-1979; that opposite party No. 6 Ledu Mia sold the suit land along with other land to the plaintiffs-opposite parties Nos. 1 to 4 by 4 kabalas dated 17-8-1983, 18-8-1983, 8-10-1986 and 20-10-1986.

4. The further case of plaintiffs-opposite parties is that defendant-petitioner No. 1 Abdul Aziz Mia obtained an order of redemption of the suit land dated 25-9-1984 passed by the Upazila Revenue Officer in Miscellaneous Case No. 239/923 of 1973-74.

5. As against the order dated 25-9-1984 of the Upazila Revenue Officer, Raipur the proforma defendant Ledu Miah filed a petition before the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Lakshmipur, who vacated the order of the Upazila Revenue Officer in due course. Thereafter, the defendant No. 2 Abdul Aziz filed a review petition before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), Lakshmipur, and the review petition was allowed by him affirming the order dated 25-9-1984 passed by the Upazila Revenue Officer, Raipur. It also transpired that the Miscellaneous Appeal being No. 4 of 1984 was filed in the court of the Assistant Judge, Raipur as against the said order of the Upazila Revenue Officer on declaring the same as illegal, fraudulent, void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiff which was dismissed on 24-6-1986.

6. Thereafter the opposite party No. 6 Ledu Miah preferred an appeal before the opposite party No. 5 Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong against the order of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 104 of 1988 and the opposite party No. 5 by his order passed on 24-11-1991 ultimately affirmed the order of redemption of the Upazila Revenue Officer dated 25-9-1984. The plaintiff came to know about all the developments relating to the suit land only on 23-12-1991. Hence this suit for declaration that the order of the defendant No.1 Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong dated 24-11-1991 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 104 of 1988 is illegal, void, without jurisdiction, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

7. The defendant Nos. 2 and 3 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. They have traversed the material allegations made in the plaint. The defence case, in short, is that the suit is not maintainable as framed; that the suit is barred by the principles of estoppel, waiver and acquiescence and that the suit is hit by the principle of res judicata. It is also stated that the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 were the original owners of the suit property and they mortgaged the same to Bashir Ullah Bepari with an agreement for re-conveyance executed by him on 22-12-1960. The period of re-conveyance was for 6 years. The entire transaction was a complete usufructuary mortgage within stipulated period of 6 years.

8. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 Abdul Aziz and Bodiuzzaman asked Bashir Ullah Bepari time and again to reconvey the suit property on receipt of the mortgage money of Taka 1000 but in vain. At a subsequent stage Bashir Ullah Bepari disclosed that he had transferred the suit land to Ledu Miah in violation of the terms of agreement. It is also stated that finding no other alternative, the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 Abdul Aziz and Bodiuzzaman filed a Miscellaneous Case before the Sub-divisional Magistrate of Noakhali for redemption of the suit land in view of the President's Order Nos. 88 and 136 of 1972 and the President's Order No. 24 of 1973. The miscellaneous case was ultimately transferred to Upazila Revenue Officer who in his turn passed an order of redemption on 25-9-1984 holding the transaction as a complete usufructuary mortgage. As against the order of the Upazilla Revenue Officer, Raipur, Ledu Miah filed an appeal before the Assistant Judge, Raipur which was dismissed. At one stage, the Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Rev), Lakshmipur, vacated the order of redemption of the Upazila Revenue Officer of Raipur. Thereafter, on review, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) of Lakshmipur reversed his earlier order and affirmed the order of the Upazila Revenue Officer. The defendant No. 1 Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong also affirmed the order of redemption dated 25-9-1984 passed by the Upazila Revenue Officer in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 104 of 1988. It is further stated that the suit has been brought on some false and frivolous allegations as such the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.

9. After hearing the parties and on an appraisal of the evidence on record, the learned trial Judge dismissed the suit holding the transaction to be a complete usufructuary mortgage and, as such, the same is redeemable by the impugned judgment and decree dated 31-8-1996.

10. Being aggrieved at and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 31-8-1996, the plaintiffs have preferred appeal being No. 117 of 1996 before the learned District Judge, Lakshmipur.

11. During the trial, the plaintiffs examined one witness in support of this case. On behalf of the plaintiffs, PW 1 Kabir Ahmed Patwary is plaintiff himself. The contesting defendants examined one witness in support of their case. For the defendant, Altaf Hossain, who is the son of defendant No. 2 Abdul Aziz, was examined as DW 1.

12. On behalf of the plaintiffs Exhibits 1 to 5 were filed as Exhibits 1, 1(A), (B) (C), (D)2 and 4(Ka) which are different types of deeds. The Exhibit 3 is the certified copy of the order sheets of case No. 31 of 1984-85 of ADC(Rev) and Exhibit 5 is the certified copy of the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 104 of 1988 of Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong. On behalf of the defendant, Exhibits 'Ka' to 'Chha' were filed. Exhibit 'Ka' is power of attorney, Exhibit 'Kha' is certified copy of the agreement, Exhibit 'Ga' is certified copy of the case No. 239/923 of 1973-74, Exhibit Ga(1) is the certified copy of the writ of delivery of possession and Exhibit 'Gha' is certified copy of the order sheets of Miscellaneous Appeal No. 4 of 1984 and Exhibits 'Oma', 'Cha', 'Chha', and 'Ja' are the certified copies of order sheets of proceedings of different revenue courts.

13. The learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Lakshmipur framed following issues:

1. Is the suit competent as framed?

2. Is the suit hit by the principle of res-judicata?

3. Can the sale of the suit property to Bashir Ullah Bepari with an agreement for re conveyance executed by him on the self-same date be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. If so, is it capable of redemption?

4. Are the impugned judgment and decree of the court below valid and sustainable in law?

14. The learned Subordinate Judge by his judgment and decree dated 31-8-1996 dismissed the suit and affirmed the order dated 24-11-1991 in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 104 of 1988 passed by the learned Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong.

15. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 31-8-1996, the plaintiffs-opposite parties took the appeal before the learned District Judge, Lakshmipur being Title Appeal No. 117 of 1996 and the appeal was heard by the learned District Judge who by his judgment and decree dated 14-11-2000, reversed the judgment of the trial Court. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 14-11-2000 the petitioners moved this court and obtained the present Rule.

16. Mr Md Ismail with Mr Shihabuddin Mahmood, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the suit is not maintainable and the same is also barred by principles of res judicata, estoppel, waiver and acquiesce that the petitioners had been continuously and consistently fighting for the re-conveyance and redemption of the suit land, first from Bashirullah and thereafter from his vendee opposite party No. 6 Ledu Miah alias Lokman and ultimately, started Miscellaneous Case No. 239/ 923 of 1973-74 in the Court of the Sub-divisional Officer, Noakhali which eventually gave rise to the suit which was also dismissed. It is further submitted that the transaction dated 22-12-1960 was never dead, past or closed.

17. Mr Ismail further submits that the defendants-petitioners obtained an order of redemption on 25-9-1984 and got delivery of possession thereunder on 2-10-1984 against the vendor of the plaintiffs-opposite parties in Miscellaneous Case No. 239/923 of 1973-74 and that the plaintiffs-opposite parties were fully aware of the redemption proceedings starting with the aforesaid case and ending in the impugned order dated 24-11-1991 from its very inception, in view of the fact that the vendor's knowledge was the knowledge of the vendee and that their title deeds were made while their vendor was out of possession of the suit land and that thereby the suit was hit by the provision of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. He further submits that findings of the learned appellate Court that the transaction dated 20-12-1960 was past and closed before the aforesaid orders of the President came into force being based on misconception of fact and law.

18. The learned Advocate for the petitioners placed before us the decisions in the case of Bangladesh vs Haji Abdul Gani Biswas and others reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233, in the case of Md Osman Gani Talukder alias Sijat Ali Talukder vs Md Osman Ali Mondal reported in 1996 BLD 165, in the case of Rakhal Chandra Das and others vs Benecha Khatun and others reported in 24 DLR 42, in the case of Mokthar Masum Abedin and others vs Niranjan Kumar Mondal and others reported in 56 DLR 341, in the case of Meghaji Mohanji Thakkar vs Anant Pandurang reported in AIR (35) 1948 Bombay 396, in the case of Shah Alam Sheikh and others vs Syed Ali and others reported in 4 BLC 331, in the case of Sheikh Belal Uddin Bilu vs Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs reported in 4 BLC 336, in the case of Rafiqul Alam (Md) vs Mustafa Kamal and others, reported in 42 DLR (AD) 137, in the case of Omar Ali vs Idris Meah reported in 35 DLR 209, in the case of Bangladesh Leaf Tobacco Company Ltd vs Md Abdul Mannan and others reported in 43 DLR 7, in the case of Jamal Uddin vs Rabeya Begum reported in 32 DLR 63, in the case of Jamila Khatun vs Md Lutfor Rahman @ Nefasiur and others reported in 3 BLC 306, in the case of Darasatullah and others vs Manik Mondal and others reported in 36 DLR (AD) 88, in the case of Ashwani Kumar Karmaker being dead his heirs Sree Radha Raman Karmaker and others vs Hari Mohan & others reported in 36 DLR (AD) 1, and in the case of Abdus Satter being dead his heirs Sayera Khatun and others vs Abdun Noor and others reported in 49 DLR 414 in support of his contention.

19. Mr Khair Ezaz Masud, the learned Advocate for the opposite parties, submits that the transfer of the suit property to Bashirullah Bepari by the defendant Nos. 2, and 3 was an out and out sale subject to an agreement for re-conveyance executed by Bashirullah Bepari in favour of his vendors and the entire transaction was not a complete usufructuary mortgage as held by the learned trial Judge and since the transaction was not a complete usufructuary mortgage, the question of its redemption does not arise at all.

20. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties cited the rulings in the case of Mrs Feroza Majid and another vs Jiban Bima Corporation represented by its Managing Director reported in 1987 BLD (AD) 124, in the case of Mohadeb Chandra Mondal and another vs Dulal Chandra Mondal and other reported in 2005 BLD (AD) 233, in the case of Dildar Ahmed Choudhury vs Farooque Ahmed Choudhury and another reported in 27 DLR 138, in the case of Abdur Rauf and others vs Abdul Hamid Khan and others reported in 17 DLR (SC) 515, in the case of Chy Sir Muhammad Zafarullah Khan, Sheikh Ijaz Ahmed, Begum Ijaz Ahmed and Ch Asadullah Khan vs Custodian of Evacuee Property West Pakistan, Karachi, Additional Rehabilitation and Settlement Commissioner, Hyderabad and 4 others reported in 17 DLR (SC) 126, in the case of Md Naimuddin Sarder @ Naimuddin Sarder vs Md Abdul Kalam Biswas @ Md Abul Kalam Basiruddin @ Abul Kalam Azad & another reported in 39 DLR (AD) 237, in the case of Joynal Abedin and others vs Mafizur Rahman and others reported in 44 DLR (AD) 162, in the case of Abdullah and 3 others vs Abdul Karim and others reported in 20 DLR (SC) 205, in the case of RM Subramanian vs Sundaram Iyer reported in AIR 1963 Madras 217, in the case of Chellammal and others vs Aiyamperumal Kudumban and others reported in AIR 1937 Madras 495, in the case of Bangladesh Water Development Board represented by its Chairman vs Syed Moazzam Hossain and others reported in 1 BLC (AD) 13 and in the case of Mokbul Hossain and others vs Akhil Kumar Saha and others reported in 1985 BLD 76 in support of his contention.

21. The only point for determination is, whether the learned District Judge committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision in passing the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-11-2000.

22. Admittedly, the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 Abdul Aziz and Badiuzzaman were the original owners-in-possession of the suit property. It is also admitted that on 22-12-1960 they transferred the suit property in favour of Bashirullah Bepari for consideration of Taka 1000 and that on the self-same date, Bashirullah Bepari executed an agreement for re-conveyance of the suit property in favour of his vendors Abdul Aziz and Bodiuzzaman. It is also admitted that the maximum period of re-conveyance of the suit property to the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 by Bashirullah Bepari was 6 years as mentioned in the agreement for reconveyance. It is also undisputed that Bashirullah Bepari transferred the suit property to Ledu Miah before expiry of the stipulated period of 6 years. There is no denying the fact that the plaintiffs-petitioners are the transferees of the suit property from the transferor Ledu Miah by 4 kabalas dated 17-8-1983, 18-8-1983, 8-10-1983 and 20-10-1986.

23. It also appears from the record that the petitioner No. 1 had obtained an order of redemption of the suit land against the opposite party No. 6 on 25-9-1984 passed by the Upazila Revenue Officer Raipur, in Miscellaneous Case No. 239/923 of 1973-74 under provisions of President's Order Nos. 88 and 136 of 1972 and No. 24 of 1973; that opposite party No. 6 Ledu Miah alias Lokman Miah preferred SA Petition No. 39 of 1984-85 against the aforesaid order before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Lakshmipur who was eventually pleased to affirm the impugned order dated 25-9-1984; that the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 4 of 1984 was preferred against the aforesaid order of redemption dated 25-9-1984 in the court of Upazila Munsif, Raipur, which was also dismissed on 24-6-1986; that the opposite party No. 5 also had affirmed the aforesaid order of redemption by his order passed on 24-11-1991 in Miscellaneous Case No. 104 of 1988.

24. The opposite parties Nos. 1 to 4 as plaintiffs instituted the suit for declaration that order dated 24-11-1991 passed by the learned Additional Divisional Commissioner. Chittagong Division, Chittagong, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 104 of 1988 affirming the order of redemption dated 25-9-1984 of Upazila Revenue Officer, Raipur in respect of the suit land is illegal and without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

25. The main contention of the petitioners is that the opposite parties Nos. 1 to 4 as plain-tiffs had no locus standi to bring the suit as the land purchased by the plaintiffs does not relate to the suit land.

26. In this connection, the learned Advocate for the petitioners took us to the paragraph 13 of the written statement wherein it is stated that the plaintiffs did not acquire any title in the suit land by virtue of deeds dated 17-8-1983, 18-8-1983, 8-10-1986 and 20-10-1986 nor did the plaintiffs get any title thereof.

27. DW 1 Altaf Hossain, son of Abdul Aziz, denied in his cross-examination the contention of the plaintiffs that Ledu Miah did not transfer the suit land to the plaintiffs by virtue of alleged 4(four) deeds. He categorically stated in his cross-examination that the land of those 4(four) deeds was non-suited which does not relate to the suit land. In comparison of the schedule of kabala deeds filed by the plaintiffs marked Exhibit 1(B), 1(C) and 1(d) with the schedule of the plaint, it appears that the area of suit land is 1.20 acres and out of this land 0.32 acres appertained to plot Nos. 200/201 of khatian No. 101 and 0.88 acres appertained to plot Nos. 62/202/204 of khatian No. 130 of mouza Char Beconsfield. But the plaintiffs have purchased only 22½ decimals from plot Nos. 200/201 whereas the area of suit land in these plots is 0.32 acres. The plaintiffs purchased .34 acres from plots No. 62/202/204 whereas the area of suit land of these plots is 0.88 acres. Thus it appears that the plaintiffs have not purchased the entire suit land. There is no denying of the fact that there are more lands in these plots but the plaintiffs have totally failed to prove that the suit land and the land purchased by the plaintiffs are identical.

28. The contesting defendants by adducing evidence have succeeded in proving that the land purchased by the alleged 4(four) deeds are non-suited land. Since the plaintiffs-opposite parties Nos. 1 to 4 have no specific title and interest in the suit land, so they have no locus standi to bring the suit.

29. It appears from the record that the petitioner No. 1 Abdul Aziz filed Miscellaneous Case No. 239/923 of 1973-74 for redemption of the suit land against the opposite party No. 6 Ledu Miah and obtained the order of redemption on 25-9-1984; that opposite party No. 6 preferred SA Petition No. 39 of 1984-85 against the aforesaid order before the Additional Deputy Commissioner Lakshmipur who eventually affirmed the order dated 25-9-1984; that the opposite party No. 6 preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 4 of 1984 against the aforesaid order of redemption dated 25-9-1984 in the court of Upazila Munsif, Raipur, which was dis-missed on 24-6-1986 and that the opposite party No. 6 again preferred Miscellaneous Case No. 104 of 1988 before the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong, against the order dated 25-9-1984 passed by the learned Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), Lakshmipur who affirmed the order dated 25-9-1984 by his order dated 24-11-1991.

30. As per section 147 of SAT Act, the proper course was to prefer appeal to Board of Administration but the opposite party No. 6 Ledu Miah did not prefer any appeal there and without taking the proper and legal way, the successors of opposite party No. 6 Ledu Miah filed Title Suit No. 4 of 1992 in the court of Subordinate Judge which was dismissed on contest. The successors of the opposite party No. 6 i.e. the plaintiffs, are bound by the result of the legal proceedings of their predecessors.

31. In all the proceedings mentioned above the plaintiffs were not parties. It is the contention of the plaintiffs that they purchasing the suit land from Ledu Miah by four kabala deeds dated 17-8-1983, 18-9-1983, 8-10-1986 and 20-10-1986 acquired right and title in the suit land and filed Title Suit No. 4 of 1992 in the court of the learned Subordinate Judge praying for a declaration that the order dated 25-11-1991 by the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong, Division, Chittagong, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 104 of 1988 affirming the order of redemption of the suit land dated 25-9-1984 of Upazila Revenue Officer, Raipur was illegal and without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff.

32. It appears from Exhibit Ga (1) which is an order of the delivery of possession that as per the order dated 25-9-1984 of Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong the defendants petitioners were given possession of the suit land on 2-10-1984 and the defendant-petitioners took delivery of possession through proper authority on 2-10-1984.

33. In the eye of law, even a symbolical possession obtained through court has the effect of actual possession so far as the judgment debtors are concerned. Under such circumstances, the plaintiff's suit for simple declaration of title without any prayer for recovery of khas possession is barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, as at the time of filing of the suit the plaintiffs had no possession.

34. The court of appeal below did not consider that the defendants-petitioners had already taken delivery of possession through court on 2-10-1984. The plaintiffs-opposite parties filed Title Suit No. 4 of 1992 on 21-1-1992 when they had no possession in the suit land. Thus, the suit filed by the plaintiffs for declaration without the prayer for khas possession is not maintainable in its present form.

35. Any party to the suit or any proceedings may challenge the judgment and order only on the ground of fraud or collusion. The plaintiffs did not urge any ground of fraud or collusion about the order dated 24-11-1991 of the Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong, nor did they give particulars of persons who are alleged to have committed the fraud nor did they take any positive steps towards furtherance of the said object. Fraud must be specifically pleaded and proved but in the instant case plaintiffs-opposite parties did not try to make out any case of fraud and since no evidence has been adduced in the suit before the trial Court as regard fraud, so the question of proving the same does not arise at all. Moreover, since the same is not in the pleadings, plaintiff-opposite parties cannot plead the same and, in fact, section 44 of the Evidence Act is a bar.

36. It appears from above discussion that the plaintiffs failed to prove his title and possession in the suit land. A man having no title and possession cannot file a suit for declaring a legal order passed by any court who decided the matter on contest. Moreso, it appears from records that the plaintiffs were not parties in the proceedings of Upazila Revenue Officer, Raipur, or in the Miscellaneous Appeal of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev), Lakshmipur or in the proceedings before the Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong. In all these proceedings, the alleged predecessor-in-interest Ledu Miah alias Lokman Miah was party who contested the matter.

<u>37. Being defeated in the court of Additional Divisional Commissioner, Ledu Miah did not prefer any appeal before the Board of Land Administration which was a proper forum to ventilate his grievances nor did he file any case before the civil Court on the ground of fraud. But the alleged successors-in-interest of Ledu Miah, that is the plaintiffs, filed Title Suit No. 2 of 1992 and thus they are barred by the principle of res judicata as they are bound to obey the decisions in the proceedings of their predecessors-in-interest. Since the plaintiffs-opposite parties purchased alleged property during the pendency of the proceedings of their predecessors, thus they will be subjected to the result of the proceedings. In the instant case, since the plaintiffs were not parties in proceedings of their predecessors, so they have no locus standi to bring the suit for declaring the order of the proceedings illegal in which they were not parties. They were bound by the decisions taken by the Revenue courts against their predecessors. So, the suit of the plaintiffs are barred by the principle of res judicata. Moreso, the plaintiffs have also failed to prove title and possession in the suit land.</u>

<u>38. Scanning the evidence on record, it appears that the plaintiffs-opposite parties as pendente lite transferees cannot challenge the impugned judgment dated 24-11-1991 of the Additional Divisional Commissioner when their vendor invoked the jurisdiction and obtained the order. In such case their vendor could prefer appeal before the Board of Land Administration or could file case before the court only on grounds of fraud and collusion but their vendors did take neither of the above courses. Thus, his successors, who have no title and possession in the suit land, cannot challenge the impugned order dated 24-11-1991. Their suit is also hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The suit of the plaintiffs is also hit by section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act as they purchased the alleged suit land during the pendency of the proceedings and the decisions upon the predecessors of the plaintiffs are binding upon the plaintiff. Against such order no suit lies except on the grounds of fraud and collusion but no suit was filed by the predecessor of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs having no title and possession in the suit land have no locus standi to bring the suit against the order or the proceedings in which they were not parties.</u>

39. It appears from the record that plaintiffs filed 12 criminal cases against the contesting defendants-opposite parties immediately after purchasing alleged suit land which clearly indicates that the plaintiffs were aware of proceedings going on in the revenue course. But their contention that they knew about the proceedings only on 23-12-1991 is not correct and thus, they failed to file the suit within stipulated time and, as such, their suit is also barred by limitation.

40. Since the plaintiffs have no locus standi to file the suit which is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and 52 of Transfer of Property Act and since the suit is barred by principle of res judicata and barred by limitation, so the facts and circumstances of the cases referred by the opposite parties in support of their contention are quite distinguishable from those of the present case and, as such, the cited cases are of no assistance to the opposite parties.

41. On the other hand, the contention of the petitioners is that their sale was a complete usufructuary mortgage; that the petitioners Abdul Aziz and Bodiuzzaman transferred the suit land to Bashirullah Bepari who with evil intention transferred the suit land to Ledu Miah alias Lokman Miah subject to condition of re-purchase; that in the deed of Ledu Miah, there was no specific period of re-conveyance, that thereafter the defendants-petitioners began to run after Bashirullah Bepari and Ledu Miah to get back the land by way of reconveyance and finding no other alternative, they filed Miscellaneous Case No. 239/923 of 1973-74 under provisions of President's Order Nos. 88 and 136 of 1972 and No. 24 of 1973; that the opposite party No. 6 Ledu Miah preferred SA petition No. 39 of 1984-85 against the aforesaid order before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Lakshmipur who was eventually pleased to affirm the impugned order dated 25-9-1984; that the opposite party No. 6 Ledu Miah preferred the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 4 of 1984 against the aforesaid order of red-emption dated 25-9-1984 in the court of Upazila Munsif, Raipur which was also dis-missed on 24-6-1986, that opposite party No. 5 Additional Divisional Commissioner, also had affirmed the aforesaid order of redemption by his order passed on 24-11-1991 in Miscellaneous Case No. 104 of 1988.

42. In view of the fact and circumstances of the case discussed above, we are of the view that the suit was not maintainable and the same is also barred by principle of res judicata and that the transaction dated 22-12-1960 was never dead, past and closed before the aforesaid orders of the President's Order came into force being based on misconception of fact and law.

43. Turning to the judgment of reversal as passed by the learned District Judge, Lakshmipur, we are of the view that he has failed to grasp the facts of the case and the law bearing with it. He totally failed to assess and evaluate the facts as well as the evidence on record which led him to reverse the findings of the learned trial Court.

44. In the facts of the case, we have no hesitation to find that the appellate Court wrongly applied his judicial mind and illegally dismissed the appeal assigning no good reason. We thus, find illegality and material irregularity in this impugned judgment and decree dated 14-11-2000 occasioning failure of justice to justify interference by this court exercising revisional jurisdiction under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure in this revision.

45. We find merit in the Rule.

46. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost and the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-11-2000 passed in Title Appeal No. 117 of 1996 by the learned District Judge, Lakshmipur allowing the appeal and setting aside the judgment and decree dated 31-8-1996 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, First Court, Lakshmipur dismissing the suit and setting aside the order of redemption dated 24-11-1991 passed by the learned Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong is set aside.

47. The order of redemption dated 24-11-1991 passed by the learned Additional Divisional Commissioner, Chittagong Division, Chittagong is affirmed.

Send down the LCR at once.

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the impugned judgment and decree dated 26-10-2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge 1st Court, No. 2 Bagerhat in Title Appeal No. 13 of 1999 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 17-1-1999 passed by the learned Assist ant Judge, Chitalmari, Bagerhat in Title Suit No. 217 of 1985 dismissing the suit.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule are that the suit land belonged to defendant Nos. 6 and 7 who sold the suit land by a Kabala dated 16-11-1959 in favour of plaintiff. The plaintiff executed and registered an Ekrarnama on that date that is on 16-11-1959, admitting that he would reconvery the said land in favour of the defendant Nos. 6 and 7 if they refunded back the Kabala money within 10 years. For the mistake of the deed writer the name of mouza of the transferred land was wrongly written as Chitalmari in place of Aruabarni. Ultimately, that money was not returned to the plaintiff within the stipulated period. After expiry of the stipulated period the plaintiff got his name mutated and paid rent. The defendant Nos. 6-7 gave up their claim which accrued to them on the basis of agreement dated 16-11-1959 and there accrued absolute title in the suit land in favour of the plaintiff. Long after expiry of the stipulated period the defendant Nos. 1-4 filed a Miscellaneous Case being No. 50/1982-83 before the concerned CO (Revenue) and got an ex parte order on 14-11-82 allowing redemption of mortgage on the strength of the agreement dated 16-11-1959. The plaintiff filed a review petition before the concerned CO (Revenue) and that was allowed. The Miscellaneous Case No. 50/82-83 was restored for hearing. Thereafter the CO (Revenue) by order dated 16-8-1983 allowed the Miscellaneous Case and allowed the prayer for redemption of the suit land. That order was void, illegal, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff. The plaintiff has been in possession in the suit land through Bargadar. The defendant Nos. 1-4 threatened the plaintiff with dispossession on 28-8-83 on the strength of the order in question dated 16-8-83 passed by the CO (Revenue) and, as such, the suit.

3. The defendants Nos. 1-4 contested the suit by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that admittedly the suit land belonged to defendant Nos. 6/7 who sold by a Kabala dated 16-11-59 in favour of the plaintiff on condition that if the defendants refund money to the plaintiff within 10 years, the latter would reconvey the suit land in favour of the former. It was the further case of the defendants Nos. 6-7 that they sold out 1.4350 acres of land by 2(two) Kabala deeds and out of the sale proceeds the suit land was redeemed. Thereafter, the defendant Nos. 6/7 started possessing the suit land. The defendant claimed back the Kabala dated 16-11-1959 but in reply the plaintiff gave out that the said Kabala was lost. The plaintiff claimed title in the suit land on 13-10-1982 and, as such, the defendants were constrained to file Miscellaneous Case No. 50/82-83 under section 95(Ka) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The order passed in the said Miscellaneous case was a valid order. The plaintiff had no title and possession in the suit land.

4. Both the parties adduced evidence. The plaintiff examined 4 PWs and the defend-ant examined 3 DWs. The plaintiff's documents were marked as Exhibit 1, 1(ka), 2, 3, 4, 4(ka) and the defendants' documents were marked as Exhibits Ka, Kha, Ga, Gha, Uma, Uma(1)-Uma(4), Cha, Cha(1) and Chha.

5. The learned Assistant Judge-in-charge Chitalmari by the judgment and order dated 17-1-1999 dismissed the suit against which the plaintiff took Title Appeal No. 13 of 1999. That appeal was heard by the learned Joint District Judge, Court No. 2, Bagerhat who dismissed the appeal by the impugned judgment and decree dated 26-10-2002. The petitioner being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree has obtained the instant Rule.

6. Mr Md Abdul Jabbar, the learned Advocate on appearing for the petitioner, submitted that the defendants having had filed to get the suit land redeemed within 10 years from 16-11-59 the transaction was a passed and closed transaction and the CO (Revenue) had no jurisdiction to entertain any proceeding under the President's Order No. 88 of 1972 for redemption of mortgage. He submitted that the orders dated 14-11-1982 and 16-8-1983 passed by (the concerned CO (Revenue), the defendant No. 5, were illegal, void, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff. He further submitted that both the Courts below upon misconception of law and fact have dismissed the suit. He further submitted that the plaintiff proved his continuous and uninterrupted possession in the suit land and the suit was liable to be decreed.

7. Mr Sadananda Rana, the learned Advocate, on the other hand, submitted the following points of argument to protect the impugned judgment and decree:

(a)	The land was redeemed earlier by defendant Nos. 6 and 7 on payment of the Kabala price but the said redemption having had not taken place by written instrument and the plaintiff having had claimed title in the suit land the defendants Nos. 1-4 were constrained to file Miscellaneous Case No. 50/82-83.

(b)	The transaction does not come within the doctrine of passed and closed transaction.

(c)	The plaintiff having failed to prove possession in the suit land was not entitled to get decree in the suit.

(d)	The judgment and decree impugned in the Rule being based on concurrent finding of facts are not liable to be disturbed in revision.

8. Mr Rana relied upon the following case laws in support of his submission [34 DLR (AD) 237; 5 BLT (AD) 38; 49 DLR 319, 15 BLT (AD) 106.]

9. In view of the pleadings of the parties, the following issues are required to be decided:

(i)Whether the transaction was a passed and closed transaction within the meaning of President's Order 88 of 1972 and whether the CO (Revenue), Chitalmari had any authority to entertain any proceeding under the said PO for redemption of mortgage.

(ii) Whether the orders dated 14-11-1982 and 16-8-1983 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 50/82-83 were valid in law.

10. The matter in issue having been based upon absolute law point let us investigate into the terms and conditions as contained in the Kabala deed dated 16-11-1959 and as well as the deed of agreement of the same date effected between the parties.

11. The certified copy of the Kabala deed dated 16-11-1959 was filed by the defendant. On perusal of the recitals of the said Kabala, it shows that initially the defendant Nos. 6/7 intended to transfer the suit land by an out and out sale deed. The contents whereof runs thus:

"কষ্য বিক্রি খোষ কবলা পত্র মিদং কয্যাঙ্গাগে আমাদের নানা কারণে নগদ টাকা অবান্যক হওয়ায় আমাদের ভোগদখলীয় নিম্ন তফসিল বর্ণিত জমি আমরা বিক্রয় করার প্রস্তাব করায় গ্রাহকগণ মধ্যে সর্ব্ব উচ্চ পোন দিয়া খরিদ করিতে ইচ্ছুক হওয়ায় আমি সর্বত্র যাচাই করে আপনার নিকট হইতে সং ৬৫০টাকা পোনবাহার গ্রহণে অত্র বিক্রয় খোশ কোবলা লিখিয়া দিয়া স্বীকার ও অঙ্গিকার করিতেছি যে বিক্রিত জমি জমাতে আমাদের যে কোন সত্ব সামিত্য দখল অধিকার যাহা কিছু দিল বা আছে তাহা অদ্য হইতে বিলুপ্ত হইয়া আপনার কোষবরিদা স্বত্বে বালিত। আপনি মালেক সেরেস্তারা আমাদের নাম খরিদ দিয়া আপনার স্বীয় নাম পত্তন পূর্বক দান বিক্রয় যদইচ্ছা ব্যবহারে পুত্র পৌত্তাদিক্রমে পরম সুখে ভোগ দখল করিতে বহেন। কবলার লিখিত জমি জমা নির্দয় মুক্ত অবস্থায় থাকায় আপনার নিকট বিক্রয় করিলাম। যদি ভবিষ্যতে কোন প্রকার তক্তকতা প্রকাশ হইয়া আপনার স্বত্ব দখলের বিঘ্ন বাধা হয় তাহা হইলে আইনতঃ দায়ী ও দন্ডনীয় হইব ও ক্ষতিপূরণ দিতে বাধ্য থাকিলাম। এই নিয়মে সরল মনে কবলার লিখিত পনের টাকার মধ্যে পূর্বের বায়না স্বরুপ ২০০ টাকা লইয়াছি বাকী ৪৫০ টাকা নগদ বুঝিয়া পাইয়া অত্র বিক্রি খোষ কবলা লিখিয়া দিলাম। ইতি সন ১৩৬৬/২৯মে কার্তিক ইং ১৬-১১-১৯৫৯।"

12. The said Kabala was followed by a registered deed of agreement dated 16-11-1959 executed by the plaintiff in favour of defendant Nos. 6/7 in respect of the suit land The said Ekrarnama was admitted into evidence as Exhibit "Gha". The recital of the said Exhibit "Gha" runs thus:

"কষ্য ১০ বৎসর মেয়াদী একবার নামা পত্র মিদং আমি আপনাদের নিকট হইতে নিম্ন চৌহাদ্দি মুক্ত জমি ৬৫০ টাকা কবলায় খরিদ করিয়াছি। তাহাতে একবার দিতেছি যে উক্ত টাকা ১৩৬৭ সাল হইতে ১৩৭৬ সালের মধ্যে ফসল আন্তে সময় মধ্যে টাকা দিলে তাহা আমি গ্রহণ করিয়া জমির দখল ত্যাগ করিব আপনে টাকা না প্রদানে নাইলে আপনার জমা জমির দখল লইতে পারিবেন না। এতদার্থে সুস্থ্য শরীরে স্বেচ্ছায় এই একবার লিখিয়া দিলাম। ইতি সন ১৩৬৬ সনের ২৯শে আর্শ্বিন ইং ১৬-১১-১৯৫৯।"

13. On plain reading of the Kabala dated 16-11-1959 executed and registered by the defendant Nos. 6/7 in favour of the plaintiff along with the Exhibit "Gha", the Ekrarnama dated 16-11-1959, it shows that the defendant Nos. 6/7 sold out the suit land by Kabala deed out and out in favour of the plaintiff and the plaintiff by executing the Ekrarnama dated 16-11-1959 (Exhibit Gha) agreed to hand over possession of the transferred land in favour of the defendant Nos. 6/7 if they refunded the Kabala money within 10(ten) years from 16-11-1959 or within 1376 BS. On perusal of the contents of Exhibit "Gha" it shows that the plaintiff did not agree upon to recovery of the suit land by a deed of reconveyance. The word reconveyance or ফেরত কোবালা দিবার অঙ্গিকার, is absent in the recitals of the Exhibit Gha. It is only available there that the plaintiff agreed upon to hand over possession of the transferred land in favour of defendant Nos. 6 and 7 if they repaid back the Kabala money. If that Ekrarnama was accepted to be an instrument of an undertaking for reconveyance, the terms contained therein were required to be performed within 15-11-1969.

14. Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was incorporated in the said Act by the President's Order No. 88 of 1972 which runs as follows:

"95A—Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any transfer of a holding or of partition or share thereof, either by way of out and out sale with one agreement to reconvey or where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferor acquires the right to possess and to enjoy the usufruct of such consideration, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provision of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (Second Amendment) Order 1972.

15. To construe a sale deed into a complete usufructuary mortgage it requires that a sale deed must be accompanied by a separate deed of reconveyance within the language of PO 88 of 1972.

16. But on perusal of the Exhibit "Gha" the deed of Ekrarnama dated 16-11-1959 I find that within the 4(four) corners of the Exhibit "Gha" there is nothing mentioned that the plaintiff agreed upon to reconvey the land transferred in his favour by defendant Nos. 6 and 7. The word "reconveyance" having not found avail-able in the Exhibit "Gha" the same if be read together with the Kabala dated 16-11-1959 that did not construe the said Kabala into a deed of mortgage within the meaning of President's Order 88 of 1972.

17. Ekrarnama does not necessarily mean an undertaking to reconvey land it may be for various other purposes. The meaning of a particular "Ekrarnama" has to be drawn from its contents. From the contents of the 'ekrarnama' as quoted above it shows that the plaintiff intended to hand over possession of that transferred land in favour of the defendant Nos. 6 and 7 only in the case of refund of the entire Kabala money within 10 years from 16-11-1959.

18. The President's Order No. 88 of 1972 has come into being on 3-8-1972 by which a Kabala deed out and out if was accompanied with a deed of agreement for reconveyance constituted usufructuary mortgage and by the President's Order the revenue officers were vested with the power to redeem mortgage if any comes within the ambit of President's Order No. 88 of 1972.

19. In the instant case admittedly, the stipulation for refunding back the money was within 10 years from 16-11-1959 that is within the 15th November 1969—when the President's Order No. 88 of 1972 was not enacted and was not in operation.

20. The defendant by filing Miscellaneous Case No. 50/82-83 before the CO (Revenue), Bagerhat claimed, on the one hand, that they had repaid the Kabala money to the plaintiff long ago and got back possession in the suit land but on the other hand, disclosed in the prayer for redemption that considering the period of limitation for 60 years the suit land be redeemed treating the same to be a complete usufructuary mortgage within the meaning of PO 88 of 1972, President's Order No. 136 of 1973 and treating redemption automatically after the expiry of 7(seven) years. The filing of the said case presumes that the Kabala money was not refunded to the plaintiff within November 1969.

<u>21. I have already seen that the Kabala deed dated 16-11-1959 together with the Exhibit "Gha" (ekrarnama dated 16-11-1959) do not constitute any deed of usufructuary mortgage. For argument's sake, if the said Kabala is treated to be a complete usufructuary mortgage but the Kabala money having not been repaid before 16-11-1969 the transaction between the plaintiff and the defendant which arose on 16-11-1959 (after execution and registration of the ekrarnama dated 16-11-1959 (Exhibit "Gha") following the Kabala dated the same) was nothing but a passed and closed transaction. The right accrued in favour of the defendant numbers 6 and 7 for getting back the land was lost and expired after the 15th day of November 1969. The transaction was a dead transaction and no right was open before the defendants to make any prayer for redemption of mortgage under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the defendant No. 5 was not entitled to entertain any application from the defendants. This view finds supports from the case law of Bangladesh vs Abdul Gani reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233 and the case of Abdul Khaleque Surnamat reported in 1 BLC (AD) 90.</u>

22. The case laws referred to by Sadananda Rana reported in 34 DLR (AD) 237, 5 BLT (AD) 38, 49 DLR 319, 15 BLT (AD) 106 have got no manner of application in the instant case.

23. In the case of 34 DLR (AD) 237, the Kabala in question was dated 11-11-1953. The Kabala itself was termed as usufructuary mortgage which was clothed with the term "মেয়াদী নির্দায় কোবালা" Moreover, that Kabala was followed by a deed of agreement for reconveyance. Since the Kabala itself was a "মেয়াদী নির্দায় কোবালা" the defendant instituted a regular suit for redemption of mortgage and it was held that the Kabala being itself a mortgage deed the President's Order No. 88 of 1972 shall not have any effect in that case and the doctrine of transaction past and closed shall not arise. In the instant case, the Kabala itself is Kabala out and out and the agreement which followed the Kabala had expired long before the promulgation of President's Order No. 88 of 1972. So, the instant case comes within the mischief of the doctrine of "transaction past and closed" and there was no scope open before the defendants to file an application for redemption of mortgage under section 95A of the SA and T Act.

24. In the 5 BLT (AD) 38 case, the Kabala sought to be redeemed was of the years 1975 and 1976, that is after promulgation of PO 88 of 1972 and the case of 49 DLR (AD) 319, the Kabala sought to be redeemed was dated 18-3-1981. So, the facts of those cases were quite distinguishable from the fact of the instant case. The case of 15 BLT (AD) 106 was related to the question of possession in a suit for permanent injunction and that case law has got no manner of application in the instant case.

25. From the facts and circumstances and the discussions made above I have no hesitation but to hold—

(i) that the Kabala dated 16-11-1959 executed and registered by the defendant Nos. 6 and 7 followed by the deed of agreement (registered) executed by the plaintiff in favour of defendant Nos. 6 and 7 was not a complete usufructuary mortgage within the meaning of President's Order 88 of 1972.

(ii) For argument's sake, if that be treated to be a complete usufructuary mortgage but the transaction of refund of the Kabala money having had not been made within the stipulated time, that is within 15-11-1969, the same comes within the mischief of the doctrine of "transaction passed and closed."

iii) The CO (Revenue) Chitalmari, Bagerhat, the defendant No. 5, had no jurisdiction to entertain the Miscellaneous Case No. 50.82-83 and the order in question dated 16.3.1983 passed by the defendant No. 5 in the said Miscellaneous Case was a void and illegal order and that was passed without having any lawful authority.

26. Now, let us discuss the question of possession. On perusal of the record, it shows that the RS record was prepared in the name of plaintiff. It further appears that after filing the suit the plaintiff made a prayer for temporary injunction against the defendant and that prayer was allowed. That injunction order was continuing till disposal of the suit. On perusal of the application made under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act by the defendants, it shows that they made a prayer for redemption and for getting delivery of possession. The injunction order granted in favour of plaintiff by the trial Court (by the Assistant Judge) was challenged before the learned District Judge, Bagerhat in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 85 of 1988. By order dated 12-12-88 the parties were directed to maintain status quo. That order of status quo having had been made on the prayer of the plaintiff that tantamounts to injunction. The PW 1 himself deposed in support of possession. He paid rent vide Exhibit I series. The SA record was marked as Exhibit 2. That was recorded in the name of plaintiff as it shows. That certified copy of the SA record was marked as Exhibit 2. The PW 2 Dhirendranath supported the plaintiff's possession. The PW 3, PW 4 corroborated the evidence of possession adduced by the PW 1. The defendants although adduced some evidence in support of their possession but the SA record having had not been prepared in their names and the Kabala deed dated 16-11-59 (Exhibit 3) being not redeemed before 15-11-1969 and they having been restrained by an order of injunction by the trial Court, their evidence of possession did not come to any help to them. In view of the above, I hold that the Courts below were wrong to hold possession in favour of the defendants. That finding is hereby set aside. In view of the above, I hold that the plaintiff being in possession had instituted the Title Suit No. 217 of 1985 and that possession was protected by an order of injunction by the trial Court. This Court initially granted injunction in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner and thereafter by order dated 12-11-2003 directed the parties to maintain status quo on modifying its earlier order.

<u>27. The plaintiffs name having recorded in SA Khatian, the plaintiff having paid rent, the defendants by filing redemption case No. 50/82-83 having made a prayer for getting delivery of possession, the plaintiff having had got order of injunction against the defendants and that order having been modified directing the parties to maintain status quo and the PW 1-PW 4 having had supported the plaintiff's possession in the suit land, the Courts below were not justified to hold possession in favour of the defendants. The finding of possession as found by the Courts below are hereby set aside.</u>

28. On perusal of the appellate Court's judgment it shows that in dismissing the plaintiff's case he relied upon the case law of 49 DLR 319, 32 DLR (AD) 223, 34 DLR (AD) 237. On perusal of those case laws it shows that the learned Joint District Judge without going through the entire case law and failing to consider the contents of agreement (Exhibit "Gha") and upon misconception of the doctrine of "transaction past and closed" had arrived at his decision. The decision of both the Courts below being not lawful, those are reversed and are set aside. The Courts below have committed error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice. I find merit in the Rule.

29. In the result, the Rule is made absolute with cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 26-10-2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge 2nd Court, Bagerhat in Title Appeal No. 13 of 19991 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 17-11-1999 passed by the learned Assistant Judge-in-charge, Chitalmari, Bagerhat in Title Suit No. 217 of 1985 dismissing the suit are hereby set aside. The Title Suit No. 217 of 1985 of the Court of Assistant Judge Chitalmari, Bagerhat is hereby decreed. The order dated 16-8-1983 passed by CO (Revenue), Bagerhat (defendant No. 5) in Miscellaneous Case No. 50/82-83 under President's Order No. 88 of 1972 is hereby declared void, illegal, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff. The order of status quo granted by this Court be vacated. The office is directed to send the lower Court's records at once.

The defendants are restrained permanently from interfering with the peaceful possession of the plaintiff in the suit.

End.

lawyer:
MF Ahmed, Advocate—For the Petitioners. 
Md Ziaul Haque, Advocate—For Opposite Parties.
parties:
Abdur Razzak Khandkar and others ----- Defendant-Appellant-Petitioners
Vs
Maleka Khatun & others ----- Plaintiff-Respondent-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
The Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 17-7-1994 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Narayanganj in Title Appeal No. 76 of 1993 affirming the judgment and decree dated 29-7-1993 passed by Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Narayanganj in Title Suit No. 47 of 1991 should not be set-aside.

2. Briefly, the facts of the case, are that, the opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 47 of 1991 in the 4th Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Narayanganj for redemption of alleged usufructuary mortgage and for recovery of possession of the suit property. Kazi Shamsuddin Ahmed husband of the plaintiff Maleka Khatun was the owner of the suit property who by a registered kabala dated 23-3-1967 mortgage the suit property to Mohammad Asgar Hossain Khandker the predecessor of the defendant and in the same sitting said Mohammad Asgar Hossain Khandker executed registered another agreement for reconveyance of the suit property in favour of Shamsuddin Ahmed provided that if he repaid back the consideration money of Taka 500 to Abdur Awal within two years i.e within month of Chaitra, 1375 BS corresponding to 13-4-1969 the deed should be reconveyed.

3. It has further been alleged that in the meantime, PO 88 of 1972 was promulgated which section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has incorporated by which the sale with separate agreement for re-conveyance became usufrucuary mortgage. The plaintiff alleged that the transaction was a mortgage and lastly requested on 25-4-1991 to get back the suit land but no effect. Hence the suit.

4. The suit was contested by the defendant petitioner by filing written statement denying all the material averment made in the plaint contending inter-alia that the transaction is an out and sale and does not come within the mischief of PO 88 of 1972 as the alleged transfer with agreement for re-conveyance was made dated 23-3-1967 and subsistence of the agreement was for two years only and after expiry of the fixed dated i.e. on 22-3-1969 alleged agreement for sale is to be treated as past and closed transaction so the sale in question became absolute before the promulgation of PO 88 of 1972 and, as such, which cannot be redempt. It has also been arrested that the suit property is non-agricultural property situated within Narayanganj Municipality and so section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not applicable in this case. The defendant 'has strongly asserted that the plaintiff has never offered: to repay the consideration money within agreed period for getting, back the property, so the sale has become absolute and the agreement became past and closed transaction. Thus the suit is liable to be dismissed.

5. The case was heard by the Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Narayanganj who after hearing the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of the case decreed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 29-7-1993.

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree dated 29-7-1993 the defendant-petitioner filed Title Appeal No. 76 of 1993 before the District Judge, Narayanganj. The said appeal was heard by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Narayanganj who after hearing the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as the evidence on record disallowed the appeal and thereby upheld the judgment and decree of the trial court by its judgment and decree dated 17-7-1994.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree of, the courts below the defendant-petitioners filed this revisional application under Section 115 (1) of the code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule.

8. Mr FM Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that both the courts erred in law in not considering the material facts and circumstances of the case. The learned Advocate further submitted that whether a transaction is a sale or mortgage would be decided by the court mainly on the basis of the recital of the main deed not on the basis of the separate agreement signed by the defendant alone but both the courts below decreed the suit without considering the main deed signed by the predecessor of the plaintiff. He further submitted that on perusal of the said deed it is found that the executants sold the land to the defendant by receiving entire consideration money and which is an out and out sale deed not a mortgage deed. The learned Advocate further submitted that usufructuary mortgage only depend on the provision of Section 2 (6) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and by observing the conditions laid down in the said section. In support of his argument he referred the case of Abdul Hafiz Chowdhury vs Somor Ali reported in 4 DLR 126. The learned Advocate further submitted that the usufructuary mortgage is only for agricultural land but the suit land is a homestated situated within the municipal area so it cannot be redempt under Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In support of his argument he referred the case of Shahjahan Mizi vs Md Shamsul Haque Mizi report in 3 BLC 528. The learned Advocate further submitted that without taking loan money question of mortgage is not acceptable and in this case the plaintiff neither mentioned in the plaint that the executants took loan from the defendant nor it is stated in the main deed and, as such, the impugned transaction cannot be a mortgage. The learned Advocate further submitted that the impugned transaction is a past and closed transaction because the agreement was for two years and the period having been expired in the year 1969 and the transaction between the parties undisputedly came to an end before the promulgation of president order No. 88 of 1972 which came into force on 3-8-1972. In support he referred the decision of the case of Asmat Ali vs Abdur Rafique Mridha reported in 52 DLR (AD) 132 and the case of Abu Bakkar vs Nazir Ahmed reported in 34 DLR (AD) 237. Thus, he prayed for making the Rule absolute.

9. On the contrary, Mr Md Ziaul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties submitted that both the courts after considering the evidence on record and the facts and circumstances of the case decreed the suit and the concurrent finding of fact cannot be interfered with in revisional jurisdiction under Section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate further submitted that as per Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy act mortgage should be applicable for all categories of land including holding or house or building. He further submitted that in the instant case it is clear that the petitioner executed a re-conveyance deed on the same sitting through a separate deed which should be treated as complete usufructuary mortgage. In support he reliance the case of Asmat Ali vs Abdur Rafiq Mridha reported in 52 DLR (AD) 132. The learned Advocate further submitted that if the plaintiff succeed to prove that there is an agreement of re-conveyance in such a case the said agreement should be treated as complete usufructuary mortgage and the petitioner can file redemption case within 60 years as per Article 148 of the Limitation Act. The learned Advocate further submitted that on close reading of Sub-Section 16 of Section 2 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, Section 95A of the State Acquisition of Tenancy Act, PO 88 of 1972, PO 137 of 1972 and PO 24 of 1973 the claimed land is to be treated as complete usufructuary mortgage which supported by the decisions reported in 34 DLR (AD) 237, 52 DLR (AD) 132, 36 DLR (AD) 90, 49 DLR 172, and 49 DLR (AD) 71. Thus, he prayed for discharging the Rule.

10. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment, papers and documents as available in the records. The plaintiff case is that the deed dated 23-3-1967 executed by the predecessor of the plaintiff is mortgage deed since on the same sitting another re-conveyance deed was executed by the predecessor of the defendant. Both the courts after considering the evidence on record and the law opined that the same is mortgage deed which should be redempt. It appears that the trial court after considering the decision of the case of Abu Bakkar vs Nazir Ahmed reported in 34 DLR (AD) 2.37 opined that a mortgage is always mortgage which cannot be treated as out and out sale by expanding time except Article 148 of the Limitation Act. In the instant case it is found that there is a re-conveyance deed but defendant claims that after lapse of 2 years which termed as out and out of sale deed. So as per above decision the case of the defendant is not sustainable.

11. Section 58 of the Transfer of Proper Act defines the Mortgage. According to Section 58 of TP Act some conditions should be considered in testifying the case of mortgage. The said conditions elaborately discussed in the case of Abdul Hafiz Chowdhury vs Somor Ali reported in 4 DLR 126.

The said conditions are:—

(i) The existence of a debt,

(ii) The period of repayment a short period being indicative of sale a long period of a mortgage:

(iii) Possession of the property-the continuance of the grantor in possession indicating a mortgage

(iv) Existence or otherwise of a stipulation for payment of interest or reconveyance, a stipulation for interest or re-payment indicating a mortgage

(v) Adequacy or inadequacy of the consideration, a price below the true value indicating mortgage

(vi) Presence or otherwise of the stipulation of conveyance embodied in the deed Prima facie indicating that the transaction is a mortgage; and

(vii) Purchaser of stamps and payment of registration costs, the same if done by the transferee being indicative of a sale.

12. In the case of Shahjahan Mizi vs Md Shamsul Hoque Mizi reported in 3 BLC 528 a single bench of this court opined that the mortgage is applicable only in the case of Agricultural land. But the Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act defines usufructuary mortgage which is reproduced as below: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any transfer of a holding or of portion or share thereof [either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey, [for] where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess, and to enjoy the usufruct of such holding or portion or share thereof for a specified period in lieu of such consideration, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provisions of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Amendment) Order, 1972] (President's Order No. 88 of 1972).

13. This section clearly provides that notwithstanding contained in any other law for the time being in force any transfer of a holding or of portion or share thereof either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to re-conveyance where transferor received from the transferee any consideration. So from the aforesaid section it is clear that section 95A indicates that all the holding is to be treated as usufructuary Mortgage.

14. It appears that the deed was executed on 23-3-1967 and on the same day i.e. on same sitting a separate agreement of reconveyance was executed. As per decision of the case of Asmat Ali vs Abdur Rafique Mridha reported in 52 DLR (AD) 132 it is settled that any transfer with a re-conveyance should be treated as mortgage. Though in the instant case it is found that the said matter was not stated in the deed of transfer but on the same day the another re-conveyance deed was executed and wherein it is clearly stated that if the executants pay the said amount within two years the property will be returned back to the executant.

<u>15. On close reading of the Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act it is clear that the transfer deed executed on 23-3-1967 is a mortgage deed. Though it is found that Section 58 (C) of the TP Act does not mention the same but ultimately Section 95A clearly provides that mortgage is applicable in all the holdings including house or building or any portion or share. So the deed dated 23-3-1967 is a mortgage deed not out and out sale deed. In the case of Abu Bakkar vs Nazir Ahmed reported in 34 DLR (AD) 237 it is settled that once it is proved mortgage always a mortgage not a past and closed transaction.</u>

16. It appears that the re-conveyance deed provides only two years time but as per PO 88 of 1972 and the decision of our Apex Court the Plaintiff can prayed for redemption within the time prescribed in Article 148 of the Limitation Act i.e. within the time prescribed in Article 148 of the Limitation Act i.e. within 60 years. In the case of Asmat Ali vs Abdur Rafique Mridha reported in 52 DLR (AD) 132 wherein their lordships held "the learned Single Judge failed to consider that the filing of a suit for redemption of mortgage in a civil Court is wholly different from filing of an application under President's Order 88 of 1972 before the Revenue Authority. The Court also held that President's Order No. 88 of 1972 created special forum for restoration of mortgaged property. But it did not take away right of redemption available to a mortgagor by filing a mortgage suit under Order 34 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In that view of the matter High Court Division was totally wrong to hold that the suit was not maintainable as the transaction was past and closed." Considering the above decision it is my view that the suit is quite maintainable and the transaction is not past and closed transaction.

17. It also appears that both the courts concurrently found that the plaintiff case is maintainable and the transfer is a mortgage. The concurrent finding of fact cannot be interfered with in revisional jurisdiction. This proposition supported by the decision of the case of Ganaprojatantri Bangladesh Sarker represented by the DC, Bakerganj vs Joinal Abedin Dewan reported in / BLC (AD) 26 wherein their lordships held "High Court Division cannot interfere with the concurrent finding of facts without finding upon consideration of evidence that the plaintiff's case was proved and/or that the Courts below committed illegality in finding against the plaintiff resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice."

18. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the discussions above I do not deserve any interference with the findings of the courts below.

19. In the result, the Rule is discharged. However, without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and decree dated 17-7-1994 passed by the Subordinate Judge, (Now Joint District Judge), 1st Court, Narayanganj in Title Appeal No. 76 of 1993 disallowed the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 29-7-1993 passed by Senior Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 47 of 1991 are hereby upheld.

Send down the lower Court's records at once.

End.

lawyer:
MR Hasan, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 
Md Mozibur Rahman Miah, Advocate—For the Respondent No. 2.
parties:
City Bank Ltd ------ Petitioner 
vs
Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: This Rule called in question the legality of the ex parte judgment and decree dated 3-10-2004 (preliminary decree signed on 13-10-2004) as contained in "Annexure-D and D-1" to the writ petition passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka in Artha Rin Suit No. 470 of 2004.

2. Material fact relevant for disposal of this Rule is that the petitioner is a Public Company Ltd by shares and is engaged in the business of banking as per law of the land having its registered office at 10, Dilkusha C/A (Jiban Bima Tower), Dhaka. The petitioner-City Bank Ltd has been doing banking business by its various branches throughout the country. Respondent No. 2, Agrani Bank as a plaintiff instituted the Artha Rin Suit No. 470 of 2004 in the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as "the Adalat") (respondent No. 1) for recovery of loan amounting to Taka 46,26,59,843 impleading the petitioner as defendant No. 7. The defendants did not turn to contest the suit and ultimately, the suit was decreed ex parte by the Adalat against the defendants vide ex parte judgment and decree dated 3-10-2004 (preliminary) decree signed on 13-10-2004).

3. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid ex parte judgment and decree dated 3-10-2004 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, No. 1, Dhaka (respondent No. 1) the petitioner City Bank Ltd approached this Court and obtained the present Rule.

4. Respondent No. 2, Agrani Bank entered appearance and contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition controverting the material allegations of the writ petition contending, inter alia, that the instant writ petition under Article 102 of the Constitution challenging the ex parte judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka in Artha Rin Suit No. 470 of 2004 is misconceived, incompetent and not maintainable.

5. Mr MR Hasan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, in the course of argument, has taken us through the writ petition, supplementary affidavits, plaint of the Artha Rin Suit No. 470 of 2004 and other materials on record including the impugned ex parte judgment and decree dated 3-10-2004 and thereafter he criticised the impugned ex parte judgment and decree dated 3-10-2004 on various grounds.

6. Firstly, Mr Hasan submits that the learned Judge of the Adalat, under misconception of law and facts, most illegally without applying judicial mind passed the impugned ex parte decree against the petitioner City Bank Ltd in a sweeping manner which is not only illegal but also cryptic in nature and, as such, the same is liable to be struck down.

7. Secondly, he submits that no loan having been granted in favour of the petitioner City Bank Ltd as admitted in the plaint of Artha Rin Suit No. 470 of 2004 and the City Bank Ltd (petitioner) not being a guarantor or mortgagor of the loan for recovery of which the Artha Rin Suit No. 470 of 2004 was filed, the Adalat (respondent No. 1) acted without jurisdiction under section 5(1) of the Ain, 2003 in proceeding against the petitioner-bank and in passing the impugned ex parte judgment and decree against the writ petitioner-bank and, as such, the impugned ex parte decree, so far it relates to the petitioner-bank, is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

8. Thirdly, he submits that admittedly the petitioner was not a party to the tripartite agreement, hence it had no knowledge of the said agreement which is not registered nor the said agreement is binding on the petitioner. Respondent No. 2, Agrani Bank did not claim to have sent CIB report to Bangladesh Bank, vide their plaint nor the question of procuring CIB report was an issue before the trial Court in the suit filed by respondent No. 2 (plaintiff-bank).  This is a matter between the lender bank and Bangladesh Bank. The loan being admitted and secured by mortgage, the petitioner is a secured lender but the respondent No. 2 bank has included the mortgaged property in its plaint in violation of section 8(2) (kha) of the Ain.

9. Fourthly, he submits that the respondent No. 2, plaintiff-bank, having no right to file a suit for foreclosure as permitted by section 67 of the TP Act, the Artho Rin Adalat has exercised a jurisdiction not vested in it in passing the decree in preliminary form and against the writ petitioner in exercising of jurisdiction under section 5(2) and 5(3) and section 6(5) of the Ain, 2003, hence the impugned order and decree are without lawful authority.

10. Fifthly, the learned Advocate submits that the respondent No. 2, plaintiff-bank is not legally entitled to take advantage of its own inaction for not mortgaging the subject landed property or in not taking action for alleged breach of unregistered tripartite agreement that is neither a mortgage nor creates any charge on the said property as per sections 58, 59 or 100 of the Transfer of Property Act 1882.

11. Sixthly, the learned Advocate submits that the respondent No. 2, plaintiff bank has acted illegally, unauthorisedly and in violation of section 8(2)(kha) of the Ain 2003 by including a schedule of properties in the plaint of Artha Rin Suit No. 470 of 2004 and thereby obtained the impugned judgment and decree by misleading the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat which amounts to malice in law, hence the impugned ex parte judgment and decree are liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect to the extent the decree has been passed treating the scheduled property as property mortgaged in favour of the respondent No. 2, plaintiff-bank and, as such, the impugned order and the decree are liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.

12. Finally, MR Hasan contends that the petitioner-Bank as a financial institution has been doing banking business throughout the country with name and frame but in spite of that the Adalat (respondent No. 1) without notifying the petitioner-Bank decreed the suit ex parte against the petitioner-Bank and others vide ex parte judgment and decree dated 3-10-2004 (decree signed on 13-10-2004) and, as such, at any rate the ex parte judgment and decree should be liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.

13. On the other hand, Mr Md Mozibur Rahman Miah, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent-Bank, by filing an affidavit-in-opposition opposes the Rule. He submits that the petitioner-Bank with an ill motive as well as having got prior knowledge of the liabilities of the respondent No. 3, Mainamoti Textile Mills Ltd towards this respondent-Bank (plaintiff-bank) motively sanctioned fresh loan in neither obtaining any clearance from the plaintiff-bank (respondent No. 2) nor bother to procuring any CIB report from Bangladesh Bank knowing very well those requirements as condition-precedent in granting fresh loan above Taka 10 lac to any borrower-company and, as such, granting such fresh loan as well as mortgaging of the schedule property is ex facie illegal from its very beginning and thereby it has ceased to create any legal authority over the schedule property by the petitioner-Bank.

14. Mr Mozibur Rahman, next after placing the affidavit-in-opposition straight forward submits that the instant writ petition challenging the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat (respondent No. 1) in Artha Rin Suit No. 470 of 2004 is misconceived, ill-motivated and not maintainable since there is express provision of law as laid down in section 41 of the Ain, 2003 for filing appeal against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat. Mr Mozibur Rahman in support of his submission relied on the decisions reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, 54 DLR (AD) 6, 59 DLR (AD) 6 and 13 BLC 391.

15. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition, supplementary affidavits dated 13-4-2004 and 9-6-2008 filed by the petitioner-Bank and other materials on record including the ex parte judgment and decree dated 3-10-2004 (decree signed on 13-10-2004).

16. To appreciate the points raised by the respective parties before us it would be convenient for us to decide first of all the question of maintainability of the writ petition preferred by the petitioner City Bank Ltd Admittedly, the respondent No. 2, Agrani Bank as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 470 of 2004 impleading the Mainamoti Textile Mills Ltd and other defendants including the petitioner-Bank as defendant No. 7 for recovery of Taka 46,26,59,843. The Adalat decreed the suit ex parte by its ex parte judgment and decree dated 3-10-2004 (decree signed on 13-10-2004) against the defendants including the defendant-petitioner-Bank.

17. In the case of Zahirul Islam vs National Bank Limited reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, where it has been decided as follows:

"The petitioner, without filing any appeal, filed an application under Article 102 of the Constitution, namely, Writ Petition No. 892 of 1991 which was dismissed summarily by a Division Bench of the High Court Division on 30-6-1991 on the ground that the petitioner has an alternative and efficacious remedy by way of appeal.........The petition is dismissed."

18. In the case of Gazi M Towfic vs Agrani Bank reported in 54 DLR (AD) 6, where the principle has been laid down in the following terms:

"The law is now settled that since specific provision for appeal has been made against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat no application under Article 102 lies against such judgment and decree."

19. In the case of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) vs Artha Rin Adalat reported in 59 DLR (AD) 6, it has been laid down in the following terms:

"In view of the decisions quoted above we are led to irresistible conclusion that there being specific remedy in the statute for filing appeal against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat in the present case the defendant not availing of the aforesaid remedy cannot maintain the writ petition."

<u>20. Ongoing through the above quoted uniform decisions of our Apex Court, we find a clear view of the law as it stands today that an application under Article 102 of the Constitution does not lie against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat since there being specific provision in the statute for filing appeal against the judgment and decree whether ex parte or on contest passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. Therefore, we find no other way but to hold that the instant writ petition is not maintainable.</u>

21. Mr MR Hasan, the learned Advocate, tried his best to convince us that when a writ petition is filed raising purely a question of law or jurisdiction of the Court/Adalat or interpretation of a statute, availability of an alternative remedy will not stand and, in that view of the matter, the present writ petition is well maintained, inasmuch admittedly the petitioner-Bank is neither a borrower nor a guarantor nor a mortgagor in respect of loan in question.
