The simple reason for putting such condition-precedent can be gathered from the provisions of section 3(3)(খ) of the EPO and the objectives detailed in section 3(1) of the EPO, namely the (a) security, (b) safeguard of interest, (c) maintenance of law and order, (d) economic life, (e) supply and availability of essential commodities and (f) the service to be given to the nation and the public, as a whole, and so that no abuse or misuse of the authority can be made except with malafide and bad motive. The "offence" referred to in Rule 19ঞ(4) must not only be of "public importance" but should also affect or be related to the objectives mentioned in section 3(1) of EPO.

47. In the Affidavit-in-Opposition also the respondent has categorically stated that the sanction has been given on consideration of the "status of the accused" and the "status of the accused" increased the gravity of the offence. In the instant case, thus it is clear, that the sanction as given is not on the basis of "gravity of the offence" having regard to the nature of the "public importance" thereon, but has been given on consideration of the "status of the accused", and therefore, there was misapplication of mind on the part of the sanctioning authority in giving the impugned sanction. The impugned sanction has not been given in accordance with law, since the condition precedent has not been fulfilled. Therefore, initiation and continuation of any case pursuant to the impugned sanction is without lawful authority.

48. Both the learned Advocates appearing for the writ petitioner, as well as the Amici Curiae, referring to the format of the oath taken by the Judges of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, pointed out that neither in India nor in Pakistan, the word 'defend' is found in the format of the oath taken by their Judges, thereby our Constitution has added "extra duty and obligation" on the Judges of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh to "defend" the Constitution in addition to the duty to "preserve and protect" the Constitution. This has cast upon the Judges of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh an additional duty to "read and apply" the provisions of the Constitution strictly, when right of a citizen is being infringed.

49. Mr Tawfique Nawaz, the learned Advocate, referred to the portion of the Code of Conduct framed by our Supreme Judicial Counsel, which is quoted herein: "the function of interpretation and applications of the Constitution and the law is to be discharged by all the Judges of the Supreme Court for the maintenance of the Rule of Law over the whole range of human activities within the nation."

50. Considering the preamble of the Constitution as well as the provisions of Article 26 thereof and the contents of the oath prescribed for the Judges of the Supreme Court, we find substance in the submissions of the learned Advocate Mr TH Khan that no law or rule or any provision can be made during the Emergency curbing or curtailing the authority and power of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, subject to the restrictions imposed by the Articles 141B and 141C, and that during Emergency period no law or rule can be framed inconsistent with provisions of Articles 27 to 35 and as well as any existing law and the orders passed by the Judges of the Supreme Court should demonstrate that justice is done without fear or favour.

<u>51. The provisions negating the authority of the Court to grant bail under Rules 19ঘ, 11 and 15ঘ of the EPR, being inconsistent with the provisions of Articles 31, 32, 33 and 35 of the Constitution as well as sections 426, 496, 497 and 498 of CrPC, are void and the power and authority of the Court under sections 426, 496, 497 and 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure relating to granting of bail has not been affected or infringed by said Rules 19ঘ, 10(2), 11 and 15ঘ of the EPR. Further, no penalty or sentence can be imposed by any Rule of the EPR, framed under the authority of EPO. Since the Rules 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 154 of the Rules, 2007 are inconsistent with the existing law as well as the provisions of Articles 27 to 35 of the Constitution, said Rules to the extent of the inconsistency for containing the provisions of penalty and sentence are void as per Article 26(2) of the Constitution.</u>

<u>52. Since in the Rule the impugned sanction is under challenge and we have found that the impugned sanction has been given without lawful authority, for non-fulfillment of the condition-precedent set out in Rule 19ঞ (4) and the alleged offence having been committed prior to the promulgation of Emergency, the instant case initiated under the Emergency Power Rules, 2007 is illegal, without lawful authority and cannot be proceeded with further.</u>

<u>In fine, it is held that:</u>

<u>(a) any case arising out of an offence committed prior to the date of promulgation of the Emergency i.e. 11-1-2007, cannot be tried under the Emergency Power Rules, 2007;</u>

<u>(b) existing rules framed under the Emergency Power Ordinance, 2007 are not retrospective in view of the objectives detailed in section 3(1) of the said Ordinance, 2007; Emergency Power Rules, 2007 is prospective;</u>

<u>(c) for the purpose of granting sanction, consideration should be given to the importance of the "offence committed" and not the status or importance of the accused, and that such offence must affect or be related to the objectives detailed in section 3(1) of the Emergency Power Ordinance, 2007;</u>

<u>(d) Rules framed under a Statute being sub-legislation, the same cannot curb or infringe a right or benefit given by a Statute, hence the penal provisions as well as the provisions, curbing the right to bail, as contained in the Emergency Power Rules, 2007, are void and not enforceable;</u>

<u>(e) Emergency has not curtailed the power and authority of any Court; and the Court retained its power and authority to deal with the bail and other matters in accordance with the existing laws in force;</u>

<u>(f) Gulshan Police Station Case No. 34 dated 13-6-2007 cannot be proceeded under the Emergency Power Rules, 2007, pursuant to the impugned sanction dated 16-7-2007.</u>

53. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned sanction given by the respondent No. 2 under Rule 19ঞ (2) of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007, vide Memo No. স্বঃমঃ(আইন-১)/জক্ষবি-১/০৭/(অংশ-৫)/৭১২ dated 16-7-2007, for proceeding with the Gulshan Police Station Case No. 34 dated 13-6-2007 filed under sections 385/109 of the Penal Code, 1860, under the Emergency Power Rules, 2007 treating the offence to be of public importance, evidenced by the Annexure-C to the Writ petition, is declared to be without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and consequently, any action taken and or initiation and continuation of any proceeding and or trial of any case, arising out of said Gulshan Police Station Case No. 34 dated 13-6-2007, under the Emergency Power Rules, 2007, in any Court of law or authority, is declared to be without lawful authority, and stands quashed.

We are grateful to (1) Mr. TH Khan, (2) Mr Abdur Rab Chaudhury, (3) Mr Mahbubur Rahman (4) Mr Mahbubey Alam, (5) Mr Md Rafiqul Islam Miah, and (6) Mr Md Munsurul Hoque Chowdhury, the learned Advocates, for their experienced and learned opinion and the assistance given on our request, which helped us in arriving at our decision.

End.

full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J : This rule under section 14 read with section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay 4,614 days in preferring revisional application against judgment and decree dated 10-6-1998 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Mymensingh dismissing Title Appeal No. 233 of 1995 affirming those dated 25-6-1995 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, lswargonj, Mymensingh decreeing Title Suit No. 33 of 1992.

2. It is stated in the application for condonation of aforesaid long 4,614 days delay that against judgment and decree passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Iswargonj, Mymensingh petitioner filed, Title Appeal No. 233 of 1995 before the learned District Judge, Mymensingh which was transferred to the court of Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Court, at present Joint District Judge, Mymensingh and was heard and the appeal was dismissed by the judgment dated 1-61998 Petitioner on the wrong advice of the learned Advocate of Mymensingh Bar, filed review petition being review Case No. 19 of 1998 for reviewing the judgment and decree dated 1-64998 passed in the appeal. The review petition was allowed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge by order dated 22-9-1999. The learned Judge ordered, for hearing of the appeal afresh and after hearing of the appeal afresh, learned judge by the judgment dated 24-4-2000 allowed the appeal and set-aside the judgment. Against which plaintiff having aggrieved, moved this Court in Civil Religion No. 3570 of 2000. A Single Judge of the Hon'ble High Court Division made the rule absolute, set-aside the judgment and decree of the court of appeal below and restored those of the trial court by judgment and order dated 28-7-2998. Petitioner against the judgment of the Honible high Court Division dated 28-7-2008 passed in Civil Revision No. 3570 of 2000 moved the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for leave to appeal being Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 383 of 2009 on the wrong advice of the learned Advocate. The said Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal was dismissed on 6-10-2010. Thereafter, the petitioner engaged the present learned Advocate and whose advice filed this revision against the judgment and order passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge passed in Tittle Appeal No. 233 of 1995.

3. Mr Manoj Chandra Bhadury, learned Advocate, appearing for the defendant-appellant-petitioner, on reference to the judgment of the Appellate Division passed in the case of Kohinoor Chowdhury vs Sree Kamada Ranjan Bhattacharja, 20 BLT (AD) 47 submits that, this Court in on the chronological happenings of the case have jurisdiction to condone the unusual delay happened which find support from reported decision and further submits that since the litigant petitioner moved with ill advice of the learned Advocate proceeding taken after the appeal was dismissed on wrong forum the delay should be condoned.

4. Let us, quote: the relevant portion of the judgment of the Appellate Division reported in 20 BLT. It is held that :-

"As it appears the High Court Division discharged the Rule holding that admittedly the earlier suit was filed within time in a court of competent jurisdiction but since but since wrong relief was sought the suit ended unsuccessfully up to the Appellate Division and the plaintiff proceeded with the earlier suit bonafide with the diligence and in good faith and he under the advice of his layer instead of filing the suit fir specific performance of contract wrongly filed the suit for redemption of the suit land from usufructuary mortgage and that the plaintiff have categorically pleaded in his  plaint that he proceeded with the earlier suit under the wrong advice of his learned Advocate and that though the learned Advocate for the defendant petitioner contended before the High Court Division that since the suit was not filed before a Court of wrong jurisdiction the plaintiff was not entitled to get the benefit Of section 14 of the Limitation Act but the factual position is that the plaintiff filed the suit before a competent court of jurisdiction but prayer wrong relief under the wrong advice of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and it is a settled principle of law that question of limitation is a mixed question Of facts and law and needs to be settled only upon taking evidence and further in terms of the decisions of the superior courts, a litigant should not. Suffer for wrong advice of his learned Lawyer and so the plaintiff is entitled to get benefit of section 14 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay consumed due to wrong advise of his lawyer."

<u>5. Section 5 and 14 of the Limitation Act are for condonation of delay. Condonation means pardon or forgiveness and in too generous over look. It is implicated to give a defaulting party to knock the door of justice if the offence of not Moving the court in time explained satisfactory In condoning the delay is conclusion Of fact, not of law. If a case make out on chronological happenings i.e. on facts which satisfy the Court as to its existence; then Court in its desecration condone the offence i.e. delay in moving the Civil Section14 of Limitation Act applies when a litigant prosecute a proceeding bonafide in wrong forum. Tithe spent in choosing a wrong forum bonafide and  with clue diligence is excluded as per Section 14 of the Limitation Act. It appears that petitioner on the advice of the learned advocate, (in the case of Debabaria Chatterjee vs Md Munsur Ali 36 DLR 136 it is held even senior Advocate can commit mistake) filed review instead of moving High Court Division in revision and this Wrong prosecution continue, either at this instance of the petitioner or at the instance of the opposite-party, up to Appellate Division and although the petitioner was before the Court. The facts revealed shows the petitioner is misled by wrong advice. It is quite clear from the chronological happenings of the case that petitioner Was always prosecuting with due diligence another civil proceeding with the same cause of action. The wording in section 14 of the Limitation act is not only from defect of jurisdiction but also "or other cause of a like nature" The case in hand comes within the later wordings of Section 14 of the Act. All the facts Of the case if taken into a narrow compass than it is seen that petitioner honestly good faith, in due case and attention for relief travel from pillar to post in whatever forum as was advised render the court to apply  provision of section 14 of the Limitation Act.</u>

6. We are view with the delay for preferring revisional application 4,614 days should be condoned.

7. In the result, the rule is made absolute Without any order as to cost.

8. The delay 4,614 days for filing revisional application before this Court is condoned.

9. Office is directed to place the revisional application in appropriate motion bench immediately.

Communicate this order at once.

End.

parties:
Bangladesh Ship Builders Association ------ Petitioner. 
Vs.
Bangladesh & others ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Sheikh Hassan Arif J : Rule was issued challenging the legality of the impugned decision taken in the 17th meeting of ECNEC held on 22-12-2009 for procurement/construction of four Nos. 108-TEUs self propelled multi-purpose container ships by spending Taka 137,79,00,000 engaging Khulna Shipyard and Chittagong Dry Dock without inviting any Tender.

2. Short facts, relevant for the disposal of the Rule, are that the petitioner Bangladesh Ship Builders Association is an Association of ship builders in Bangladesh and the Association is registered with the joint stock companies and firms. The members of the Association are engaged in ship-building, and some of them have already acquired high reputation by exporting ships constructed/built by them. The Government having taken decision to procure four 108-TEUs multi-purpose container vessels (hereinafter called the said vessels), it obtained report from BUET through project evaluation committee which in its meeting held on 29-6-2009 decided amongst others, to float tender in this regard. Subsequently, on 22-12-2009, in a meeting of the Executive Committee for National Economic Council (ECNEC), the project for procuring the said vessels has been approved and the procurement cost has been determined as Taka 137,79,00,000. However, in the said meeting the ECNEC took the impugned decision for procuring the said vessels directly from Khulna Shipyards and Chittagong Dry Dock, two government owned ship builders, without any tender, and respondent No. 11 has communicated the same to the concerned authorities vide letter dated 11-1-2010. Being aggrieved by this, the petitioner association moved this Court and obtained the Rule. The Rule is contested by respondent No. 1, 3, 5, 10 & 11, however, respondent No. 10 and II have filed separate affidavit-in-opposition, although the contentions of the contesting respondents are almost same.

3. Mr Nakib Saiful Islam, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the provisions of Public Procurement Act 2006 ("the said Act") and the Rules framed thereunder, namely Public Procurement Rules, 2008, made it mandatory for the government procurement authorities of Bangladesh to do procurements through open public tender except in few cases specifically provided by the said Act. He submits that only under situations mentioned in section 32 and section 68 of the said Act, the procurement authority can deviate from the mandatory procurement by open tender. However, he submits, the impugned decision to procure the said container vessels directly from Khulna Shipyards and Chittagong Dry Dock grossly violated the said mandatory provisions as the decision does not come under the categories of exceptions as provided by section 32 and section 68.

4. Mr Md Mujibur Rahman Miah, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for respondent Nos. 1, 3, and 11 submits that the petitioner association being not a person aggrieved as provided under Article 102 of the constitution it does not have locus stand to move this writ petition against the impugned decision in a representative capacity. In this regard he refers to some decisions of this Court, namely Dada Match Workers Union vs Bangladesh reported in 29 DLR 188, Bangladesh Shangbadpatra Parishad vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 43 DLR (AD) 126 and Bangladesh Electrical Association vs Bangladesh reported in 46 DLR 221, and mainly relies on Sangbadpatra Parishad case. He further submits that the impugned decision is a policy decision of the government and, as such, the same is not amendable to writ jurisdiction as held by our apex Court in Prof A Rahim vs Ministry of Industries reported in 7 BLT (AD) 313. Mr Azmalul Hossain QC, the learned Senior Counsel representing respondent No. 10, submits that the project will economically benefit the country as it is evident from the discussion in the impugned decision and, as such, ECNEC can avoid tender procedure for greater public interest and the interest of the country. He submits that for public interest and greater interest of the country, the government has the right to negotiate with any individual for procurement and in this regard he refers to an Indian Supreme Court decision, namely Kasturi Lal Lakshmi Reddy vs State of Jammu and Kashmir reported in AIR 1980 SC 1992. The learned Advocates for respondents further submits that the impugned decision comes under the exception provided in section 32 (1)(খ)(উ) and, as such, the decision in no way has violated the provisions of the said Act. In reply to objections as regard standing of the petitioner, Mr Nakib Saiful Islam refers to the landmark case of our apex Court in Dr Mohiuddin Farooque vs Bangladesh reported in 17 BLD (AD) 1 = 49 DLR (AD) 1 and submits that after this decision our Appellate Division has expanded the concept of locus stand and came out of the traditional rigid view of "person aggrieved". He submits that the petitioner association being a registered association of its members under Company Act, it has sufficient interest to move this writ petition for and on behalf of its members against a gross default or abuse by the executives.

5. Perused the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition and papers as annexed thereto and considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates. Since the question of Locus standi has been seriously raised by the learned Deputy Attorney General, we need to address the same first although this issue has by this time settled by our apex Court in Dr Mohiuddin Farooque's case as cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. In Dr Mohiuddin Farooque's case the case of Sangbadpatra Parishad has been considered and our Appellate Division moved forward leaving behind the traditional view of "person aggrieved" as formulated in the Sangbadpatra Parishad case and held that persons with sufficient interest, not being a busy body, should be entitled to have audience under writ jurisdiction challenging the illegality committed by the State and its machineries. His Lordships Justice Mostafa Kamal, while delivering the main judgment, observed that the Sangbadpatra Parishad case was not an authority even for the proposition that an association could never be a person aggrieved if it espoused the causes of its members in a representative capacity. His Lordship made the point with the following observation (at page 18)

"With the power of the people looming large behind the constitutional horizon it is difficult to conceive of Article 102 as a vehicle or mechanism for realizing exclusively individual rights upon individual complaints. The Supreme Court being a vehicle, a medium or mechanism devised by the Constitution for the exercise of the judicial power of the people on behalf of the people, the people will always remain the focal point of concern of the Supreme Court while disposing of justice or propounding any judicial theory or interpreting any provision of the Constitution. Viewed in this context interpreting the words any person aggrieved" meaning only and exclusively individuals and excluding the consideration of people as a collective and consolidated personality will be a stand taken against the Constitution."

<u>6. Apart from above, in some other cases also this Court has allowed locus standi to the persons having sufficient interests. As for example, in Bangladesh Retired Government Employees Welfare Association vs Bangladesh reported in 46 DLR 426, the High Court Division has allowed locus stands to an Association of retired government employees to espouse the causes of its members. Although the decision has been over ruled by the Appellate Division on a different point [51 DLR (AD) 1211, the petitioner-association's locusstandi as allowed by the High Court Division was not interfered with. Resonating the words of Justice Naimuddin Ahmed in the above mentioned Retired Government Employees Case [46 DLR 426], we like to hold that the Constitution of our country is not a morbid document but a dynamic instrument capable of being interpreted and applied in the ever-changing socioeconomic context of society. Therefore, to make it dynamic in the practical sense, the pedantic and lexicographic interpretation of the words "person aggrieved" should, as far as possible be avoided if it can be done without causing repugnancy to a specific provision of the Constitution. In the instant case, we also do not think that by expanding the meaning of the words "person aggrieved" we are causing any repugnancy to any provision of the Constitution. Considering the above reported cases and the fact that the petitioner association is a registered association under the Companies Act espousing the cause of its members, we do not find any reason to disallow it right to audience under writ jurisdiction for challenging the impugned decision as the impugned decision directly affected the interests and rights of its members to participate in the open tender. Furthermore, just because the names of one or two of its members have not been mentioned in the cause title of the writ petition as petitioners, the locus standi should not be denied when we are convinced that the petitioner-association in this case is bonafide in espousing the cause of its members. Besides, the impugned decision being a specific decision for specific procurement, it cannot be a policy decision as suggested by the learned Deputy Attorney General. Therefore, we hold that this writ petition is maintainable.</u>

7. Now, as to the merit of the case, it appears that section 3 of said Act provides for applicability of the provisions of the said Act in procurements by spending government fund, and section 4 has given the provisions of the said Act over riding effect. Section 31 provides for open-tender procedure as a priority in public procurement, however, section 68 provides that in case of urgent state necessity  or to face any disastrous event, government, in public interest, can take recourse to direct procurements in accordance with-section 32 or any other method. Sub section (2) of the section 68 further emphasises that the government will procure as per provisions of the said Act unless different decision is taken by the government on the ground of national security or in the  interest of national defence.

Now let us examine section 32 of the said Act, which is heavily relied upon by the learned Advocates for the respondents. The learned Advocates mainly rely on section 32 (10)0). The relevant portions of section 32 are quoted below:

“৩২। পণ্য, কার্য, ইত্যাদি ক্রয়ে অন্যান্য ক্রয় পদ্ধতির প্রয়োগ।

(১) ক্রয়কারী কার্যালয় প্রধান বা তৎকর্তৃক ক্ষমতাপ্রাপ্ত কোন কর্মকর্তার অনুমোদনক্রমে ধারা ৩১ এ উল্লিখিত পদ্ধতি ব্যতীত অন্য কোন পদ্ধতিতে পণ্য, সংশ্লিষ্ট সেবা, কার্য বা ভৌত সেবা ক্রয়ের ক্ষেত্রে, কারিগরী অথবা অর্থনৈতিক কারণ যুক্তিযুক্ত বিবেচিত হইলে ক্রয়কারী নিম্নবর্ণিত যে কোন পদ্ধতি প্রয়োগ করিতে পারিবে, যথাঃ-

(ক) নিম্নবর্ণিত ক্ষেত্রে সীমিত দরপত্র পদ্ধতি পয়োগ করা যাইবে যথাঃ

(খ)সম্ভাব্য প্রতিযোগিতা এড়াইবার জন্য বা দরপত্রদাতাদের মধ্যে বৈষম্য সৃষ্টি করিতে পারে এমন কোন পন্থা অবলম্বন না করিয়া নিম্নবর্ণিত ক্ষেত্রে সরাসরি ক্রয় পদ্ধতি প্রয়োগ করা যাইবে, যথাঃ-

(উ) সরকার ভিন্নরুপ সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ না করিলে, বিশেষ ক্ষেত্রে সরকারী মালিকানাধীন কোন শিল্প প্রতিষ্ঠান বা কারখানা হইতে সরকারের নিজস্ব অর্থে পণ্য ক্রয় করা হইলে,

(ঊ)------------

(৩)--------------

8. It appears from the above provision that sub-section (1) of section 32 enables the procurement authority to take recourse to direct procurement from government owned industrial establishments or factory if the same is found to be logical on mechanical or economic consideration কারিগরী অথবা অর্থনৈতিক কারণ যুক্তিযুক্ত বিবেচিত হইলে and the same bats be done by not adopting a method avoiding prospective competition or creating discrimination among the tenderness underlines supplied to give emphasis)

However, the minutes of the concerned ECNEC meeting as reproduced by the petitioner in the writ petition shows that although there was one proposal for open tender to encourage competition, the ECNEC took the impugned decision to do direct procurement from Khulna Shipyard and Chittagong Dry Dock, two government owned ship-builders, without assigning any reason for such direct procurement and/or without holding that such method was required on the mechanical or economic necessity as provided by sub-section (1) of section 32. We have read the discussions prior to reaching the impugned decision, but found not a vestige of discussion on the applicability or non-applicability of the provisions of Public Procurement Act 2006 and the rules made there under. It has been decided in several cases by the Supreme Court of this sub-continent that the government cannot act like an individual in disposing of State properties or in granting any benefit of largess in favour of any particular person because of the simple reason that the government is not the owner of the said properties and benefits. They belong to the people of the country and the government is only a trustee for the people and, as such, they can only act in accordance with law. The ratio of Kasturi Lal case as cited by Mr Azmalul Hossain, QC rather supports the above view. Speaking for the Court in Kusturi Lal, Bhagwati, J observed:

"Every activity of the Government has a public element in it and it must, therefore, be informed with reason and guided by public interest. Every action taken by the Government must be in public interest; the Government cannot act arbitrarily and without reason and if it does, its action would be liable to be invalidated."

9. Before Kasturi Lal, the Indian Supreme Court in the landmark case of Rahmana Dayaram Shetty vs International Airport Authority reported in AIR 1979 SC 1628 emphasized that the government cannot act in a discriminatory manner in awarding a contract.

<u>10. We are of the view that the ECNEC or any executive authority, how high so ever, cannot grant any benefit in favour of any one at its sweet will. It will have to act in accordance with law, and in the instant case the said law is Public Procurement Act, 2006. Since the ECNEC has decided in the instant case to do direct procurement not on mechanical or economic ground as provided by section 32 (1), we are of the view that it has acted illegally. The impugned decision does not even show any urgent state necessity or disastrous event to justify direct procurement under section 68. The impugned decision has not only affected the interests of prospective ship-builders in this country. It has deprived the members of the petitioner of their right to participate in the tender for no fault of them. Thus, we hold that the impugned decision does not come under the purview of exceptions as provided by section 32 and 68, and, as such, we are inclined to hold that the same is without lawful authority and of no legal effect.</u>

In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned decision of ECNEC taken in its 17th meeting held on 22-11-2009 for procurement/construction of four 108-TEUs self propelled multi-purpose container ships engaging Khulna Shipyard and Chittagong Dry Dock without inviting any tender is hereby declared to have been taken without lawful authority and of no legal effect.

End.

full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: In this Rule Nisi the respondents have been called upon to show cause as to why the respondents should not be directed to implement the decision as contained in memorandum No. Sha-8/Faj-65/93- 191 dated 29-6-1994 (Annexure-E) and as to why the respondents should not be directed to demarcate the road pursuant to "Annexure-E" and master plan dated 12-12-92 in CS Plot Nos. 1020, 1021, 912 and 913 (Annexure-E-1) and layout map dated 19-10-1985 (Annexure-E-2) and (Annexure-G) and RS Map being Plot No. 3319 (Annexure-L) and the gazette notification dated 9-3-1998 (Annexure-L-1) should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts giving rise to this Rule are as follows:

The petitioner No. 1 is a practicing lawyer of Bangladesh Supreme Court and is a Social Worker and has been working to uphold the rights of the citizens and the petitioner No. 2 is the resident of Badda area. He is a social worker and the President of "Protibashi Samajik Nirapatta Committee of East Badda" and the Secretary of local mosque namely "Baitul Sujud Zamey Mosque."

3. The Government through the respondent No. 4 (Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka) made acquisition of 2760.00 acres of land of Badda and other 6(six) Mauzas in favour of Rajuk in LA Case No. 138 of 1961-62 and in the year of 1992 the Ministry of Land released 1223 acres of land in favour of original owners. The remaining land is still in custody of the respondent No. 3. In order to uphold the right of the citizen the petitioner No. 1, as a social worker, submitted a representation dated 2-12-93 to the Minister, Ministry of Housing and Public Works to implement the decision of the committee constituted by the Cabinet on 7-2-93 issued vide Memo No. Sha-6(U) Badda Hu: Da: Ma: 429/92/15 dated 16-3-93 and subsequent decision of the said committee dated 18-4-93 of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works relating to 'C' Block at Mouza Badda, Map Sheet No. 2 under LA Case No. 138/1961-62. On the basis of said representation, the concerned Ministry directed to constitute a 3(three) members committee for spot enquiry and to submit a report in the matter and accordingly, the 3(three) members committee issued notice on 5-1-94 to the concerning people of Badda area including the petitioner No. 1 and thereafter made local enquiry relating to 'C' Zone/Block and heard the people of the locality including both the petitioners and then submitted a report to the concerned Ministry with the following recommendation:

যেহেতু সার্বিক পরিস্থিতি বিবেচনায় নিম্নরুপ সুপারিশ করা যাইতেছেঃ

(ক)রাজউক ১৯-১০-৮৫ইং তারিখের অনুমোদিত লে-আউট নক্সা অনুযায়ী প্রগতি স্বরণী হইতে সংযোগকারী রাস্তাটি ৭৫/৬০ ফুট চওড়া রাখিয়া সি জোনের শেষ প্রান্ত পর্যন্ত সোজাসুজি বাস্তবায়ন করিতে পারে।

(খ) ঐ রাস্তার উত্তর পার্শ্বের (রাজউক স্টাফ কোয়াটারের জমি ও পুলিশ ফাড়ির জমি বাদ দিয়া) ঘন বসতিপূর্ণ এবং মসজিদ, কবরস্থান সম্বলিত জমি প্রায় ৬.00 একর অবমুক্ত করিয়া সেই মতে সি জোনের নক্সা সংশোধন করিতে পারে।

4. The Government on considering of the aforesaid enquiry report arrived at a decision as evidenced by Memo No. SHA-8/RAJ-65/ 93/91 dated 29-6-94 which was written to the Chairman, RAJUK Dhaka. The relevant portion of that decision is quoted hereunder:

(১) হুকুম দখল আইন অনুসারে মসজিদ ও কবরস্থান হুকুম দখল করা যাইবে না। সেহেতু রাজউককে ঐ জমি অবশ্যই ছাড়িয়া দিতে হইবে। তাছাড়া রাজউকের জোনের পূর্ব ও উত্তর পার্শ্বের ব্যাপকে এলাকা নগরায়ন হইলে ঐ সমস্ত এলাকার জনগণের যোগাযোগের জন্য সি জোনের ঐ ৭৫ ফুট রাস্তার গুরুত্ব ও প্রয়োজন অত্যাধিক। ঘন বসতিপূর্ণ এলাকা হুকুম দখল করিলেও সরকার বা রাজউকের কোন লাভ হইবে না। (উচ্ছেদকারীদেরকে প্লট দিয়া) এবং রাজউকের জোনের পূর্ব ও উত্তর দিকের ব্যাপক এলাকার জনগণের যোগাযোগের বিষয়টি লক্ষ্য রাখিয়া ৭৫ ফুট রাস্তা বাস্তবায়ন অত্যন্ত যুক্তিযুক্ত বিধায় রাজউক ১৯-১০-৮৫ ইং তারিখের অনুমোদিত নকসা অনুযায়ী প্রগতি স্মরণী ও সি জোন সংযোগকারী ৭৫ ফুট রাস্তা বাস্তবায়ন করিবে।

(২) রাজউক ১৯-১০-৮৫ইং তারিখের নকসা অনুযায়ী প্রগতি স্মরণী জোনের সংযোগকারী ৭৫ ফুট চওড়া রাস্তার অবশিষ্ট অংশ ভরাট করিয়া সি জোনের শেষ প্রান্ত পর্যন্ত বাস্তবায়ন করিবে এবং এই রাস্তার উত্তর পার্শ্বের মসজিদ কবরস্থান ও ঘনবসতিপূর্ণ এলাকা মোট আনুমানিক ৬.00 একর জমি রাজউকের (স্টাফ কোয়াটার ও পুলিশ ফাড়ির জমি ব্যতীত) অবমুক্ত করিবে।

5. As per said decision of the Ministry of Housing and Public Works dated 29-6-94 the RAJUK submitted a map after corrections of the alignment showing the north-east area of the 'C' Zone without indicating the road as directed by the Ministry of Housing and Public Works. The Ministry of Works, on proper consideration of the map and as per earlier decisions of the Ministry dated 12-11-96 sent all the papers including plot index vide Memo No. Sha-8/Rajuk-65/93 /319 dated 12-11-96, to the Ministry of Land (respondent No. 1) for making arrangement to release the land measuring 5.92 acres with full particulars of the land of Mouza Badda, JL No. 291 and since then the matter has been pending for decision before the Ministry of Land. That the original owners of the land had already refunded the compensation money on different dates to the Government as per direction of the Government but in spite of that the respondent No. 1 (Secretary, Ministry of Land) did not issue any appropriate order of release of land for which the original owners are not in a position to utilise the land to their benefit. The respondent No. 4, (Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka) Came to the local area of Badda and demarcated the land with pucca pillars and accordingly, Kanongo and Surveyor demarcated the land for putting pucca pillars. In the background of such facts the petitioners and others approached to respondent No. 3, Chairman, RAJUK to implement the decision of the Government but in spite of that the respondent No. 3 did not or could not take any step to construct the road of Progati Sarani connecting the Badda 'C' Zone/Block as per the decision of the Ministry dated 19-10-85, 7-2-93 and 18-4-93 with malafide and ulterior motive for illegal gain.

6. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the activities of the respondent No. 3, Chairman, RAJUK, the petitioners moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

7. Respondent No. 3 contested the Rule by filing counter-affidavit denying the material allegation of the writ petition and contending, inter alia, that the writ petition is not maintainable, inasmuch as the writ petition is based upon incorrect information and it involves controversial question of facts which cannot be decided in writ jurisdiction. The correspondences mentioned in the writ petition are inter-ministerial governmental correspondences which do not create any right to any public individual to ask/claim for the inter-ministerial communications and, as such, the Rule is devoid of substance.

8. Mr Shafique Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, after placing the writ petition, submits that the Government decisions as evidenced by "Annexure-E & "Annexure-I" to the writ petition that the grievances raised in this writ petition involved breach of the constitutional obligations and statutory duties of the respondent Nos. 1-4 with regard to public interest but the respondent No. 3(Chairman of Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha) most illegally did not take any step to execute the Government decisions which tantamounts to relinquish the state power with regard to public interest by the public servants for their personal gain. The learned Advocate next submits with force that the respondents are jointly and severally liable to execute the decisions of the Government for the public interest but respondent No. 3 with an ulterior motive did not or could not implement the decision of the Government and therefore, the respondents are required to be directed by this Court to implement the decision as contained in 'Annexure-E' and 'Annexure-I' to the writ petition otherwise the people at large in the locality will suffer irreparable loss and injury as well as the very purpose of the public interest will be frustrated by willful negligence of the executives of the Government.

9. On the other hand, Mr Md Abdun Nur, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 3, after placing the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition and other materials on record, submits that the writ petition itself does not disclose any cause of action to file the writ petition. Furthermore, the petitioners have failed to show any law under which the respondents shall be compelled to discharge the duties as claimed in the writ petition and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. Mr Nur next argues that the so-called Inter-ministerial Governmental correspondences cannot be enforced through a writ for the simple reason that it is not law. The learned Advocate, in support of his submission, has relied on the decisions namely, the decisions reported in 50 DLR (AD) 11 and 7 BLT (AD) 313.

10. We have heard the learned Advocates, perused the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition, supplementary and the relevant papers as annexed therewith. Now, to deal with the contentions raised by the learned Advocates before us, we feel it necessary to decide first, whether in the facts and circumstances of the case, there is any legal scope to direct the respondents to implement the Inter-ministerial Governmental correspondences as contained in 'Annexure-E' and 'Annexure-I' to the writ petition.

11. The question as to implementation of the Government's decision or Inter-ministerial Governmental correspondences arose in the case of Al-Haj Abul Basher being dead his heirs Hosne Ara Begum and others vs Bangladesh and others reported in 50 DLR (AD) 11 wherein the Appellate Division held that:

"These Inter-Ministerial Communications are merely policy guidelines as to how the excess and unutilized lands are to be treated but these instructions do not create any legal right in favour of the petitioners to ask for return of the land from the Government after the same has been validly requisitioned under the law."

12. In the case of Professor Abdur Rahim Khan and others vs Ministry of Industries and others reported in 7 BLT (AD) 313 wherein it has been laid down as hereunder: "The recommendation of a Cabinet Committee cannot be enforced through a writ for the simple reason that it is not law. It is as simple as that. The Writ Petition was misconceived at the inception."

<u>13. On examining the writ petition, it appears to us that in the writ petition the petitioners made sole grievance against the respondent No. 3, Chairman, RAJUK to implement the Government decisions as we have noticed above. So, in view of the above quoted uniform decisions of our Apex Court, we are led to hold that the contention of the petitioners with regard to implement the recommendation/decision of Inter-ministerial correspondences by the Court in Writ Jurisdiction does not find any leg to stand on, inasmuch as the same bears no binding force to the Court in any way.</u>

14. However, the submissions made by Mr Shafique Ahmed, the. learned Advocate for the petitioner, with regard to construct the road of Progati Sarani connecting the Badda 'C' Zone/Block as per the decision of the Ministry dated 19-10-85, 7-2-93 and 18-4-93 in the interest of public may have some substance which is apparently a subject matter of inter-ministerial act of the Government. In the summary proceeding under Article 102, it is not possible to interfere with such disputed question of facts.

Consequently, the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost. The order of injunction granted at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

End.
