parties:
Gour Chandra Mohan to Babu and others ----- Petitioner 
Vs.
Md. Abu Bakar Siddque  and others ----- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
This rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 13-5-1999 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Rangpur in Other Appeal No. 260 of 1992 allowing the appeal by reversing the judgment and decree dated 27-7-1992 passed by the Additional Assistant Judge, Temporary Court No. 2, Rangpur in Other Suit No. 124 of 1989 dismissing the suit.

2. The opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted Other Suit No. 124 of 1989 in the Court of Additional Assistant Judge, Temporary Court No. 2, Rangpur impleading the predecessors of the petitioners as defendant paying for a declaration of title in 'Ka' schedule and recovery of possession of schedule 'Kha' and 'Ca' under schedule 'Ka' by evicting defendant there from.

3. The plaintiffs alleged that Shambhu Charan Das was original CS recorded tenant in 'Ka' schedule land. He died issueless leaving behind brother's sons Dino Das and Hari Das who got the property in equal share; Dino Das gave pattan of 4 decimals out of 6½ decimal of land to one Loknath Ghose in Chaitra, 1347 BS through dakhila; he also gave pattan 1/2 decimal to Loknath by registered deed dated 3-1-1942; Loknath has been possessing the same by constructing house upon 4½ decimal of land; Dino Das and Hari Das remained in ejmali possession of remaining 8½ decimals; then Hari Das died childless and his brother Dino Das inherited his share and subsequently gave pattan of 8½ decimals in favour of Abdul Majid in the month of Baishak, 1350 BS; Abdul Majid purchased 4 decimal land out of remaining land from Loknath Ghosh by registered deed dated 15-1-1953 and he also purchased 1/2 decimal by unregistered deed; he constructed house upon 13 decimals of land; Abdul Majid used to pay rent for 'ka' schedule land to his landlord Protap Chandra Das and RS record was prepared in his name; he was a member of Aahali hadish and there was a prayer room in the schedule land; in RS it was wrongly recorded as mosque and tin-shed house Kua but in fact there was no mosque; the defendant used to live by raising tin-shed house upon the land of Panchanon at new Senpara; during the time of liberation he went to India and his tin-shed house and other materials were looted away; this time Panchanan Barman sold his land to one Mokbul Hossain; then defendant prayed for shelter from Abdul Majid and he gave permission to raise 'a tinshed upon 1 decimal of land on the south side of the suit land; on 26-7-1975 the plaintiff purchased 'ka' schedule land by registered deed and extended their house upon the schedule 'kha' and he lived in half portion and gave rent to the tenant in the remaining half portion; plaintiff requested the defendant to surrender possession of 1 decimal amicable; then defendant filed Other Suit No. 167 of 1977 in the 2nd Court of Munsif, Rangpur impleading Abdul Majid as defendant; then plaintiffs were made parties in the said suit and contested the suit; subsequently defendant withdraw the said suit on 3-8-1989 with permission to sue afresh; in recent times the defendant gave threat to plaintiff to disposes him; the defendants were asked to give up possession of 'Ga' schedule but without vacating the property he filed Other Suit No. 167 of 1977 and refused to deliver possession; during pendency of the suit the defendant dispossessed the plaintiffs from 'Kha' schedule land on 2-2-1992.

4. The predecessors of the petitioners, herein. Khagendra Chandra Das as sole defendant contested the suit by filing written statement on 18-11-1990. The defendants contend that the suit is not maintainable and the same is barred by limitation. Shambhu Charan Das was the CS recorded tenant and he lived there with family by constructing house; he died of leaving his only son Bipin Chandra Das as sole heir; Bipin Chandra died of leaving only son defendant Khagendra Chandra Das as his heir; he has been in exclusive possession of the suit land for more than 30 years by paying rents and living with his family; Shambhu Charan Das had no brother's son namely Dino Das and Hari Das; that field SA record has been prepared in the name of defendants; on 22-1-1977 defendant came to know that SA record of 'Kha' schedule land has been prepared wrongly in the name of one Abdul Majid; defendant then filed Other Suit No. 167 of 1977 for correction of SA record but eventually withdraw the suit with permission to sue afresh; since then defendants are in possession of the suit land; since plaintiff filed the present suit of declaration of title, the defendants have not filed any other suit and decided to contest the present suit.

5. The trial Court considered the evidence of 3 PWs and 4 DWs including the documentary evidence and found that the suit is not maintainable in the present form and plaintiffs failed to prove their right, title, interest and possession in the suit property and also failed to prove their dispossession of the suit property on 2-2-1992 and also the case of permissive possession. The trial court further found that plaintiffs did not acquire any valid title in the suit property since the plaintiffs failed to prove the patta and dakhila in respect of acquisition of 4½ decimals urban land from Dino Das to Loknath Ghosh and successive acquisition by vendor of the plaintiff Abdul Majid is not in accordance with law. Thus the transfer of suit property by Abdul Majid to the plaintiffs by registered kabala is not also valid in 'the eye of law. Finally trial court clearly found that legally plaintiff is to prove his own case and for the weakness of the defendants, plaintiff's suit cannot be decreed. Accordingly, the trial Court dismissed the plaintiff’s suit by judgment and decree dated 27-7-1992.

6. The plaintiff then preferred Other Appeal No. 260 of 1992 before the District Judge, Rangpur. The learned Subordinate Judge, 1st court, Rangpur who heard the said appeal found that the plaintiff's predecessors Abdul Majid validly acquired title and possession by purchase and settlement (Pattan) and SA Khatian recorded in their name. Defendant was in permissive possession and living in 1 decimal land. The lower appellate court thereafter concluded that the suit properties were sold by Abdul Majid to the plaintiffs by registered kabala No. 34891 dated 26-7-1975 and delivered possession. Plaintiffs by mutated their names have been possessing the same by paying rent and taxes Learned Subordinate Judge accordingly by judgment and decree dated 13-5-1999 allowed 'the appeal and reversed the decision of the trial court, and decreed the suit of the plaintiffs.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 13-5-1999 the defendants as petitioners moved this court and obtained the present rule.

8. Mr Sajjad Ali Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that judgment of the appellate court is not a proper judgment of reversal. Learned appellate court committed an error of law in failing to notice that plaintiffs purchased the suit properties from their vendor Abdul Majid by registered sale deed on 26-7-1975 (Exhibit-15), who acquired 4 decimals of land from Loknath Ghosh by registered kabala dated 15-1-1953 (Exhibit-3) and 8½ decimals land from Dino Das by lease in Baishak 1350 BS and Loknath Ghosh got said 4 decimals land through Dakhila and 1/2 decimal by registered patta dated 3-1-1942 (Exhibit-14) from Dino Das. Plaintiffs failed to produce the dakhila but filed the registered patta (Exhibit-14) for 1/2 decimal land but the plaintiff did not file any document in respect of Patta of 8½ decimals land by Dino Das to Abdul Majid i.e. vendor of the plaintiffs and also failed to prove their title over the suit land. Trial Court after consideration of Exhibits Nos. 3, 14 and 15 rightly found that plaintiff failed to prove their title since the vendor of the plaintiffs did not acquire any valid title by the said exhibits. Accordingly, plaintiff did not acquire any right, title, interest and possession in the suit land by their pattan and sale deed, Exhibit-14 and 15, respectively. The learned appellate court set aside the decree of the trial court and allowed the appeal without giving any finding on this important issue. He further submits that the patta (Exhibit-14) is not 30 years old document so it has got no presumptive value in the eye of law, Both the courts below failed to consider and appreciate that the patta is not the original patta but a meadi patta for a period of 3 years and the same has not been produced/furnished from the custody of the original lessee Loknath Ghosh. He further submits that said patta does not create any title in the suit property as the same is barred under section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act. Appellate court without consider those important legal aspects of the matter and without reversing the finding of the trial court illegally allowed the appeal and decreed the suit. He finally submits that the decision of the appellate court is based on misconception of law, gross misreading and. misinterpretation of materials and evidence on record.

9. Mr Bhabesh Chandra Mustafi, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties on the other hand support the decision of the lower appellate court and submits that the appellate court below has rightly passed the judgment adverting the: finding of the trial court with reference to material evidence on record. He further submits that the learned appellate court rightly found that the vendor of the plaintiffs has acquired title in the suit property by settlement and purchase and SA Khatian was correctly prepared in the name of the vendor of the plaintiffs. Subsequently, the plaintiffs mutated their name in the khatian and have been possessing the properties by paying rent and taxes (Exhibits- 5, 6, 7 and 8 series), which clearly' proved that the plaintiff has been in possession. of the suit property and those important exhibits are always be used as collateral evidence of title, but the learned trial court has not consider those documents and erroneously found that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title in the suit property, and thereby committed error of law in not decreeing the suit.

10. On a meticulous examination of the judgment and decrees of the courts below, depositions of witnesses, all Exhibits, especially Exhibits No. 14 and 15, registered patta and sale deed, and other materials on record legal position and given my anxious consideration to the submissions of the learned counsel. It is not disputed that Shambhu Charan Das was admittedly the raiyati tenant in the suit property and CS khatian No. 124/23 (Exhibits-1 and ka) accordingly recorded in his name it appears that the learned trial court in his judgment discussed the evidence and also considered the certified copy of the registered patta (Exhibit-14) produced by the plaintiff which is the basis of the plaintiffs claim. After perusal of said Patta it appears that Dino Das gave pattan to Loknath ½ decimal of land by the said patta on 2-1-1942 and certified copy of the said patta was obtained on 18-10-1952. With regard to unregistered patta 4 decimals urban land by Dino Das to Loknath through dakhilas he did not acquire any title as no such dakhila was filed by the plaintiff. Plaintiff also did not file any document in respect of purchase of 8½ decimals of land by Dino Das to Abdul Majid, the vendor of the plaintiffs excepting the sale deed dated 26-7-1975 (Exhibit 15). Since Loknath and Dino Das did not acquire valid title in the suit properties, subsequent transfer of the suit land by Abdul Majid and ultimately to plaintiffs is not valid in the eye of law. The trial court has recorded clear finding in this regard that plaintiffs failed to prove their right, title and interest in the suit land, but the appellate court, without discussing the evidence had abruptly reversed the finding of the fact arrived of by the trial court. Such findings of the appellate court without adverting and reasoning of the trial court is not a proper judgment of reversal.

11. Further on consideration of oral and documentary evidence the trial court found that Abdul Majid had no title in the suit land, so preparation of SA khatian (Exhibit 2) and subsequently payment of rent by him under rent receipts (Exhibit 8 series), Exhibits 5,6 and 7 he did not acquire any title in the suit land. Eventually transfer of suit land by Abdul Majid to the plaintiffs by sale deed dated 26-7-1975 (Exhibit 15) is not valid in the eye of law. The learned appellate court without adverting such finding of the trial court found that those documents of possession are always admissible and may be used as collateral evidence of title. Such finding of appellate court is against the principles that the rent receipts, mutation khatian and the record of right do not create any title, in the suit property.

12. Trial Court after considering the Exhibit 14 found that the acquisition of the suit property by the vendors of plaintiffs and subsequent transfer to the plaintiffs is not valid as per provisions of section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act but appellate court without reversing such finding of the trial court decreed the suit. Such finding of the learned appellate court is not based on law. It appears that the plaintiffs filed certified copy of the patta dated 19-101952 allegedly executed by the Dino Das in favour of Loknath Ghosh in respect of 1/2 decimal on- 3-1-1942, which was not formally proved in evidence, as the plaintiff have not file the original patta nor they called for the volume of said patta from registry office. Accordingly, trial court left this certified copy of patta out of consideration in adjudicating claim of plaintiffs as this was not admitted in evidence in accordance with law, but appellate court after considering the said patta and erroneously decreed the suit. In Atul Gomes vs Julian Rozario, 6 MLR (AD) 46 original kabala was not produced in court and certified copy of deed was admitted in evidence and marked as Exhibit. It has been said that unless document is proved in accordance with provisions of Evidence Act such documents cannot be admitted in evidence and mere filing of document is not sufficient to satisfy the requirement of law. However, on close examination of said patta it appears that the patta was not a Patta creating tenancy right rather it was a meadi patta for 3years and is not a patta in respect of permanent settlement. More over the said patta has not been executed by both lessor and, as such, the same is void under section 107 of TP Act. In this connection I like to refer the decision in a case of Sheikh Md Siddique vs Hari Lai Nath Respondents reported in 22 DLR 359 wherein it is laid down: —

"Unilateral lease document void for offending against provisions of section 107 of TP Actlessor and lessee respectively executed unilateral patta and kabuliyat the same day-The two documents cannot be treated as one for complying with the provisions of section 107-held as each of the documents has not been executed by both the lessor and the lessee, the lease is void."

Thus trial court rightly held that the plaintiff's predecessors did not acquire any permanent tenancy right or title in respect of the suit properties by virtue of said patta. The lower appellate court has not assessed the evidence of 3 PWs. And 4 DWs as he was .being the last court of facts. The finding of the appellate court that the plaintiffs prove their title and possession in the suit property. While recording such findings the appellate court has not reverted the findings of the trial court who found that no title and possession in favour of the Plaintiffs upon proper assessment of evidence of 3 PWs and 4DWs and also on consideration of documentary evidence.

<u>13. More over courts below found that the patta-Exhibit No. 14 is 30 years old document and it may be taken as proved. But both the courts below totally misread and misconstrue the patta-Exhibit 14 and failed to consider that the patta is not original one but a certified copy and it was not produced from proper custody as such, it has got no evidentiary value in the eye of law. That the patta in question has wrongly accepted as evidence without any proof of its execution. So provisions of section 90 of the Evidence Act will not be attracted in the facts and circumstances of the present case. In this connection I like to rely on the decision in a case of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) vs Md Reazuddin PK reported in 5 BLC (AD) 76 wherein it has been held.</u>

"An attempt has also been made to argue that the amalnama in question was wrongly accepted as evidence without any proof of its execution. The learned counsel has, however, failed to satisfy us that the amalnama is not a 30 years old document and that it has not been produced from the proper custody. Once such a document more than 30 years old is produced from proper custody section 90 of the Evidence Act entitles the court to presume that it is a genuine document. The contention thus merits no consideration."

14. In the premises above, I find that the decision of the appellate court suffers from non-reading, misreading, misinterpretation of material evidence and misconception of law in deciding the issue involved in the suit and thus committed an error of law which has occasioned a failure of justice.

15. I have considered the decision cited by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties in the case of Fatema Khatun vs Fazil Meah reported in 6 BLC 241. The facts of the said decision have no manner of application in the present case and quite distinguishable.

16. In view of the facts and circumstances and the points of law involved in the case, I am of the view that the impugned judgment and decree dated 13-5-1999 suffers from illegally which calls for interference by this court. Thus the rule having merits succeeds.

17. In the result, this rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and decree dated 13-5-1999 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 1st court, Rangpur in Other Appeal No. 260 of 1992 are set-aside and judgment and decree dated 27-7-1992 passed by the learned Additional Assistant Judge, Temporary Court No. 2, Rangpur in Other Suit No. 124 of 1989 are hereby restored. There will be, however, no order as to costs.

18. Send down the Lower Court Records at once.

19. It is ordered and decreed that the Rule be and the same is hereby made absolute without any order as to costs. And it is ordered and decreed that the impugned Judgment and decree dated 13-5-1999 passed by the sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Rangpur in other Appeal No. 260 of 1992 be and the name is hereby set-aside.

20. And it is further ordered and decreed that the judgment and decree dated 27-7-1992 passed by the learned Additional Assistant Judge, Temporary Court No. 2, Rangpur in Other Suit No. 124 of 1989 are hereby restored.

Dated this the 11th day of March in the year of two thousand and nine of the Christian Era.

End.

lawyer:
Md Afzal Hossain with Shanaz Haque with Md Jahir Ahmed, Advocates-For the Appellant. 
Hosneara Begum Advocate-For the Respondent No.1.
parties:
Noor Alam ----- Defendant No. 3-Appellant
Vs
Sonali Bank & others ----- Plaintiff-Respondent
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: This appeal at the instance of appellant Noor Alam is directed against the Judgment and decree dated 23-11-1999 (decree signed on 4-1-2000) passed by the Sub-ordinate Judge, Additional Commercial Court No.1, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 145 of 1999 decreeing the suit.

2. Relevant facts of the case, in short, are that the respondent No.1, Sonali Bank as plaintiff filed a suit being Title Suit No.145 of 1999 in the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka impleading the present appellant Noor Alam and 2(two) others as defendants for realization of its outstanding dues amounting to Taka 4,43,888.50 with interest. The plaintiff's case in short, is that, the defendant No. 2 approached to the plaintiff-Bank vide his application dated 9-9-80 for issuance of a Bank Guarantee for Taka 6,50,000 for a period of one year to transact the normal business of defendant No.1 with Bangladesh Biman offering 15 Kathas of land as counter guarantee which valued at Taka 15,00,000 under Mouza Gulshan adjacent to Road No. 8 in Gulshan Model Town owned by the defendant No. 2, the proprietor of defendant No.1; that defendant No.3 vide his letter dated 15,9,1980 also prayed to the plaintiff-Bank to issue a Bank Guarantee for Taka 6,50,000 on behalf of the defendant No.1 of which defendant No. 2 is the proprietor offering his immovable property measuring 7½ Kathas of land with three-storied residential building situated thereon under Khatian No. 135 (New) and CS Khatian No. 14774 and C.S plot No. 28 in sheet No. 49 as described in the schedule 'B' of the plaint as security of the said Bank Guarantee; that the plaintiff-Bank through its Eskaton Road. Branch vide letter No. Eska/ BG-80/4 /1423 dated 1-10-1980 issued Bank Guarantee for Taka 6,50,000 for a period up-to 30th September, 1981 as required by them and thereupon, the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 mortgaged their property in favour of the plaintiff-bank as described in the schedule of the plaint; that on 22-11-1981 Bangladesh Biman, the beneficiary of the aforesaid Bank Guarantee, requested its Banker at Ramna Branch of the plaintiff-Bank to collect the amount of Taka 4,91,980/99 against the aforesaid Bank Guarantee for Taka 6,50,00.0 from the Eskaton Road Branch of the plaintiff-Bank and thereupon, the plaintiff-Bank on various occasions asked the defendant No. 2, to do the needful regarding the claim of the beneficiary Bangladesh Biman. The defendant No.2 instead of regularizing the Account filed a suit being TS No. 37 of 1981 in the Court of 3rd Sub-ordinate Judge, Dhaka for Temporary injunction restraining the plaintiff-Bank and the beneficiary-Bangladesh Biman, from encashing the Bank Guarantee dated 28-2-81 and obtained an order of status-quo with regard to encashment of the Bank Guarantee; that ultimately the aforesaid order of status-quo was vacated by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge Court, Dhaka vide order dated 29-7-81 and thereupon, unsuccessful-plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 329 of 1981 in the Court of the leaned District Judge, Dhaka; that during the pendency of the aforesaid Misc. Appeal No. 329 of 1981 in the , Court of District Judge, Dhaka MLO No 14 was promulgated on 22nd April, 1982 and consequent thereupon by an order of the learned District Judge, Dhaka dated 28-6-1982 the aforesaid Misc. Appeal was struck off; that the defendant No. 1 was required to make marginal deposit of Taka 3,25,000 out of which Taka 2,61,000 was given by a cheque of Agrani Bank, Ramna branch against current account of the wife of the defendant No. 2 which was dishonored twice by the Bank. In spite of repeated reminder letters issued by the plaintiff bank to the defendant No. 2 for payment against the Bank Guarantee, nothing was done. Under this facts and circumstances the plaintiff-Bank was compelled to pay Taka 4,91,980.99 to the beneficiary, Bangladesh Biman on 17-10-82 under obligation for the Bank Guarantee on behalf of the defendant No. 1. Hence the suit.

3. The defendant No. 3 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaintiff contending, inter-alia, that the defendant No. 3 did not go to the plaintiff-Bank at any point of time, neither he mortgaged his property nor he became guarantor for anybody whatsoever; that some of the officers of the plaintiff-Bank in-collusion with defendant Nos. 1 and 2 prepared some forged documents in his name by way of false personating; that the defendant No.3 is not acquainted with the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in any manner and, as such, the question of being a guarantor for them by using his original title deed of 'B' schedule property does not arise at all; that due to missing of his original deed of his property relating to 'B' schedule of the plaint he lodged to GD dated 23-1-1978 and 14-10-1978 respectively and knowing about the suit as well as whereabouts of his original deed the defendant No.3 requested to the plaintiff-Bank to return his deed relating to "B-schedule" property of the plaint and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost.

4. At the trial the plaintiff-Bank (respondent No. 1) examined as many as 4 (four) witnesses and only contesting defendant No.3 examined in all 3(three) witnesses and both the parties exhibited a series of documents to prove their respective cases.

5. The learned Subordinate Judge and Additional Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 heard the learned Advocates of both the sides and ultimately, on consideration of the evidences and other materials on record arrived at a finding that the plaintiff-Bank is entitled to get a decree as prayed for and accordingly, decreed the suit against the defendant No. 3 on contest and ex-parte against the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by his judgment and decree dated 23-11-1999 (decree signed on 4-1-2000).

6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree the only contesting defendant No. 3 as appellant preferred the instant First Appeal.

7. Mr Md Afzal Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-appellant after placing all the relevant materials on record submits that the judgment of the trial Court below is perverse being contrary to law and material evidence on record.

8. Drawing our attention to the opinion of hand writing experts dated 19-11-1988 and 12-7-1990 respectively, Mr Afzal Hossain submits that 2 finger print experts of CID in their respective opinion categorically stated that the signatures as contained in deeds in question are forged and the present appellant as defendant No. 3 contested the suit by filing written statement and himself was examined as DW-1, who in his written statement as well as deposition categorically stated that he never mortgaged his property as security of the Bank-guarantee in favour of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by executing any mortgage deed accompanied with power of attorney and at the trial finger print specialist of CID Mrs. Setara Begum was examined as DW-2, who proved her report as "Exhibit- Go" but the trial Court below without assigning any cogent reason most illegally discarded the consistent evidence of DW-1, DW-2 and DW-3 including the opinion of hand writing expert.

9. He next upon referring to the decisions reported in 3 BLC (AD) 85, 56 DLR (AD) 42 submits that since by scientific process or method examination of signature, particularly thumb impression, has been developed much, and, as such, it is safe and sound to leave the matter of examination of signature/ thumb impression as well as hand writing to the expert or to the person specialist in the examination of writing including thumb impression for avoiding possibility or probability of failing very much in error in arriving at an opinion by the Court.

10. Mr. Afzal Hossain, while elaborating his submission has taken us to the evidence of PWs and DWs and then points out that from a plain reading of the evidence of DW-1, DW-2, DW-3 and the evidence of PW-1 it would be apparent that the appellant did never go to the plaintiff-Bank for mortgaging his property not he became guarantor for any body and that some of the officers of the plaintiff-Bank in-collusion with defendant Nos.1 and 2 created some forged documents in his name by way of false personating for getting illegal gain and in the facts and circumstances of the case the defendant-appellant has been made scapegoat. He finally submits that the trial Court below having failed to consider the hand writing expert's opinion dated 19-11-1988 and 12-7-1990 respectively and GD Entry dated 23-1-1978 and 14-10-1978 as proved by "Exhibit A, Exhibit A-1 and Exhibit Go" and thereby erred in law in passing the impugned judgment and decree without following the correct principle relating to the appreciation of the evidence on record and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree so far it relates to the present defendant-appellant is set-aside.

11. On the other hand, Mrs. Hosneara Begum, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-respondent supports the impugned judgment and decree which was, according to him just, correct and proper. Mrs Hosneara Begum in the course of her argument upon referring to the opinion of the hand writing expert as evidence by "Exhibit-Ga" together with the deposition of DW-2, Setara Begum submits that the hand writing expert without properly examining the thumb impression of the appellant submitted her opinion which, in fact, does not carry any legal value and the trial Court below on assessment of the entire evidence on record rightly doubted he expert's opinion. The learned Advocate further upon placing the evidence of PW Nos. 1-4 submits that all the PWs. testified in one voice that the present defendant-appellant himself mortgaged his property by executing deed of mortgage along with power of attorney in accordance with law, the PWs are all officers of Sonali Bank and the defendant-appellant by adducing evidence could not show anything that there was any enmity or hostile relation between the parties and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree should not be disturbed.

12. Mrs. Hosneara Begum, the learned Advocate finally argues that "Exhibit-12" reflects that the father of defendant-appellant No. 3 made an under taking that if his son failed to pay the money against the Bank guarantee he will pay the same, who as witness also put his signature in the power of attorney in question, the trial Court below on assessment of the entire evidence on record both oral and documentary committed no illegality in decreeing the suit and the same does not call for any interference by this Court.

13. To effectively deal with the contentions raised by the learned Advocates for both the parties before us it would be convenient for us to decide first whether the learned trial Judge was Justified in decreeing the suit ignoring the opinion of experts in respect of thumb impression of defendant No. 3. In order to resolve this dispute let us advert the material evidence on record.

14. At the trial the plaintiff-Bank examined as many as four witnesses to prove its case. PW-1, Shudankshu Kumar Das as officer of the Bank stated in his deposition that the defendant No. 3 voluntarily stood as guarantor for and on behalf of defendant Nos. 1-2. This witness also stated that since the defendant No. 2 did not pay any amount against the Bank-guarantee and thus, the plaintiff-Bank was compelled to pay the amount against the Bank-guarantee to the beneficiary, Bangladesh Biman. This witness proved the power of attorney of defendant. No.3 and all other documents relating to the property of defendant No.3 as "Exhibit-4", "Ext.4 (A)" and "Exhibit-7 series". This witness in his cross-examination stated that:

২ নং বিবাদী ব্যাংক কর্মচারীদের সাথে অবৈধ যোগাযোগে এসব কাগজ তৈরি করেছে কিনা বলতে পারি না। একজিবিট-৩ তে একটি ফটো আছে যিনি এফিডেভিট করেছেন তার এই ফটো দেখে এবং আমাকে দেখানো ৩ নং বিবাদী কথিত ব্যক্তিকে দেখে বলতে পারছি না  যে ঐ ব্যক্তির ফটোই এটি কিনা কারন দাড়িওয়ালা এবং দাড়ি ছাড়া এবং চুলের সাইজ ও সমান নয়।

This witness also stated in his cross-examination that:

একজিবিট-৪, ৩ নং বিবাদী ও তার পক্ষের কেউ ব্যাংকে দাখিল করেছে এটা দেখানোর কোন কাগজ নাই। ২ নং বিবাদী এটি তৈরী করেছে অন্য লোককে ৩ নং বিবাদী সাজিয়ে একথা সত্য না মিথ্যা বলতে পারি না। একজিবিট-৪ জাল না প্রকৃত বলতে পারি না। ২ নং বিবাদী ব্যাংকের সংশ্লিষ্ট কর্মচারীদের সাথে যোগাযোগ করে দাখিল করেছে কিনা বলতে পারি না।

This witness also stated in his cross-examination that:

কথিত মর্টগেজ ছাড়াই ৩ নং বিবাদীকে গ্যারান্টোর দেখানো হয়েছে কিনা বলতে পারি না। একজিবিট-৭ এর কোন কাগজ ৩ নং বিবাদী ব্যাংকে জমা দেয়নি কিনা বলতে পারি না। ৩ নং বিবাদীর “বি” সিডিউল সংক্রান্ত কাগজপত্র চুরি হয়েছিল কিনা, সে সম্পর্কে সে জি,ডি, এন্ট্রি করেছিল কিনা বলতে পারি না।

PW-1, also stated in his cross-examination that he could not say anything as to whether any investigation was held in connection with the "B schedule" property.

15. PW-2, Abdus Salam Miah, stated in his deposition that at the relevant tune he was Deputy Chief Accountant of the principle office and he proved the power of attorney and his signature thereon as "Exhibit-4 (A)". This witness also stated that the defendant No. 3, executed the said power of attorney in his presence and one Abdul Haque, the father of the defendant No. 3 put his signature in the power of attorney as witness. This witness denied the suggestion that he deposed falsely and signatures as made in "Exhibit-4 (b)" and "Exhibit- 4 (c)" are not genuine signature of Nur Alam and Abdul Haque. This witness finally denied the suggestion that he and Md Habibullah in connivance with the defendant No.2 forged the documents in question by way of false personating,

16. PW-3, Abdur Rouf as clerk (Mohrar) of Sub-registrar office proved "Exhibit-D" (thumb impression book) and his signature thereon as "Ext. Dl". This witness also proved the thumb impression of appellant-Nur Alam.

17. PW-4, Md. Habibullah Bhuiyan, who in his deposition stated that at the relevant time in the year of 1980 he was manager of Sonali Bank, Eskaton Branch and at that time defendant No. 2 and his wife had account in that branch of Sonali Bank. This witness also stated that: ব্যাংক গ্যারান্টির জন্য ৩ নং বিবাদী ও ২ নং বিবাদীর নিকট হইতে কাউন্টার গ্যারান্টি নেয় প্রদর্শনী-২, ৩ নং বিবাদী নূর আলম দিয়েছিল। This witness in his cross-examination stated that: আমার সম্মুখে নুর আলম সহি দিয়াছে। নুর আলমের পিতার সাক্ষী আছে কিনা আমি জানি না।

18. On assessment of the evidence of PWs, it appears that PW-2, PW-3 and PW-4 all of them testified in one voice that Nur Alam, defendant No.3 stood as guarantor against the Bank-guarantee for and on behalf of the defendant No. 2 by mortgaging his property as security of the bank-guarantee.

19. From the above quoted evidence of PW-1, it also transpires that PW-1, failed to disclose in his evidence that whether the appellant (defendant No. 3 ) himself executed the counter guarantee in question or not. This witness in his evidence also could not disclose that whether "Exhibit-4" and "Exhibit-7(3)" are related to the property of defendant No. 3 (present appellant).

20. Now, let us turn our eyes to the evidence of DWs. As already noticed that the present appellant as defendant No. 3 only contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint stating, inter-alia, that he filed two GD dated 23-1-1978 and 14-10-1978 respectively to the effect that his deed relating to "B-Schedule" property was missing; that some of the officers of Sonali Bank, Eskaton Branch in-collusion with defendant No. 2 of practicing fraud manipulated/created a forged counter bank guarantee in the name of the defendant No.3 by way of false personation in using his missing deed.

21. At the trial the defendant No. 3 himself was examined as DW-1, Md Nur Alam, who in his deposition categorically stated that the defendant No. 2 in-collusion with some of the officers of the Bank on practicing fraud by using his missing deed created a forged counter bank-guarantee in his name. This witness in his deposition also stated that he had no relation with the defendant No. 1, that is, company of defendant No. 2 and the defendant No. 2 so the question to stand as guarantor for defendant Nos-1-2 by mortgaging his property does not arise at. all whatsoever. This witness also stated in his deposition that his original deed relating to "B-schedule" property was missing long before filling the instant suit and to that effect he lodged two GD with Sutrapur police station on 23-1-1978 and 14-10-1978 respectively, that is, long 3/4 years prior to filing the present suit on 29-2-1983. This witness also stated in his deposition that: একজিবিট-৪ যে জ্বাল সেটা প্রমান করার জন্য এক্সপার্ট অপিনিয়নের জন্য পাঠাতে চাই। This witness in his cross-examination denied the suggestion that on 29-9-1980 he went to the Sub-registrar office and executed power of attorney.

22. DW-2, Mrs Setara Begum, who stated in her deposition that she is in service under CID as Finger Print Expert. This witness proved her opinion and her signature thereon as "Exhibit-Ga" and "Exhibit Ga-1" respectively. This witness stated in her deposition that: দলিল নং ৩২২২৪ তারিখ ২৯-৯-৮০ তে নুর আলম (৩ নং বিবাদী) জামিনদার নামের বরাবরে প্রদত্ত ‘এ’ চিহিৃত আংগুলের ছাপটি গত ১৯-২-৯০ তারিখে লওয়া নুর আলমের দুই হাতের দশ আংগুলের নমুনা ছাপ গুলির সহিত কোনই মিল নাই।

DW-2, in her cross-examination stated that:

আমি শুধু এল, টি, আই, (টিপ সহি) এনলার্জ মর্মে (বর্ধিত আলোকচিত্র) করিয়াছি। দশ আংগুলের নমুনা ছাপ গুলি পরীক্ষা করিয়াছি। ঐগুলি এনলার্জ করিনি।

23. DW-3, Ashfaque Ahmed, in his evidence corroborated the deposition of DW-1, in respect of all material particulars.

24. On a careful scrutiny of the evidence of DW-2, Setara Begum, it appears that she examined the finger print of DW-1 in applying scientific method and who on comparison of the thumb impressions on the alleged documents with the admitted thumb impression of the defendant No. 3 found the thumb impressions on the alleged documents are forged. It is found that trial Court below without assigning any reason as to the question of doubting the expert opinion "Exhibit -Ga" decreed the suit mainly on the basis of documents produced by the plaintiff-Bank holding that :—

“৩ নং বিবাদীর জবাবে ১/২ নং বিবাদীর ঋণের বিষয় অস্বীকার করলেও ১/২ বিবাদীর ঋণের নিশ্চয়তা স্বরুপ গ্যারান্টর এ বিষয় অস্বীকার করলেও ১/২ নং বিবাদীর ঋণের জন্য ৩ নং বিবাদীর জামিনদার হয়েছেন তাহা বাদী ব্যাংকের দাখিলকৃত কাগজ পত্র দৃষ্টে প্রতীয়মান হওয়া যায়। বিবাদীপক্ষের স্বাক্ষীগণ ৩ নং বিবাদীকে ঋণের বিষয়ে বা জামিনের বিষয়ে সমর্থ না করলেও ৩ নং বিবাদীর দালিলিক কর্মকান্ড প্রমান করে যে, ৩ নং বিবাদী ১/২ নং বিবাদীর ঋণের গ্যারান্টর ছিল। কাজেই ৩ নং বিবাদীর দায় এড়াইবার মত কোন উপযুক্ত প্রমান আদালতে উপস্থিত করে নাই ও ৩ নং বিবাদীর আংগুলের ছাপ আদালতে দাখিল করে গ্যারান্টির বিষয় অস্বীকার করলেও উক্ত বিষয়ে ২ নং বিবাদী প্রদর্শনী সম্পর্কে যে, বিশেষজ্ঞ মতামত প্রদান করেন বাদীর এই মামলার দায় এড়ানোর জন্য তাহা যথেষ্ট নহে।”

25. Now, let us examine the legal position in this regard.

26. In the case of Prafitllah Kumar vs Govt. of Bangladesh reported in 28 DLR 123, it has been observed that:—"Expert's opinion enables the Court to come to a satisfactory conclusion, though the said opinion is not binding upon the Court."

27. In the case of SK Abdul Quaseni vs Mayez Llddin Mondal reported in 45 DLR 169, it has been held as follows:

"It is true that the Court itself can compare any signature or LTI of any concerned person himself under section 73 of the Evidence Act and come to a decision but it is better to have an expert's opinion also particularly in case of LTI."

28. In the case of Serajuddin Ahmed vs AKM Saifitl Alam reported in 56 DLR (AD) 41; it has been held that:—

"The law permits the Court to compare signature of a person with his admitted signature, but still then superior Courts have sounded caution to avoid the curse of comparing the signature thumb impression by the Court itself. Since by scientific  process or method examination of signature particularly thumb impression has  developed much and. as such, it is safe and  sound to leave the matter of examination of  signature including thumb impression as  well as hand writing to the expert or to the  person specialized in the examination of writing including thumb impression for  avoiding possibility or probability of falling very much in error in arriving at an  opinion by the Court upon resorting to comparison for ascertainment of similarity or dissimilarity of writing or thumb impression."

29. In the case of Eklas Khan vs Prajesh Chandra Das reported in 7 BLD (AD) 142, it has been held as follows:—

"Opinion of an expert, such as, a hand-writing expert, is only a relevant fact under section 45 of the Evidence Act. The Court will certainly consider the expert's opinion but it is the Court which alone will come to its own conclusion regarding the matter on which the Expert gives opinion that is why an expert's opinion, particularly of a hand-writing expert, is always received with great caution."

30. In the case of Kessarbai vs Jethabai reported in AIR 1928 (PC) 277, it has been held as follows:—

"mere comparison of admitted signature without expert's advice or microscopic examination is dangerous."

31. In the case of Tarak Chandra Majhi vs Atahar Ali Howlader reported in 13 BLT (AD) 3 it has been held as follows:— "In case of contentious writing signature etc. though provision of section 73 of the Evidence Act permits the Court to compare the contentious signature with the admitted signature, the safe and best course in our view for the court would be to avoid the practice of comparing the writing or signature etc. and should not stake its judgment on the opinion formed or view taken upon resorting to risky or in other words unsatisfactory and dangerous' procedure."

32. These are the consistent view taken by the superior Court of different jurisdictions on an analysis of the aforesaid decisions it appears that section 73 of the Evidence Act empowers the Court to compare any signature or LTI of any concerned person but it is better to rely on expert's opinion in a case of LTI. Keeping this view in mind, let us now, examine about the opinion of the hand writing experts. In this case it is found that as per Court's order Ranjit Paul, hand writing expert, CID, Dhaka submitted a reported on 19-11-1988 stating as follows:—

মতামত

উল্লেখিত দলিল পত্রাদিস্থ আংগুলের ছাপগুলিকে বৈজ্ঞানিক যন্ত্রপাতি দ্বারা বিস্তারিত ভাবে পরীক্ষা নিরীক্ষা করিলাম এবং নিম্নে মতামত প্রদান করিলাম।

জেনারেল ইরেভোকেবল পাওয়ার অব এ্যাটর্নি দলিল নং ৩২২২৪ তারিখ ২৯-২-৮০ তে নূর আলম নামের বরাবরে প্রদত্ত “এ” চিহিৃত আংগুলের ছাপটি গত ১৯-২-১০ ইং তারিখে হলুদ কার্টিজ কাগজে লওয়া নূর আলমের ১০ আংগুলের নমুনা “ব” সিরিজ চিহিৃত নমুনা ছাপগুলির সহিত কোনই মিল নাই।

33. It is also found that as per Court's order Mrs Setara Begum, hand writing expert, CID, Dhaka also submitted a report on 12-7-1990 stating as follows:—

আমি উপরোক্ত দলিল পত্রাদির আংগুলের ছাপ পরীক্ষা করিলাম এবং আমার মতামত নিম্নরুপ।

মতামত

থাম বই খন্ড ৩০/৮০, তালিকা নং ২৭৫১ এ ২০ পৃষ্ঠায় ক্রমিত নং ১৪৩৫২ এ নূর আলমের বরাবরে “A-1” চিহিৃত আংগুলের ছাপটি গত ইং ২৫-৯-৮৮ তারিখে সাদা কাগজে লওয়া “B” সিরিজ চিহিৃত নুর আলমের দশ আংগুলের নমুনা ছাপের সহিত কোনই মিল নেই।

34. From the above, it appears that as per Court's order 2 (two) hand writing experts of CID, Dhaka on comparison of the thumb impressions on the alleged documents with the admitted thumb impressions of the appellant (defendant No. 3) found the thumb impressions on the alleged documents are forged. The hand writing experts appears to have examined the thumb impressions in question in accordance with law.

35. On a careful perusal of the aforesaid opinion of the hand writing expert together with the evidence of PWs and DWs vis-a-vis the decisions reported in 56 DLR(AD) 41, 45 DLR 169 and 3BLC (AD) 85, we do not find any logic to discard the opinion of hand writing experts dated 19-11-1988 and 12-7-1990 respectively.

<u>36. As already noticed that the Trial Court below without assigning any reason as to the question of consecutive expert's opinion or the legal strength of expert's opinion abruptly arrived at a finding that in the facts and circumstances of the case expert's opinion is not enough to disbelieve the plaintiff-Bank's case. The Court is required to take into account that in the modern world science has been developing very much day by day and it is also need of the day to detect the truth by applying modern technology. In this case highest team of CID in order to detect the genuineness of truth impressions on the alleged documents examined the thumb impressions on the alleged documents with the admitted thumb impressions of the appellant (defendant No. 3) by applying scientific method and submitted two consecutive reports dated 19-11-1988 and 12-7-1990 respectively stating the thumb impressions on alleged documents were not in the hand of the defendant-Nur Alam. Therefore, our view is that the trial Court committed wrong in discarding the GD entries (Exhibit-A) as well as opinion of the hand writing experts (Exhibit-Ca & Ga-1). In the facts and circumstances of the case the trial Court ought to have believed the opinion of the hand writing experts.</u>

37. We have already found that the thumb impression of defendant -No. 3 was examined by two experts of CID, Dhaka and both of them on comparison of the thumb impressions on the alleged documents with the admitted thumb impression of the appellant (defendant No. 3) found the thumb impressions on the alleged documents are forged. The trial Court below therefore, was absolutely wrong in decreeing the suit ignoring consecutive expert's opinion with regard to thumb impression of the defendant No. 3.

38. A drowning man catches at a straw. So is the case with Mrs Hosneara Begum, the learned Advocate for the respondent-Bank. Mrs Hosneara Begum, at the end of the day upon referring to the decisions reported in 1BCR-490 and 7 BLD (AD) 142 submits that the opinion of the hand writing expert is not binding upon the Court, it is only admitted in evidence to help the Court in forming an opinion of its own and in the facts and circumstances if the case the trial Court below committed no illegality in decreeing the suit ignoring the opinion of hand writing expert.

39. To appreciate this last branch of argument, we have carefully studied the decisions reported in 1 BCR-490 and 7 BLD (AD) 142 to the best of our ability and it appears to us, in fact, none of the decisions is relevant for the issues raised in this case inasmuch in those cases thumb impression was not examined by the hand writing expert. Rather, it appears to us the observation of the 7 BLD's in respect of hand writing expert in the facts and circumstances of the present case supports the defendant-appellant's case. Therefore, we find no substance in either of the contentions as raised by the learned Advocate for the respondent-bank.

40. In view of our discussions made above, and the legal position, the facts and circumstances of the case, we hold that the plaintiff-respondent totally failed to establish its claim against the appellant (defendant No. 3) and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree cannot be sustained in law so far it relates to the claims against the defendant No. 3.

41. In the result, the appeal is allowed and the connected Rule being Civil Rule No. 89(f)/ 2003 is also disposed of. The impugned judgment and decree so far those are against the defendant No. 3 are set-aside. The parties are directed to bear their own costs. The respondent-bank is at liberty to recover its decreed amount from other defendant Nos. 1-2 in accordance with law.

Let a copy of this judgment along with lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.

full_judgment:
AFM Abdur Rahman J : In pursuance of the direction given by this Court to the defendant to satisfy this Court that the principal defendant opposite parties are not under obligation to furnish security in order to protect the interest of the plaintiff or to furnish the security, the defendant No. 1, the vessel filed application for vacating/re-calling the order of arrest of the vessel 'MV BK Ace' the also an application, by the defendant No. 5 for a direction upon the plaintiff to make payment for the cargo and take delivery of the same upon retiring the shipping documents through bank, this Court heard the parties on the application and now disposes the same by this single order.

2. This Court on 8-11-2010 passed an order of arrest of the vessel 'MV BK Ace', now lying at the outer anchorage of Chittagong Port on the prayer of the plaintiff LMJ International Limited, which instituted the instant Admiralty Suit on the ground that the plaintiff imported 28,500 MT of Bulgarian wheat from the defendant No. 5 Messrs Soared SA for onwards supply to the Director General, Ministry of Food & Disaster Management Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh, under a contract No. DGOF /DOP /EP/Wheat-35 (Quotation)/2010-1698, dated 22-9-2010, and the said consignment was loaded on board the defendant No. 1 vessel 'MV BK Ace' at the load port of Varna, Bulgaria which reached the Chittagong Port on 5-11-2010. But although the plaintiff submitted original two bills of leading dated 12-9-2010 to the shipping agent of the Vessel, yet the defendant vessel failed to discharge the cargo and in the meantime twenty days have elapsed after tendering the notice of readiness by the defendant vessel on 8-10-2010, for which under compelling circumstances and due to suffering huge financial loss and injury for delay in discharging the cargo the plaintiff submitted a claim of Taka 77,46,56,784 to the owner of the vessel and that the being not been paid or denied within a reasonable period the plaintiff instituted the instant Admiralty suit with the prayer for a decree directing the defendants to release/ discharge of 22,428 MT Bulgarian wheat to the plaintiff in terms of the bills of leading, dated 12-9-2010 and letter of credit dated 10-9-2010 and also for a decree for a compensation at a total sum of US $ 9,833,685 equivalent to BD Taka 77,46,784 together with 20% interest per annum till the date of filing of the suit and also interest pendentelity at the rate of 20%.

3. Upon such plaint and the application for arrest of the vessel this Court passed the aforementioned order for arrest of the defendant No. 1 vessel on 8-11-2010.

4. The learned senior Advocate Mr. M Hafizullah appearing on behalf of the defendant No. 1 vessel 'MV BK Ace' in order to substantiate the ground of his claim in the application that the defendant No. 1 vessel is not liable to furnish any security to protect the interest of the plaintiff in the suit argued, that the instant suit is not maintainable and, as such, the order of arrest is not sustainable on the ground that the plaintiff is neither a party to the shipping documents of the cargo nor does it have any agreement whatsoever with the defendant No. 1, hence on cause of action has arisen in favour of the plaintiff against the defendant No. 1 and, as such, the plaintiff has no locus stand to file the instant suit and therefore, since the suit is liable to be dismissed, the order of arrest cannot be sustained.

5. The learned senior Advocate Mr. M Hafizullah, further argued that the plaintiff is neither the owner nor the consignee or assignee of the bills of lading and admittedly the L/C has not as yet been negotiated upon payment of the price of the goods and the title of the goods has not yet passed in favour of the plaintiff and, as such, the plaintiff has got no locus standi to institute the instant admiralty suit for which the order of arrest of the vessel cannot be sustained.

6. The learned senior Advocate Mr. M Hafizullah, further argued that as the plaintiff did not submit the original copy of the bills of lading for the purpose of discharge or delivery of the cargo, the vessel owner or to the master of the vessel is not liable to deliver or discharge the cargo in favour of the plaintiff and, as such, plaintiff is not entitled to secure the same by way of arresting the vessel illegally.

7. In support of his arguments the learned senior Advocate Mr. M Hafizullah, relied upon the case of Modina vegetable and Oil Refinery Industries (Pvt) Limited vs MT Dolores reported in 45 DLR 740, and 13 BLD (AD) 211, Shahnewaj Traders vs MV Slater reported in 7 BLT (AD) 381, KYCR Coil Industries Ltd vs MV Thor Transity reported in 10 BLC 663 and the unreported case of Prime Cement Ltd vs MV label-e-Rahmat in Admiralty Suit No. 17 of 2010.

8. The learned Senior Advocate Mr. M Hafizullah, submitted that the master of the vessel being misleader and duped by the plaintiff shipping agent Messrs Sea Com Shipping Lines limited allowed unloading of 1,500 MT wheat into the lighterage vessel 'MV Golden Dream' but the same is still under the custody of the master of the vessel since the lighterage vessel is still remaining aside of the mother vessel and since the plaintiff is not the owner of the Cargo yet the Cargo cannot be delivered to him.

9. The learned Senior Advocate Mr. M Hafizullah, contends that the vessel is now facing hug financial prejudice as it has been arrested without lawful cause by the plaintiff.

10. The learned senior Advocate Dr. M Zahir, appearing on behalf of the defendant No. 5 in support of his application argued that the order of arrest passed by this Court on 8-11-2009 cannot be sustained and liable to be immediate vacation on the ground of suppression of facts and for the reason of misleading the Court since in paragraph No. 6 of the plaint the plaintiff admitted that the defendant No. 5 did not send the shipping documents i. e. the commercial invoice, packing list, bills of lading and other documents, but most cleverly stated in paragraph No. 8 of the plaint that the plaintiff have submitted original two bills of lading, all dated 12-9-2010 to the shipping agent for the purpose of taking delivery of the Cargo. This false statement has been made in order to obtain an order or arrest of the vessel from this Court and, as such, on this sole ground the order of arrest is required to be vacated.

11. The learned Senior Advocate Dr. M Zahir, contends that the L/C opening Bank i.e. the State Bank of India returned back the original copy of the shipping documents which was sent by the defendant No. 5, on the flimsy ground of discrepancy and, as such, no question of submitting any original copy of bills of lading before the master or agent of the vessel arises at all and therefore the instant Admiralty is liable to be dismissed and the order of arrest be vacated.

12. The learned Senior Advocate Dr. M Zahir, appearing on behalf of the defendant No. 5 submits that the plaintiff cannot get any delivery of the cargo since the law requires that the original copy of shipping documents must be submitted to the master of the vessel or the agent of the owner of the vessel in order to obtain a delivery or discharge of the consignment and since the plaintiff did not submit the original copy of the bills of lading, as it has not been retired from the issuing Bank, the plaintiff is neither entitled to obtain the delivery or discharge of the cargo nor is entitled to institute the instant Admiralty suit.

13. On the other hand, in his turn, the learned Senior Advocate Mr. Moinul Hosein, appearing on behalf of the plaintiff in order to refute the arguments as advanced by the learned Advocates on behalf of the defendants strenuously argued that admittedly the plaintiff is the importer of the cargo of 22,500 MT of Bulgarian wheat from the defendant No. 5 Messrs Sovarex SA and the same has been carried by the defendant No. 1 vessel 'MV BK Ace' from the Port of Varna, Bulgaria to Chittagong Port which has reached on 5-11-2010, but the vessel failed to discharge the Cargo within a reasonable period although the defendant vessel served notice of readiness. The learned Senior Advocate Mr Moinul Hosein argued that discharge of the Cargo after the arrival of the vessel at the discharge Port does not depend upon the production of shipping documents by the importer, rather the same is made in accordance with the provision of Customs Act 1969 and after the discharge of the Cargo when the importer wants to take the delivery of the same question of submission of original copy of shipping documents arises. He submits that in the present case since the defendant No. 5 sent discrepant the L/C opening Bank returned the same to the correspondent Bank ie BNP PARIBAS and as soon as the proper documents will be available in the hands of L/C opening Bank the plaintiff will submit the same to the vessel for the purpose of delivery of the Cargo and till that stage the Cargo will remain under the custody of the Customs Authority. The learned senior Advocate Mr. Moinul Hosein contends that since the plaintiff is not going to take delivery of the Cargo the defendants shall not face any prejudice.

14. The learned senior Advocate Mr. Moinul Hosein informed this Court that in order to get the Cargo discharged in the Port the plaintiff has submitted all the relevant documents to the defendant vessel, specially an indemnity from the ultimate buyer of the said wheat i.e. the Government of Bangladesh, indemnifying the vessel and its owner from any prospective litigation if at all arises due to any reason whatsoever.

15. The learned senior Advocate Mr. Moinul Hosein argued that the statement made in paragraph 8 at the plaint regarding the submission of the original copy of the bills of lading is a inadvertent one. The confusion caused due to the lake of adequate paper in his hands as has been supplied by the client and now it appears from the application filed by the defendant No. 5 that those original documents are now returned by the L/C issuing Bank i.e. the State Bank of India to the correspondent Bank i.e. BNP PARIBAS on the ground that there was a discrepancy for which the correspondent Bank BNP Paribas has taken back the said documents and in the meantime since the vessel has arrived in the discharge port of Chittagong, the plaintiff with the co-operation of the Government arranged for discharge of the goods and in no way the plaintiff attempted to get delivery of the consignment without the original shipping documents.

16. The learned Senior Advocate Mr. Moinul Hosein, drawn the attention of this Court to an application filed by him before this Court during the progress of the hearing that he prays for a direction from this Court upon the defendant vessel for discharging the Cargo in the Chittagong port and to allow this plaintiff to take delivery after submission of the original Shipping documents.

17. The learned Senior Advocate Mr. Moinul Hosein, further argued that the ultimate buyer of the instant Bulgarian wheat is the Government of Bangladesh through the Director General of Ministry of Food and Disaster Management which has been imported for the purpose of distribution as relief material under a contact dated 22-9-2010 concluded in between the plaintiff and the Government of Bangladesh and if the vessel is allowed to leave the territorial water of Bangladesh without discharging the said Cargo the citizen of this country will ultimately be prejudiced and the plaintiff will face a huge financial loss since the plaintiff has opened the L/C through the L/C issuing Bank i.e. the State Bank of India in favour of the beneficiary the supplier Messrs Sovarex SA in Bulgaria.

18. The learned Senior Advocate Mr. Moinul Hosein finally argued that the question of non-payment by the L/C opening Bank to the supplier cannot be taken into consideration at this because the entire transaction is being dealt under the UCP 600 and the same is a matter for the Banks dealing under the International Rules and, as such, the non-payment for the goods has no implication on the question of discharge of the goods and therefore the arrest order cannot be vacated without the discharge of the Cargo at this stage which will prejudice the plaintiff.

19. We have heard the learned Advocate, perused the application, the plaint and the submitted documents by the parties.

20. From the submitted document it appears that the plaintiff executed an agreement with the Director General of Food, Ministry of Food and Disaster Management Government of Bangladesh on 22-9-2010 for supply of 50,000 MT of wheat of 2010 crop of any country of the world except Israil origin in bulk and the plaintiff opened. L/C for import of 22,500 MT Bulgarian wheat, in favour of the supplier the defendant No. 5 Messrs Sovarex SA Bulgaria, through the State Bank of India being No. 07502101M0000591, dated 9-9-2010. Later the Government of Bangladesh through the Janata Bank opened L/C being No. 009310012829 in favour of the plaintiff LMJ International Limited on 28-9-2010 for import of 22,500 MT of Bulgarian wheat. Upon the L/C opened in its favour by the State Bank of India, the supplier Messrs Sovarex SA loaded the Bulgarian wheat 22,500 MT in the vessel `MV BK Ace' and the master of the vessel issued to bills lading being No. 1 and 2, dated 12-9-2010 which reached the Chittagong Port on 5-10-2010 wherefrom the dispute arises in between the parties.

21. It appears that although in the meantime the supplier Messrs Soverex SA sent the original shipping documents to the L/C opening bank but the same have been returned back to the correspondent Bank BNP Paribas from the L/C issuing Bank i.e. the State Bank of India upon finding some discrepancy in the original documents, through the letter dated 29-11-2010. But as the vessel 'MV BK Ace' since reached the discharge port now the question has arisen whether the vessel is liable to deliver the cargo to the plaintiff or the defendants are liable to furnish security to protect the interest of the plaintiff in the instant suit.

22. The crux of the argument of the learned Senior Advocate Mr Moinul Hosein, is that under the Customs Act, 1969 the incoming vessel is liable to discharge, meaning thereby 'unload', the consignment into the port and thereafter upon submission of the original shipping documents by the importer, the question of delivery comes. But the learned senior Advocate Dr M Zahir, contends that there will occur only one transaction i.e. the delivery of the goods when the incoming vessel reached the discharge port.

23. Upon such conflicting arguments it appears that the discharge/delivery is a term that been embodied in customs Act 1969. When a vessel reached the port of Chittagong with Bangladesh bound cargo from other ports, the entire afterward matter is to be dealt under the customs Act 1969.

24. Section 42 of the Customs Act, 1969 provides that all arrival of foreign vessel with the Bangladesh bound consignment must be made within a Customs Station and thereupon the same shall come under the purview of the Customs Authority and under the provision of Section 43 of the Customs Act, 1969 the incharge of the vessel is to deliver an Import General Manifest (IGM) to the custom authority disclosing the cargo it brought to be discharged in the said port. Upon such submission of IGM the customs authority will issue a permission under Section 47 of the Customs Act for breaking the bulk cargo order to discharge the cargo within the classified area of the port and prior to issuance of such permission no bulk cargo will be allowed to be broken. Such a discharge has been limited within specified period under the provisions of Section 75 of Customs Act 1969 and upon discharge of the cargo from the vessel the same will be kept under the Customs custody. Thereafter, the question comes for its delivery. Section 79 of the Customs Act 1969 provides the procedure for clearance or delivery of the cargo for Home Consumption or for keeping the same under the ware house and the provisions of Section 82 of the Customs Act 1969 liable the importer to take delivery of the cargo within the specified period or to invest with the penalty for taking late delivery or to face consequence of sale of the cargo on auction for not taking delivery. The control upon the vessel, drown from the point of entering the territorial water of Bangladesh up to the delivery of the cargo shall be under the hands of the Customs Authority. In this respect we find substance in the argument of the learned senior Advocate Mr. Moinul Hosein that under two sets of act, one being discharge, meaning thereby unloading the cargo, and the other being delivery to the importer, the imported cargo is being disposed off. Therefore it appears from the aforesaid provisions of Customs Act 1969 that whenever vessel comes into the territorial water of Bangladesh with the Bangladesh bound cargo it must discharge the same in accordance with the provisions of Section 73 of the Customs Act 1969 which runs as follows:

"Customs Act (Act IV of 1969)

Section 73;

Discharge of cargo by vessel may commence on receipt of due permission-When an order for entry inwards of any vessel which has arrived in any customs port or a special pass permitting such vessel to break bulk has been given, discharge of the cargo of such vessel may be proceeded with."

25. Although the provision speaks of 'may' but the comprehensive reading of the other provision regarding of cargo indicates that it is a mandatory provision that after obtaining permission for bulk breaking, the cargo must be unloaded within a specified period. The term "discharge" used in the Customs Act 1969 is nothing but "unloading" of the cargo into the classified area of the Port.

<u>26. But in the instant case question remains whether the delivery will be made of the instant cargo to the plaintiff after the discharge. It appears that admittedly the plaintiff does not hold the original copy of the bills of lading. Bills of lading, in one of its implication, being the documents of title, the holder of it gets the ownership of the said cargo carried by a vessel upon which the same was issued by the master of the vessel. Unless the original copy of the bills of lading is produced before the master of the vessel the master in no way is liable to deliver the cargo to any person, else he will face the consequence of the offence of conversion as has been held by their lordship in the Indian jurisdiction in the case of Szehali Tong bank Ltd vs Rember Cycle Company Ltd. reported in 1959 AC 576. Therefore, it appears that since the plaintiff failed to submit the original copy of the bills of lading along with other shipping document it cannot claim the delivery of the same. In this respect this Court notes that the referred decision of the case of KYCR Coil Industries Ltd vs MV Thor Transity and other reported in 10 BLC 663 has relevance to its full extent.</u>

<u>27. But it appears that admittedly 1,500 MT of wheat has been discharged into the lighter age vessel 'MV Golden Dream' which is still remaining within the outer anchorage of the Chittagong Port Besides the mother vessel and under the custody of the Mother Vessel 'MV BK Ace' The learned Advocate Mr. Moinul Hosein claimed that on the basis of an under taking issued by one Deputy Director, procurement Division Government of Bangladesh counter signed by the Manager, Janata Bank Limited such discharge has been made, but the learned Advocate Mr. M Hafizullah, seriously objected to the under taking stating that no such document has been submitted to the master of the vessel rather the plaintiff Shipping agent Sea Com Shipping Limited misleader the master of the vessel through any means to discharge 14,198 MT of wheat of the cargo into the lighter age vessel. Whatever be the reason stated by the learned Advocates the actual facts remain that the said part discharge has been made under the provision of the' Customs Act, 1969. Although the vessel is now under arrest yet the vessel will be liable to discharge the entire cargo in accordance with the Provisions of Customs Act 1969 since no breaking of bulk is allowed without the permission of Customs Authority under Section 47 of the Customs Act 1969. Since the vessel obtained the permission for breaking the bulk it became liable to discharge the entire cargo as mandated by the Customs Act, 1969. But as the plaintiff has not yet submitted the original shipping documents, the plaintiff will not be entitled to get the delivery of the said consignment till the plaintiff submits the original copy of the shipping documents.</u>

28. But it appears that the order of arrest of the vessel `MV BK Ace' cannot be sustained at this stage, since it appear that the arrest of this vessel has been procured by the plaintiff on the misstatement that the plaintiff have submitted the original copy of the bills of lading before the master of the vessel and the master has not delivered the cargo. Therefore, the order of arrest cannot be sustained when it appeared to this Court that the plaintiff upon misstatement obtained the order of arrest of the vessel.

29. Therefore, the order of arrest of the vessel 'MV BK Ace' is hereby vacated with a direction to the defendant vessel to discharge the consignment in accordance with the provision of Customs Act, 1969.

30. As the defendant No. 5, through an application, prayed for a direction upon the plaintiff to take delivery of the entire consignment upon payment and submitting the original copy of the documents, the plaintiff is directed to immediately arrange to get the original copy of the shipping documents upon instructing the L/C opening Bank to accept the discrepant documents and to pay off the L/C amount to the correspondent bank in order to get the original shipping documents for its onwards transmission to the plaintiff to facilitate the delivery of the consignment with two weeks from date and in the meantime the plaintiff is also directed to instruct the L/C issuing bank to indemnify the correspondent bank so that the entire transaction may be done within a short period.

31. The vessel 'MV BK Ace' will be at liberty to sail out the territorial water of Bangladesh after discharge of the cargo including the cargo now lying in the lighter age vessel 'MV Golden Dream' in accordance with the Provision of Customs Act 1969.

32. Let this order be served upon the defendants through the Marshal of this Court at the cost of defendant No. 1.

33. Let this Suit appear in the cause list on 13-12-2010 as an application for facilitating the parties to inform this Court about the compliance of the order, by way of affidavit of compliance.

End.
